reviewText: Great product, excelent delivery, what else can you expect

When I have gone shopping for jeans in the stores, I have, for several years, always looked for Wranglers, and always looked for a specific size with a specific label: Wrangler Men's Relaxed-fit 44x32. The word 'RELAXED' is printed on the inside label near the size. When I've bought 44x32 regular, the fit is off enough that I get lower back pain.
When I couldn't find what I was looking for at my favorite retail outlet, I turned to Amazon and found the jeans pictured above.  Perfect, I said. Ordered them and, a couple of days later, there they were. There was a clear plastic tape on the outside that said,'RELAXED'. This was missing, however, from the inside label. Tried them on and, nope, didn't fit right.
Thought about sending them back, but then I thought, well, I could lose some weight and they'd fit right. Haven't lost the weight and the jeans still don't fit right. It is now 4 months later and I can't decide if I am more mad about not losing the weight or THE MISLABELED JEANS.  I think it is the jeans right now.

reviewText: I bought the 48x28 jeans as I am short and stout, and like my jeans to sit at my waist where I am biggest.  The fit was great, and the length is true.  There is plenty of room in the seat without being overly baggy.  The thighs are roomy, a big bigger as these are work jeans meant for a lot of flexibility.  (I don't get longer jeans and shorten them because that leaves too long a rise for a short guy like me.  I have to buy them online to get the wider/shorter size.)  Overall I love these jeans.  I must emphasize that the fabric is on the heavier side so might be warm in summer, but should be extra durable.  Also, like other reviewers pointed out, the fly zipper goes almost all the way to the crotch, which seems excessively log, but isn't really noticable once one has the pants on.  I love the vintage indigo color too, which will look nicer for dressing these up.  Lastly, the price here was just as good or better than I would get in a store.
summary: Great jeans - true fit - heavy weight material

UPDATE: It has been three months since these jeans were delivered. They have torn at a non-stress area. The weave of the fabric parted and opened a tear about two inches long (see photo). The tear is in the rear just above and inboard of the left pocket. This is not uncommon. I also have another pair of these jeans (somewhat older) that have a tear in the weave in the front just to the left of the zipper. Again this is a non-stress area.  Wrangler quality is not what it once was.
SECOND UPDATE: I've been wearing these jeans for a while. I had another pair that I wore for about 27 months. This is fairly sedentary wear. Mostly sitting! The second photo below shows the holes that appeared in a non-stress area next to the zipper. The smaller hole (About two inches) appeared and I ignored it for a couple of weeks. Then the second RIP (About six inches) finished the jeans off. I remember when Jeans used to last until you out-grew them. The only place the fabric ever failed was in the knees or the seat. reviewText:
I received the first pair as a gift for graduation, in 2007.  They lasted me over three years.  I wore them quite a bit.  The heels wore down due to my overpronation and I had to replace the laces a couple years in, but other than that they lasted.  I was so impressed I didn't hesitate to get a second pair.

I wore the second pair for a little over a year.  They're still wearable, though they wore out faster than the first pair, the top portion of one has broken off.  Nevertheless, my work bought us all new boots, so I continued my loyalty and tried again.

The third pair was a complete disappointment.  Half the rivets holding the lace eyelets have broken free, making it impossible to wear them comfortably.  The soles both cracked and allow water to seep in easily.  They looks as old as the previous pair, though they're a year and a half younger.

 I had to go back to my second pair as I wait for another brand of boots to arrive.  Maybe I was unlucky with the last pair, but I suspect the level of overall quality has degraded over time.  I'm really disappointed I had to move on, I loved these boots.
summary: Have had Three Pairs, Each Worse than the Last

reviewText: I love these boots if only for the sole, as everything else has those awful glued together soles. The worthless dual density glued crap soles on work boots today are worthless, just crap. The CAT Alaska has an old fashioned solid rubber sole. Yes its heavy, yes it doesn't flex easy, yes the oiled leather doesn't breath well. No they are not Gore-Tex and you can't stand in a rain filled pot hole waiting for your soy latte while your girlfriend pays. These are MAN'S boots, the require retreatment (use Sno-Seal) every few months to stay waterproof. Read though, the leather is waterproof but that doesn't mean you can wade in them. If you are working in standing water you should be wearing rubber boots or overshoes. Where the tongue, laces and toe meet there is a small hole at the union point of the leather pieces. I always shoot some black RTV in the holes and than you actually can stand in water but really that's the time for rubbers. If you want to wear grown up man's boots buy them, than let your beard grow

reviewText: great

Let me start by saying that I've worn a fair amount of western style boots and hold them to a higher standard than most. Realistically, I'd give these a 4.5 star review.

Comfort/fit:
These bad boys are comfortable! I have a pretty wide foot, but i did not feel like these required a lot of break in time. My job requires me to do a lot of walking, up to 10 miles a day, and my feet always felt great. I've even jumped of high retaining walls and the cushion in the Ariat souls are awesome. THEY DO HAVE A TALL HEEL, which is the case with most cowboy boots, so be aware that. I'm 6'1, 190ibs, medium/large width foot and a size 10.5 - these things feel great.

Durability:
I wore these boots nearly everyday for a year and a half. Working 10+ hour days and dancing in them a few times a week (not the best for dancing because the bottom is pretty grippy, but they'll do the job). They held up pretty well. Unfortunately, my job requires me to use chemicals that are very hard on leather, I didn't keep them polished, and the side ended up splitting. KEEP THEM POLISHED and they will last a long time. I bought another pair very similar to these right after they wore out.

Style:
Great style, you will get compliments on them. Especially if you polish them, they get really shiny. Plenty of western style, without being too flashy.

All and all, these are a great boot. Keep them polished and you will be very happy.

I've worn Tony Lama's for 50 years, so I hesitated to order these until the price offered on Amazon, justified my trying them out.
Right out of the box I put them on and walked several miles in them.  The weather has been rather wet for a month or more, and I was concerned that the leathers soles on my Lama's would expedite the deteriorization and force me to have them half soled later in the year.  At first I thought these were a little larger than I had planned on, although they were very comfortable brand new.  The rubber (?) soles and heals somehow made them feel very similar to the slip on walking shoes I've work in the past.  My immediate concern about size quickly disappeared.  They are the perfect size and exactly what I wanted.  10 1/2 EE and now that they are a week old and I wear them constantly during the day, I've found them to be as comfortable as my walking shoes.
As I've done in the past, I always put rubber taps (ordered from Amazon) on the heels to guard against my heals getting worn down and forcing me to the expense of rehealing.
Bottom line; these are great boots, their comfortable, they will hold up for what will be an extended time without resoling and rehealing, and I'll very likely be ordering another pair in a few months.  They are clean looking boots and I'm sure will be easy to polish and visually give me that western look I strive for.  FYI, I've had ingrown toenails for 30 or 40 years and the Lamas did put pressure on them, which is not apparent with the Ariat.  I'm hooked!

reviewText: Outstanding

These boots are awesome. I wanted a cowboy style boot with a pointed Toe. Most Ariats don't have the traditional J-toe cowboys wore, but they have a decent R-toe. The R-toe still gives somewhat of a pointed look for your feet, but doesn't make the boot too bulky like some other Toe Styles. I was looking at these and a few other brands. What really separated these out were I was able to buy them for $144 with no tax at a local Saddle Shop in NJ because there is no tax on clothes and they had a 20% off sale. The other thing is the bottom soles are rubber and not leather. Rubber holds up better if it rains, where as leather typically does not. Thus in turn I didn't want to have to get my boots resoled all the time. That's an advantage to these. Something to keep in mind.

Pros
- Cushioning is comfortable. I danced for 6 hours the other night and no issues because my foot was at an incline all night. No knee pain with a good boot.
- Rubber Bottoms
- Leather Outs.

The only other thing is sizing. I measured my foot at the saddle shop and most shoes I wear I am a size 11. I was a comfortable size 10.5 in these. Both fit well, but the 10.5 was a snug comfortable fit.

reviewText: Perfect!

I wear these boot with my uniform at work. They fit snugly, (little small and narrow, so take that into consideration when ordering size), and once broken in are comfortable enough to wear all day, as in 24 hours.
The biggest reason I buy these however, is that they are airport security friendly; 99.99% of the time they do NOT set off the magnetometer at even the most strict airport security (don't move to fast through, and don't lift your feet too high).
This is my third pair, over a couple of decades. I have worn them for about 20,000 hours [continuous use] a piece, with my uniform, riding motorcycles, and walking many, many miles.
I bought this latest pair because my last pair became too scuffed to wear with my uniform, but I will continue to wear the old pair for everyday use, until they totally fall to pieces, which I expect to be in a few years.

These 13 inchers are a wonderful exception, giving a full two fingers of breathing room at the top, thus ensuring proper blood circulation. I could not be happier. I applied some mink oil to protect the boots, and was originally a bit worried when it darkened them significantly, and the "distressed" finish was diminished. If you want a comfy, durable boot that fits the traditional western style, and isn't too flashy, look no further, these are great!

reviewText:
I have owned several Ray-Ban aviators (both small metal and large metal 58 mm) and I ordered all of them on Amazon. This maybe a fake one or a very bad quality authentic one. I found one defect right out of the box before trying them on. The last letter "P" on the left frame(right beside the temple length number 135 and for mine it is supposed to say "3P") looked suspicious because it kind of looked like it got scratched off. But I neglected this fact and was thinking about keeping them since the box, the soft cloth and the sunglasses looked ok. But later on the same day I received these sunglasses, I noticed 2 white, tiny dots: one on the upper side of the right lens and another one very close the right upper frame. I tried to remove it with a soft cloth but it did not go away.(see it in the photos!). It seemed like some of the white paint from the logo got stuck on the other part of the right lens. And again I tried to scratch those off lightly with my nails but they wouldn't go away. This is a huge disappointment for me. I cannot say whether these are original or fake ones but there is no way I am keeping these because of these defects.

reviewText: Not original Ray Ban sunglasses.  I'm not a expert by far but they are definitely fakes.  I still do like them but would not pay that much for something that is not real.  Price point should be 1/4 of the selling price.  I gave two stars for effort.

I've now owned three pairs of Ray-Ban aviators and I will keep coming back to this style because of the look and quality.  All of my pairs have been the 55mm gold frame with polarization.  My first pair I owned for 4 years and they got a little scuffed and chipped (because I dropped them) by the time I replaced them.  My second pair I owned for 3.5 years before they were stolen.  Those were still totally fine with minor scuffing on the lenses and the hinges were getting loose.  With my third pair, I'm planning on taking much better care of them than I did with the first two.

As far as frame size, I'm 5'8" with a smallish but normal-width face and the 55mm frame fits my face just fine.  My 5'3" wife has put them on and the 55mm fits her, too.

Some people are concerned that they aren't getting real Ray-Bans when they buy online.  I bought my first two pairs of aviators from stores and my third pair is the first I've bought online.  The third pair is exactly the same as the first two in sturdiness and build quality and the polarization is working, so I'm certain they aren't knockoffs.  When buying Ray-Bans online, I would just be sure the seller is Amazon.com itself or a reputable sunglass company.  A company whose orders are fulfilled by Amazon is probably OK, too.

After purchasing this pair of sunglasses, Ive sworn off all Ray-Bans, and, by extension, all sunglasses produced by Luxottica. After a year of ownership, while sitting in the original case, in luggage, the lens cracked, propagating from the top of the frame  clearly a manufacturers defect. When I sent them into Luxottica (which owns Ray-Ban), they denied warranty service. Any attempts to contact customer service (phone and email) was met by the rote a trained technician has deemed your eyewear non-defective. In the end, all they did was ship the broken sunglasses back to me. Amazon, however, graciously let me return them, even a year after purchase; so if you insist on buying Luxottica/Ray-Ban products of dubious workmanship, at least do it on Amazon.

I wish I could more strongly dissuade everyone from purchasing Ray-Ban and Luxottica products: the quality of their products is now terrible (having owned 3 pairs of Ray-Bans), surpassed only by their abysmal customer service. Unfortunately, alternatives are few and far between: Luxottica does have near-monopoly status, with ~80% market share in the eyewear market, which helps explain their ~70% gross margins  exactly what happens when you sell crappy, cheaply-made products at a premium. Id recommend a quick Google search, which will reveal a few independent alternatives. Bottom line: for Ray-Ban/Luxottica products, buyer beware!

Not only is this my first real pair of Italian Ray-Ban sunglasses, but my first pair of aviator-style as well.  I've been an Oakley wearer for years (mostly sporty styles), and after my last set of metal-framed Oakleys just got too scratched up, I decided I needed a new pair.  I was attracted to the aviator-style, but I'm not really sure why.  After a few months of thinking about it, I decided I'd go for it, and who better to choose than Ray-Ban?

I got these in the narrower 55mm width because, even though I don't have a small head, my face seems narrow and I feared the "normal" 58mm might appear bigger on me than they really are.  After having these for a few days, I think I made the right choice.

Fit aside, I DEFINITELY made the right choice with the mirror green!  I was torn between these and the blue ones, and I'm sure that if I'd gotten blue, I would have been plenty happy.  But these are SLICK!  I love the color (they even seem blue-ish from certain side-angles), and I haven't seen anyone else wearing anything like 'em!

Every pair of Oakley sunglasses I ever had were polarized, and so, of course, as a new Ray-Ban owner I made sure I got these in the polarized version, too.  However, some pictures of polarized Ray-Bans make it seem as though the lenses are more see-through from the outside than the non-polarized version.  My number one must-have feature was a completely mirrored finish.  After doing some research, I found that these are every bit as mirrored as you would expect.  Maybe if enough sunlight shines on your face from a side-angle, your eyes might show through, but these are so reflective, it'll be tough to really see your eyes most of the time (so fellas, you're safe to scope out the chix; and ladies, you're safe to scope out the fellas, totally incognito).

Anyway, as a long-time Oakley wearer, I definitely hit a home-run with my first pair of authentic Ray-Bans.  w00t!
summary: First pair of Ray-Bans, couldn't be happier!

I was very concerned about all the counterfit Ray Bans on amazon. I did alot of research on what to look for to spot the fakes. Even people who have said "if the glass is etched on the left lense they are authentic". Well the counterfitters will go to extreme lengths to make them look as real as possable. Nearly every detail is copied. So, after looking at different sellers, watching videos of real and fake glasses I searched for SunglassHut on Amazon. They are the brick and morter authorized sellers. I saved my order to my shopping cart from the Sunglasshut page on Amazon and they were $199.95. When I checked out I noticed it said "sold by and fullfilled by Amazon for $118. This made me a little worried. I wanted to pay the extra money to be sure they were authentic. Why the seller changed I have no idea.

Now my review. I am still not 100 percent they are authentic but about 90 percent sure. All the research I have done and the fakes I have seen have all the same markings on the glasses and the case. The only thing the real ones have that the fake ones do not are that the ends of the plastic ear pieces curve a little bit. all the pictures and videos I have seen show the fakes with straight ear pieces at the very ends. The lenses are indeed polarized as you can tell from looking at different peoples rear windows of their cars in the sun. The glass has an invisable checkerboard pattern with the glasses on and it goes away with them off. The blue mirroring is nice and you cant see your eyes from other peoples perspective unless sunlight is coming in from the sides. The fit is good and I will go to my local Sunglasshut store to have them adjusted.

Overall 4 stars because of placing in my cart from the sunglasshut page and then it being changed to sold and fullfilled through Amazon, and the fact I still have that 10% doubt they could be fakes.

Back in the 60's, I wore what turned out to be B&L Outdoorsman sunglasses.  I recall finding them at the beach and had 'em for years.  I liked the brow bar from a style POV but it was a nuisance to keep clean.  After they broke, I moved on to other styles including the 52mm Randolph Engineering pilot's sunglasses.  Recently, while browsing Amazon, I saw the Ray Ban Aviators and Outdoorsman II's.  I assumed I'd want the 58mm sizes of them but wasn't sure which model I wanted so I ordered both via my Prime account.  The Outdoorsman had a brown brow bar and that looked wrong to me (the originals had a translucent white bar).  But both the Aviators and Outdoorsman looked wrong on me.  Bigger than I like (and I'm 6', 180#) and sent them back the next day.

A few days ago, I was wandering our local mall and they had the 55mm versions of the Aviators but for full MSRP.  However, they fit me the way I think this style should look, smaller than larger.  The larger versions you see on YT videos make people look bug eyed.  While they usually say the 55mm size is too small, to me they look just right on most people.

Anyway, these arrived today in the classic gold frame and G-15 lens (the *only* acceptable color combo in my world) and they fit just the way I'd hoped.

They seem well made and while the prices have skyrocketed on these (and everything else Luxottica owns), Amazon's price is great.  Unless you have a very large, round face, consider the 55mm versions of these for the correct look.  IMO, of course.  YMMV.  And if you decide to keep them and hate the cheesy lens logo, it comes off in a few moments using the edge of a penny or other small coin.  Let the coin do the work and don't press hard.  This is for GLASS lenses only.
summary: Finally!  The right sunglasses, the right size, the right price

reviewText: Not really sunglasses - they don't actually make the world much darker, just sepia-coloured...

Just received these Ray-Ban RB3025 112/O658 Polarized Aviator Sunglasses in Matte Gold Frame and Light Orange Lenses. I am happy to report that they are 100% authentic. Don't be scared due to the reviews saying these are fake, just make sure you order directly from Amazon as the seller. I can't speak for the other sellers but Amazon will not send you fake goods (they wouldn't still be here if they did). While I'm on the subject of amazon, make sure you check out any current discounts or promotions they may be running. I got these 20% off due to some fashion/accessories coupon code. Furthermore, I was able to get a price adjustment refund because they dropped from $120 to $105. Ray-Ban sells them for $200. This is an amazing deal. Thanks Amazon!

Now for the actual product review:

Since many people have written at length about RB Aviators in general, and we all know what to expect from a quality standpoint, I'll just focus on this specific configuration.

The model I ordered is part of the "Polar Special Series" which is the polarized version of their "Legends" lenses. These are a lighter tint than most of their lenses and have a retro 60s vibe compared to their other lens options. If money were no object I would also order the Green and Blue versions of these Polar Special aviators. But, since money is an object I went with Orange, as I thought it would fit my style the best and provide the best overall viewing experience.

The orange tint is a great color for driving as it filters blue light and increases perceived contrast of distant objects. In addition, polarization is in my view an essential feature of any driving sunglasses. Polarization filters the light reflected by many things, including the road, other cars, puddles, bright white clouds, and it even darkens the sky at the right angle In general it makes it easier to focus on the road and less on being blinded. As an added bonus, the polarization on these isn't so intense that you can't read your sat-nav when you need to.

These two features make wearing these glasses refreshing for your eyes, and they are a light enough tint to wear on cloudy days while still being useful, not detrimental. You won't want to take them off.

From a style perspective, these have the classic ray-ban aviator look, with a distinctive vintage feel. They tint is light enough for people to see your eyes through them, which I also like.

Not much more to say about them, get them while you still can because it seems like the Polar Special Series is being phased out.
summary: Polar Special Series: functional retro styling

reviewText: I bought these for a pair I lost. These don't feel or even look the same. Description say gold/green. I got gold/black.

I collect Rayban that is why when I received my order, I knew right away that what I got were fake. Thankfully, when I called to report it, the Amazon staff was really accommodating. I just received my new pairs and finally, they are REAL!

This is my second pair of 62mm Ray Ban Aviator Sunglasses- the 1st pair did not have Polarized Lenses, which are great also.  I recently bought a pair of RB2025 in Black with polarized lenses and look forward to using the glasses while driving. I like the larger 62mm lenses as I get better coverage when I need the sunglasses the most- when driving.

However, to buy these glasses took me a long time due to receiving counterfeits .  The first pair I bought from an Amazon competitor auction company and received a counterfeit pair of glasses.

I will not go into details about how to determine if you have a pair of fake Ray Ban glasses or not, as you can Google that information and there are Utube videos available.

Because I received the first pair of fakes, I decided to buy from Amazon using my Prime account, but Amazon direct did not offer the glasses, so I picked a company that Amazon distributed their glasses for.  I emailed that company and asked if the glasses were: From Italy and if they were 100% real Ray Ban Glasses, which the company response was yes. So I purchased the glasses and received another pair of counterfeit Ray Bans.  All of the items were real except the Glasses-as if switched out  by the company.  Also, the pair I received was NOT 62mm and 58mm.  I, of course, returned the fake wrong size glasses.

So, be careful.  Find out how to determine the difference between a fake pair and a real pair of Ray Ban sunglasses.

Luxottica is the manufacturer of Ray Ban glasses.  Currently Ray Ban glasses are made in Italy or China.  In my opinion, I would not buy a pair of Ray Ban glasses that are made in China.  Sure, the quality of the glasses will be the same, but the fact that the glasses are made in China and not Italy, simply cheapens the glasses and my guess will also effect the resale value- which should be considered.

Also, we as consumers should send a message Luxottica and NOT purchase products that were originally made in Italy now make in China for the same price.  If Luxottica wants to make their glasses in China for a lesser cost, why not pass the savings on to the consumer.  As, you can imagine, there profits from glasses made in China would probably triple.
summary: Ray Aviator 62mm is the way to go.  Only buy if made in Italy NOT China.  Be careful you do not receive a counterfeit pair.

reviewText:
I ordered this pair of sunglasses for my husband as an xmas gift.  I felt secure in the purchase because this was originally listed as 'sold by Amazon' as opposed to merely 'fulfilled by Amazon'.

Well, something changed I guess.

Unfortunately, I cannot speak in terms of the seller because I cannot say who ended up actually filling this order, but it wasn't Amazon.

I would also like, at the very least, to say that I received a fake pair of Ray Ban aviators, but that is far too generous.  A fake implies that some effort was put in to make the product mirror that which I thought I was buying.  Wouldn't that be nice?  But nope.  I received a random pair of 5-dollar aviator sunglasses with a Ray Ban sticker on them.  No markings on the frames, no markings on the lenses, not even the slightest effort made to trick me.  To that I feel somewhat insulted.  I cannot imagine a world existing where a person would receive this product and think "awesome, just what I paid $150 dollars for!!"  What a joke.

Because I made the specific effort to assure I was ordering directly from Amazon and still had my order fulfilled by some random seller, I would encourage any shopper looking at this sort of item to walk away, save your money, and spend a few more dollars for the privilege of not getting ripped off.  As a long time Amazon shopper, I can say that my confidence in this company has been significantly shaken.

I love xmas - it gives me a chance to finally spoil the people who I love and who do so much for me throughout the year.  Thanks for finally allowing me to bestow upon someone an awful pair of random sunglasses in a ripped up, fake Ray Ban box.  A dream come true.  Unbelievable.

reviewText: this watch looks great but didn't keep time from the start. i was going to return it, however, my husband was so excited that he wore it to work anyway. when he came he said it had stopped working, but when i looked at it he had already scratched it so was's able to return. took it to the jewlers, $70 later it worked for about 60 days and now has stopped keeping time again. the jewler said that many times these watches are "gray" sales. they aren't authentic and will not be repaired  when returned to Wenger. pay the extra and go to an authentic dealer.

Bought this watch for a three week trip to India.  Liked the classic simple look and the brown leather band.  Regrettably, it worked for about five weeks and then stopped.  If I pull the stem out to reset the time and then push it in, the watch works for about a day before stopping again.  This has gone on for a week now.  As I am past my  30 day return period, I am debating whether, and the extent to which, I want to pursue the warranty coverage. I did not expect this problem with a Wenger product, and am surprised and disappointed.

Save your money and try another watch, and perhaps another brand.

I've had a Wenger Classic Field for about 8 years, and the only issue has been with the date adjustment in the last year.  When the leather band wore out I replaced it with a stainless steel band and it looks great.  I love the black face, and the luminous hand and numbers glow bright and clear.  The crystal has really resisted scratches, despite wearing this for camping, fishing, and farm work as well as for going out.

The watch slowed down and the movement needed replacement after 3 months. After sending it back to Wenger (I had to pay for shipping) I got it  back with a small scratch on the crystal. I called Wenger immediately and the person in customer support told me that she couldn't resolve my issue and that her manager needed to get involved. She told me that her manager was in a meeting and would call me after it concluded. After waiting several days with no word from the manager (Irma A.), I called her directly.  After stumbling for words, she told me she was just picking up the phone to call me (yeah right).  She insisted the scratch was there when they received it. If it was there when I sent it in, I would have known it. I'm very particular about things like this. There was nothing documented on the repair checklist regarding the scratch.  It was her word against mine and guess who won?  She told me there was nothing I could do about it and there was no one else I could speak to. I was treated as if i was lying and just trying to get a free 10 dollar crystal. Their customer support philosophy is that all customers are trying to swindle them and we can't be trusted. This was my first and last Wenger purchase.
summary: Watch lost time and customer support lost my trust!

reviewText:
The marketing for this watch indicates "quick charge, high visibility" for the glow on the luminous hands and indices.

Only the hands glow at a visible strength for more than a few seconds - in fact it lasts several minutes, but the REST of the indices, numerals etc. do not and are only visible even in total darkness for maybe 60 seconds.

I recently learned that the only "glowing" type of watches that have strong and long-lasting visible glow are ones that use "Tritium tubes" for their glow illumination.

The watch itself is nice enough and has a good look, but it's not the MIL-SPEC watch Wengers' marketing materials make it out to be.

reviewText: AWFUL!!! I Purchased this in JAN/FEB2013, return date ends as of 05MAR2013 and the battery is already dead.  This watch lasted less than 6 weeks, I suggest you buy from someone else.  1) Why would a company have a return policy of less than 6 weeks if they were not selling faulty items? 2) It took darn near 4 weeks for me to receive the item to begin with.  I attempted to contact the company before placing a bad review, but their return policy prevented me from doing so, so here it is a bad review.  A great watch sold by a awful vendor.

1) As others have mentioned, the watch is big, but in the product specs it clearly says that the product case is 41 millimeters in diameter. That's 1 and 5/8 inches. So it is big, but the specs clearly state that. 2) On the other hand, one of the pictures of the watch shows that it is just a hair over 25 millimeters (1 inch) wide. That pic is incorrect, and is actually of one of the other Wenger Classic Field Watches. 3) If your wrist is bigger than 7 and 1/2 inches, then plan on getting a long band to replace the regular length band that comes with the watch. My wrist is 7 and 5/8 inches, and the band would only fit on my wrist in the last hole. 4) NOW HERE IS THE PROBLEM: After setting the watch, I noticed two hours later it had lost five minutes. Major disappointment. I set it again, and this time paid attention to it. I noticed that when walking, setting the watch down on a hard table or counter top, etc., that sometimes the second hand would stop moving. Simply gently shaking the watch would get it moving again. Then I tried to reset it again. After resetting it and pushing the crown in, I noticed that just tapping the crown in some instances would stop it. So I reset it again, and gently laid it down and made sure it was still running. 24 hours later, it had lost 55 minutes. 5) Here is the good part: I went back to Amazon.com, logged in, and returned the watch. Amazon as usual was very good about returning items, paying for the shipping and printing UPS labels for me. I gave to watch two stars because I do think it's a good looking watch. I realize it's a big watch, but that is why it looked good IMO and big watches are "in" and the norm these days for men's watches, unless you are getting a $20 lower quality watch. I looked for three weeks for watches before I ordered this watch, and most of the brands that sell $50 to $200 watches these days are 40-50 millimeters. I ordered another Wenger from Amazon after returning this Wenger Swiss Military Men's Classic Field Watch, model #72917. This time I got a Wenger TerraGraph, model #72785. I bought this watch for my husband in Sept. for his birthday. He wanted something that was easy to read and had a leather band.  This watch fit the bill perfectly.  He loved it from the moment he saw it.  It keeps great time and overall is a great looking watch.  It was a good purchase.  If you're looking for clean and simple, you can't go wrong with this watch.

Watches are a rather personal thing and each of us has specific requirements; likes and dislikes when it comes to what we want strapped to our wrist and what our requirements are in functions; it sort of boils down to "each his own."

My requirements are rather simple and "simple" leads the short list of my requirements.  First, I do not like a lot of whistles and bells.  I have no desire to know the time in each capitol of the world.  I do not need a watch that is waterproof to 10,000 feet.  I could care less as to the phases of the moon.  I do not need an alarm system to remind me of appointments nor do I want something that takes an advanced degree en engineering or computer science to set date, time and what ever.

Secondly, I want a watch that is unobtrusive - clean looking - no glitter or bling.  I want to be able to see the numbers and, both time and date.  I do not want any funny little "sub-dials" cluttering up the face. If the watch appears even slightly pretentious I want nothing to do with it.  But hey, that is just me.

Third, and this is probably one of the more important features I look for, is a watch that actually keep reasonable time consistently.  I hate setting and resetting a watch.  The numbers, both time and date, are easy to read and glow nicely in the dark.

Fifth - I absolutely hate paying more than one hundred dollars for a watch.  I am hard on watches.  I either break them, loose them or generally bang them up.  To pay big buck for something that I am surly bound to destroy, for me, is a complete waste of money.

The watch being reviewed here meets all my requirements.

Now I grant you, like another reviewer here I would prefer that this watch was that of the original and well made Swiss Army watch by Victorinox.  I had one at one time and loved it.  I destroyed it...well, actually an ostrich I was attempting to load in a trailer destroyed it, (ripped the band off and ripped the winding stem off), but the ostrich was only being an ostrich and I probably would have fought just as hard if someone was trying to load me in some strange contraption - I hold no ranker against the bird...the emergency room bill was large, but I have good insurance.  Anyway, I would have preferred to have the Victorinox but I was an am unwilling to pay the price.  The watch being reviewed here, for me, was an excellent compromise.

This watch is a bit larger that watches I normally wear but I am getting use to that.  It is clean looking, attractive and so far (about three months now) it has kept perfect time.

I must admit to have had some trepidation about the leather band.  I spend a lot of time at the gym and biking, and truth be told, sweat like a pig.  So far though the band has held up well and the staining is at a minimum.  When and if the band gets to looking too funky (through no fault of the band itself), I will replace it with something more suited for my lifestyle.

I like this watch and am completely satisfied with it.  If I can get two or three years use out of it without destroying it I will be happy...if it lasts longer, well that for me, is just extra gravy.

Don Blankenship
The Ozarks

reviewText:
I suspect many are like me and bought this watch even though we wanted something else. The original Swiss Army watch by Victorinox is exceptionally beautiful, but at a premium price (retails at three times the price). But the Wenger is a good substitute.

I like what I've seen so far, but I'll have to wait. The first watch I got had a loose minute hand that wobbled from side to side as the watch was rotated. I'm pretty sure that's not normal. Note: I'm not talking about the same phenomenon that affects the seconds hand on nearly every digital analog watch. Those are notoriously wobbly and misaligned even on very expensive marques.

This watch is a little bigger than I'm used to (don't know what the reviewer below means by "small") at 41 mm, but I think it'll grow on me. Rolex has a standard of 35mm for their dress watches and Victorinox is about ideal at 38mm. But, hey...bigger is better, right? It sure is easy to read.

Note that the watch pictured above is NOT the same watch that Amazon is shipping. You can see the actual model on Wenger's web site. The bezel is slightly bulkier and the numbers are larger and more blocky in appearance. The band is also different. I actually prefer the look of the one Amazon pictures, but that's not the one you're going to get.

I've had this watch for two months now, and I think what I like about it most, is that you can easily tell what time it is from varying angles. It is comfortable on the wrist, looks classy, and I'm sure this watch will last a long time - I have only owned swiss military watches for the past 30 years - and they have never failed me.
summary: Easy to See What Time it Is

reviewText:
I don't write a lot of reviews, especially negative ones.  But I feel the urge to write on here in part because I am confounded by what Clarks has done to their unstructured line.

I purchased a pair of unstructured shoes about 5-6 years ago that I wore to death.  Loved them; very comfortable and stylish.  About three years ago I purchased a another pair (un.bend) that were not the same.  Something had changed and the shoe dug into my foot in all the wrong places.  It was as if the base of the shoe was too narrow in the middle of the foot.  I wore them for a while, though my feet were killing me.  I eventually ate the cost and did not come back to clarks until recently.

Over the last few months I decided to try clarks again (unstructured to be specific) and I'll be darned if I am not experiences the same issue again.  I tried on several pairs from the casual line and each and everyone one of them presents the same issue.  The shoe bed appears to not be very even and it digs into the sole of my foot at the arch as well as the part opposite the arch on my foot.

I have no idea how or why I feel this and how it seems so bad for me yet not for others.  I mean, I could understand it if the insole had a high arch designed for support and that it bothered me.  But in my case, I am feeling like there is something protruding at the arch AND the other side.  That makes absolutely no sense yet there it is.

So after trying on numerous pairs, it seems unstructured is no longer for me.  Wish someone could explain what  I am feeling because in terms of style, I really like many of the shoes.

reviewText: I bought a pair of these three years ago.  I was a little reluctant on spending this much on casual shoes having never owned Clark's before.  They are very comfortable and have held up better than any other shoe I have owned in recent memory.  The outside is quite stylish and the inside pigskin is cool, soft, and very durable.  This is an area often overlooked by shoe manufacturers yet it is the inside where your feet spend all their time with the shoe.  These shoes breath, my feet don't sweat very much, the soles are supportive, and the material looks like new.  Fabric lined shoes often tear or develop holes long before the outside of the shoe wears out.  That is just throwing money away.  As an engineer I wear these every day in an industrial environment.  Other than with a suit I wear them with just about everything else.  As long as Clark's makes these I will buy them.  Best shoes ever!

This is my third pair of Clarks Unstructured Coil oxfords.

FIT/COMFORT
The fit has remained consistent through at least the last 5 or more years since I've been wearing these shoes.  This model happens to fit my foot perfectly.  Length is consistent with other footwear and I'd say is true to size.  For me, I have a slightly wide foot and these shoes fit spot on.  That being said, if you have a narrow foot, you may find the fit to be too wide.  While I require a wide in some shoes, these I can wear the regular width and it's fine.  I also have a fairly high instep and these fit me there well. They are fairly compliant and adjustable with lacing.  The shoes break in beautifully.  Not so soft to be worthless, not stiff at all.  These are honestly more comfortable than any sneaker or other shoe I own and they often get worn on the weekend too.

Durability
I wear mine down until the soles is practically worn through and i get several years of almost daily wear out of them.

MISC
Venting really works.  My feet remain as dry as possible in the summer.  Wear these with a wool blend sock and it's as dry as you can expect to be.

However, the venting is the Achilles heel of these shoes. They are NOT for all weather situations and you WILL get wet feet due to puddles and standing water in parking lots and such.  If they only made this shoe with Gore-Tex XCR liners (or at least on the vent to prevent water intrusion) I'd lose my mind!

She had explained how the shoe needed some break-in, which I didn't believe because most of my other soft leather shoes felt broken into at purchase. If there's one thing I want to ensure a good fit with, it's a pair of shoes. I was turned on to Clarks a while ago and I haven't looked back. The combination of style, comfort, and price have made their shoes winners in my book since the start. This Unstructured series was an interesting addition, being both very flexible and breathable with the air intake holes. I am actually wearing them right now as I type this, and I just got back from a long walk on a warm day and my feet feel great without being hot and sweaty.

Another feature that I feel distinguishes these shoes is the incredibly smooth and comfortable interior lining. Even with socks on, they have a very buttery feel to them when compared to other shoes I own. I could walk all day in these shoes without feeling fatigue, and I feel like they're also quite stylish. My one hesitation would be to wear this when it is wet/raining outside because the air intake holes might serve as a direct line to my socks, but since I have avoided wearing them in those conditions I can't say for sure. Ultimately, a great pair of shoes from a great shoe company.

This is a good shoe for the office if you are a tech or worker - not an executive.  You will not be wearing these shoes to your friend's wedding.  They are good looking and rugged but not very elegant and sophisticated for dress.

Comfort:
No break-in - these shoes are comfortable - and breathable with vents and breathable technology.  The sole is soft and the leather is soft as well.  Support on the arch is felt.  They run big - this is a somewhat wide looking shoe.  I usually wear size 8.5 which I ordered but then exchanged for the size 8.  Even the 8 is a bit roomy but I am keeping them regardless.

Material:
Nice soft leather and good stitching - the leather is also pre-rubbed by hand at the factory to enhance luster and durability - it is also recommended that you treat the leather occasionally.  WARNING - These are vented to in the RAIN you will get wet feet.

Price:
Very expensive - these shoes are over $100 and they should be in the $60-$70 range.

Style:
While I love the look of this shoe and the stitch patterns and lines this is not a dressy shoe.  It is for casual wear at the office - not an executive shoe.  The laces are clumsy and will protrude from the bottom of your pants - the shoe is wide.  You will not see anyone wearing a tux and these shoes - these are business casual ONLY.

I'll update as they wear down and let you know how they hold up......

The shoes are very comfortable, soft, flexible, and seem to be very well made.  I am quite happy and am now a big fan of the "Un." series.

CONS: Really not much...only minor thing is one of the "Un" logo/tags came loose from stitching after about 7-8 months, but that is it.

reviewText: Not a watch nut but own about 6 and was looking for something new to add to the rotation.  This watch was a great value and fit my needs well.  Its easy to read, face is a little larger without being a Silver Dollar on your wrist.  Victorinox makes some great watches and this one is nicer than my Tag.  The red contrasting hands look outstanding.

These are going fast - 3 left when I ordered, now down to 1 - another listing on Amazon has 5 but for a bit more money.  It's a discontinued watch that's been blown out lately.

This particular movement, as some others have noted, is an ETA 251.262 - becoming rarer to find lately as Swatch now owns it and apparently non-Swatch companies (they own quite a few major brands) no longer have access to it.  It has been used by many makers including TAG and Breitling and in several VSA models that will be very hard to find now.  I have a TAG with it that has been very reliable for several years.

The main great thing about this movement is the BIG minutes counter rather than a subdial.  There are few automatic watches that feature this and a few quartz watches based on the Soprod movement that was in TAG's Calibre S and now the VSA Chrono 1/100.  The downside to those movements is that the entire face of the watch is used for the chronograph so that real time and measured time are not simultaneously visible.

This is a great deal on a really nice looking, well built watch and a bargain at this price.  Good luck to the last lucky buyer!

As also noted, read the manual to learn how to zero the hands - there's a handy PDF version on-line too.

I am a watch aficionado with far more watches than I really need.  But this is one of my favorites.  Here are some likes:

1.  It has an ETA 251.262 movement.  This movement displays chronograph minutes with a full-diameter sweeping hand, like its red sweep second hand - but silver colored.  This makes makes reading minutes of the chronograph 1,000% easier than typical tiny sub-dial watches.

2.  It's titanium which reduces weight and makes the large size reasonably comfortable to wear.

3.  I like the clean design.  Many chronographs are encumbered with a lot of fine markings which obscure readability.

I have only one complaint:
The hands and numerals are reflective steel.  At some angles this is great.  But at other angles they are too dark against the background of the black dial.  I prefer matte finish white painted hands and numerals.

I selected this watch for my 30 year company service award 12 months ago.  After reading reviews and researching this model, am very glad I selected it. I get lots of compliments on the style and look.

I looked at other, similar watchs, but this watch just blew me away!  I "almost" bought an Air Boss, but this watch has SO much more to offer. I love that it has the Air Boss - style of full size second and minute hand chrono. But it ALSO has a standard second hand, which the AB does not. So, if you are trying to synch your time with a computer down to the second, how would you do that with an AB with no second hand? Also, the watch is drop-dead gorgeous.  I really like the counntdown bezel, which is often what I use to time the grill, etc, but this is so elegant, without the big "handles" or protrusions of other Swiss Army models. The hour up-or-down is a great feature, too, and not every model has that. In short this model has it ALL.

I can't ever recall being so happy with a purchase. Amazon makes it so easy, too.

reviewText: The presence of so many positive reviews is a testament to the quality of this watch.  For a sporty quartz chrono, it nears perfection for its price range.  Every detail is immaculately crafted, from the alternating brushed/polished steel on the bezel and bracelet, to the domed crystal and intricate detail on the face.  I hacked the second hand to official time 96 hours ago, and have been comparing the time. In four days, I am yet to see it lose or gain even a single second.  I have no doubt that it will after a while, but I can always see at least some inaccuracy after four days on most watches. Not this one.  That's one reason why so many people love the ETA 251.262 movement.  The red highlights in the hands and logo are a tasteful addition to the look of the Alpnach, and the second hour hand coupled with the rotating bezel for marking elapsed time is actually a useful feature.  This is a watch lover's watch, and I believe it stacks up in form, fit, and function to quartz watches in any price range.  I sometimes wonder at the MSRP of other Victorinox watches, but I can see why this one has a suggested retail well over $800.00. At the time of this review, I paid 360.00 for mine,and at that price the value is unbelievable.  Even if it was over $500.00, it would still be well worth it.  You can't go wrong with this watch, so long as you buy it from a reputable seller who can exchange it in the unlikely event of malfunction.  This watch will not disappoint!

Beautiful new timepiece
Love the ETA 251.262 for the central 60 minute hand chronograph. Easier to read then if it is in a smaller circle somewhere else
Especially with the red central second hand easily distinguishable from the white central minute hand
Good price for this watch too
summary: Beautiful new timepiece Love the ETA 251

The dial is solid black, but one thing you can't tell from the picture is that it gets gradient when the light hits it.  Adds an element of class to it I think.  The red hands and Swiss logo are a nice compliment to the dial as well, more sophisticated looking and less boring than just solid black dials and white hands.  And scratch-resistant sapphire is the only way to go!  You can tell it is thick and durable.  The band is also a nice style and very comfortable.

It is the perfect size too.  I hate big watches, they are gaudy.  This watch is the ideal size and design for ANY outfit.  I wear it with my dress clothes in the office, and I wear it in the gas field with my Hi-vis gear.  This thing is solid and looks great with everything.

I've worn this watch for over three years now and it's still in great shape.  The white on black contrast makes the watch easy to read at a glance.  It's also a sharp looking watch.  Highly recommended!

reviewText: My son is 6 and he uses these to take showers and keep his feet off the floor in the YMCA shower rooms after swimming! Nice shoes and comfortable. He loves them!

I'm not unhappy with the product, since most water shoes I've seen have this issue, these are as good otherwise as others we have bought, but come on, this is a Speedo product, you think they could build a shoe designed for the water.

The shoe fit a little big in the heel area and I was afraid to order the small size as we were leaving for vacation and wanted to make sure we had a water shoe.  Can speak of quality as we didn't get to use it.

We picked up three pairs of these black water shoes for each of our boys.  They are getting plenty of use for walking around in the pool area and swimming.  The extra traction afforded by these is appreciated and through numerous uses the shoes have not began to tear apart or wear prematurely.  The sizing runs somewhat large, but the shoes are narrow.  There is a neoprene padded liner in the shoe that I would recommend allowing to dry completely between uses if possible because if something is going to wear out prematurely, I would guess it to be that...we let ours sit in the sun if the weather is nice to dry them or leave them on top of the dryer during the winter so they get a chance to fully dry between uses.  While water shoes by nature are flimsy, I would recommend this type; we have had several other types and these are the best we have found.  An additional pleasant surprise we found is that they are also useful on hot sand beaches or rocky type beaches to keep feet from getting banged up.  I comparison shop a lot before buying anything - hopefully you can benefit from my time investment and review.

reviewText: this watch looks great but didn't keep time from the start. i was going to return it, however, my husband was so excited that he wore it to work anyway. when he came he said it had stopped working, but when i looked at it he had already scratched it so was's able to return. took it to the jewlers, $70 later it worked for about 60 days and now has stopped keeping time again. the jewler said that many times these watches are "gray" sales. they aren't authentic and will not be repaired  when returned to Wenger. pay the extra and go to an authentic dealer.

Bought this watch for a three week trip to India.  Liked the classic simple look and the brown leather band.  Regrettably, it worked for about five weeks and then stopped.  If I pull the stem out to reset the time and then push it in, the watch works for about a day before stopping again.  This has gone on for a week now.  As I am past my  30 day return period, I am debating whether, and the extent to which, I want to pursue the warranty coverage. I did not expect this problem with a Wenger product, and am surprised and disappointed.

Save your money and try another watch, and perhaps another brand.

I've had a Wenger Classic Field for about 8 years, and the only issue has been with the date adjustment in the last year.  When the leather band wore out I replaced it with a stainless steel band and it looks great.  I love the black face, and the luminous hand and numbers glow bright and clear.  The crystal has really resisted scratches, despite wearing this for camping, fishing, and farm work as well as for going out.

The watch slowed down and the movement needed replacement after 3 months. After sending it back to Wenger (I had to pay for shipping) I got it  back with a small scratch on the crystal. I called Wenger immediately and the person in customer support told me that she couldn't resolve my issue and that her manager needed to get involved. She told me that her manager was in a meeting and would call me after it concluded. After waiting several days with no word from the manager (Irma A.), I called her directly.  After stumbling for words, she told me she was just picking up the phone to call me (yeah right).  She insisted the scratch was there when they received it. If it was there when I sent it in, I would have known it. I'm very particular about things like this. There was nothing documented on the repair checklist regarding the scratch.  It was her word against mine and guess who won?  She told me there was nothing I could do about it and there was no one else I could speak to. I was treated as if i was lying and just trying to get a free 10 dollar crystal. Their customer support philosophy is that all customers are trying to swindle them and we can't be trusted. This was my first and last Wenger purchase.

reviewText:
The marketing for this watch indicates "quick charge, high visibility" for the glow on the luminous hands and indices.

Only the hands glow at a visible strength for more than a few seconds - in fact it lasts several minutes, but the REST of the indices, numerals etc. do not and are only visible even in total darkness for maybe 60 seconds.

I recently learned that the only "glowing" type of watches that have strong and long-lasting visible glow are ones that use "Tritium tubes" for their glow illumination.

The watch itself is nice enough and has a good look, but it's not the MIL-SPEC watch Wengers' marketing materials make it out to be.

reviewText: AWFUL!!! I Purchased this in JAN/FEB2013, return date ends as of 05MAR2013 and the battery is already dead.  This watch lasted less than 6 weeks, I suggest you buy from someone else.  1) Why would a company have a return policy of less than 6 weeks if they were not selling faulty items? 2) It took darn near 4 weeks for me to receive the item to begin with.  I attempted to contact the company before placing a bad review, but their return policy prevented me from doing so, so here it is a bad review.  A great watch sold by a awful vendor.

1) As others have mentioned, the watch is big, but in the product specs it clearly says that the product case is 41 millimeters in diameter. That's 1 and 5/8 inches. So it is big, but the specs clearly state that. 2) On the other hand, one of the pictures of the watch shows that it is just a hair over 25 millimeters (1 inch) wide. That pic is incorrect, and is actually of one of the other Wenger Classic Field Watches. 3) If your wrist is bigger than 7 and 1/2 inches, then plan on getting a long band to replace the regular length band that comes with the watch. My wrist is 7 and 5/8 inches, and the band would only fit on my wrist in the last hole. 4) NOW HERE IS THE PROBLEM: After setting the watch, I noticed two hours later it had lost five minutes. Major disappointment. I set it again, and this time paid attention to it. I noticed that when walking, setting the watch down on a hard table or counter top, etc., that sometimes the second hand would stop moving. Simply gently shaking the watch would get it moving again. Then I tried to reset it again. After resetting it and pushing the crown in, I noticed that just tapping the crown in some instances would stop it. So I reset it again, and gently laid it down and made sure it was still running. 24 hours later, it had lost 55 minutes. 5) Here is the good part: I went back to Amazon.com, logged in, and returned the watch. Amazon as usual was very good about returning items, paying for the shipping and printing UPS labels for me. I gave to watch two stars because I do think it's a good looking watch. I realize it's a big watch, but that is why it looked good IMO and big watches are "in" and the norm these days for men's watches, unless you are getting a $20 lower quality watch. I looked for three weeks for watches before I ordered this watch, and most of the brands that sell $50 to $200 watches these days are 40-50 millimeters. I ordered another Wenger from Amazon after returning this Wenger Swiss Military Men's Classic Field Watch, model #72917. This time I got a Wenger TerraGraph, model #72785. Wenger Men's 72785 TerraGraph Black Dial Black Leather Strap Watch

I bought this watch for my husband in Sept. for his birthday. He wanted something that was easy to read and had a leather band.  This watch fit the bill perfectly.  He loved it from the moment he saw it.  It keeps great time and overall is a great looking watch.  It was a good purchase.  If you're looking for clean and simple, you can't go wrong with this watch.

Watches are a rather personal thing and each of us has specific requirements; likes and dislikes when it comes to what we want strapped to our wrist and what our requirements are in functions; it sort of boils down to "each his own."

My requirements are rather simple and "simple" leads the short list of my requirements.  First, I do not like a lot of whistles and bells.  I have no desire to know the time in each capitol of the world.  I do not need a watch that is waterproof to 10,000 feet.  I could care less as to the phases of the moon.  I do not need an alarm system to remind me of appointments nor do I want something that takes an advanced degree en engineering or computer science to set date, time and what ever.

Secondly, I want a watch that is unobtrusive - clean looking - no glitter or bling.  I want to be able to see the numbers and, both time and date.  I do not want any funny little "sub-dials" cluttering up the face. If the watch appears even slightly pretentious I want nothing to do with it.  But hey, that is just me.

Third, and this is probably one of the more important features I look for, is a watch that actually keep reasonable time consistently.  I hate setting and resetting a watch.  The numbers, both time and date, are easy to read and glow nicely in the dark.

Fifth - I absolutely hate paying more than one hundred dollars for a watch.  I am hard on watches.  I either break them, loose them or generally bang them up.  To pay big buck for something that I am surly bound to destroy, for me, is a complete waste of money.

The watch being reviewed here meets all my requirements.

Now I grant you, like another reviewer here I would prefer that this watch was that of the original and well made Swiss Army watch by Victorinox.  I had one at one time and loved it.  I destroyed it...well, actually an ostrich I was attempting to load in a trailer destroyed it, (ripped the band off and ripped the winding stem off), but the ostrich was only being an ostrich and I probably would have fought just as hard if someone was trying to load me in some strange contraption - I hold no ranker against the bird...the emergency room bill was large, but I have good insurance.  Anyway, I would have preferred to have the Victorinox but I was an am unwilling to pay the price.  The watch being reviewed here, for me, was an excellent compromise.

This watch is a bit larger that watches I normally wear but I am getting use to that.  It is clean looking, attractive and so far (about three months now) it has kept perfect time.

I must admit to have had some trepidation about the leather band.  I spend a lot of time at the gym and biking, and truth be told, sweat like a pig.  So far though the band has held up well and the staining is at a minimum.  When and if the band gets to looking too funky (through no fault of the band itself), I will replace it with something more suited for my lifestyle.

I like this watch and am completely satisfied with it.  If I can get two or three years use out of it without destroying it I will be happy...if it lasts longer, well that for me, is just extra gravy.

Don Blankenship
The Ozarks
summary: FOR ME - THIS IS THE PERFECT WATCH - IT MEETS ALL MY REQUIREMENTS

reviewText:
I suspect many are like me and bought this watch even though we wanted something else. The original Swiss Army watch by Victorinox is exceptionally beautiful, but at a premium price (retails at three times the price). But the Wenger is a good substitute.

I like what I've seen so far, but I'll have to wait. The first watch I got had a loose minute hand that wobbled from side to side as the watch was rotated. I'm pretty sure that's not normal. Note: I'm not talking about the same phenomenon that affects the seconds hand on nearly every digital analog watch. Those are notoriously wobbly and misaligned even on very expensive marques.

This watch is a little bigger than I'm used to (don't know what the reviewer below means by "small") at 41 mm, but I think it'll grow on me. Rolex has a standard of 35mm for their dress watches and Victorinox is about ideal at 38mm. But, hey...bigger is better, right? It sure is easy to read.

Note that the watch pictured above is NOT the same watch that Amazon is shipping. You can see the actual model on Wenger's web site. The bezel is slightly bulkier and the numbers are larger and more blocky in appearance. The band is also different. I actually prefer the look of the one Amazon pictures, but that's not the one you're going to get.

I've had this watch for two months now, and I think what I like about it most, is that you can easily tell what time it is from varying angles. It is comfortable on the wrist, looks classy, and I'm sure this watch will last a long time - I have only owned swiss military watches for the past 30 years - and they have never failed me.
summary: Easy to See What Time it Is

reviewText:
I don't write a lot of reviews, especially negative ones.  But I feel the urge to write on here in part because I am confounded by what Clarks has done to their unstructured line.

I purchased a pair of unstructured shoes about 5-6 years ago that I wore to death.  Loved them; very comfortable and stylish.  About three years ago I purchased a another pair (un.bend) that were not the same.  Something had changed and the shoe dug into my foot in all the wrong places.  It was as if the base of the shoe was too narrow in the middle of the foot.  I wore them for a while, though my feet were killing me.  I eventually ate the cost and did not come back to clarks until recently.

Over the last few months I decided to try clarks again (unstructured to be specific) and I'll be darned if I am not experiences the same issue again.  I tried on several pairs from the casual line and each and everyone one of them presents the same issue.  The shoe bed appears to not be very even and it digs into the sole of my foot at the arch as well as the part opposite the arch on my foot.

I have no idea how or why I feel this and how it seems so bad for me yet not for others.  I mean, I could understand it if the insole had a high arch designed for support and that it bothered me.  But in my case, I am feeling like there is something protruding at the arch AND the other side.  That makes absolutely no sense yet there it is.

So after trying on numerous pairs, it seems unstructured is no longer for me.  Wish someone could explain what  I am feeling because in terms of style, I really like many of the shoes.

reviewText: I bought a pair of these three years ago.  I was a little reluctant on spending this much on casual shoes having never owned Clark's before.  They are very comfortable and have held up better than any other shoe I have owned in recent memory.  The outside is quite stylish and the inside pigskin is cool, soft, and very durable.  This is an area often overlooked by shoe manufacturers yet it is the inside where your feet spend all their time with the shoe.  These shoes breath, my feet don't sweat very much, the soles are supportive, and the material looks like new.  Fabric lined shoes often tear or develop holes long before the outside of the shoe wears out.  That is just throwing money away.  As an engineer I wear these every day in an industrial environment.  Other than with a suit I wear them with just about everything else.  As long as Clark's makes these I will buy them.  Best shoes ever!

This is my third pair of Clarks Unstructured Coil oxfords.

FIT/COMFORT
The fit has remained consistent through at least the last 5 or more years since I've been wearing these shoes.  This model happens to fit my foot perfectly.  Length is consistent with other footwear and I'd say is true to size.  For me, I have a slightly wide foot and these shoes fit spot on.  That being said, if you have a narrow foot, you may find the fit to be too wide.  While I require a wide in some shoes, these I can wear the regular width and it's fine.  I also have a fairly high instep and these fit me there well. They are fairly compliant and adjustable with lacing.  The shoes break in beautifully.  Not so soft to be worthless, not stiff at all.  These are honestly more comfortable than any sneaker or other shoe I own and they often get worn on the weekend too.

Durability
I wear mine down until the soles is practically worn through and i get several years of almost daily wear out of them.

MISC
Venting really works.  My feet remain as dry as possible in the summer.  Wear these with a wool blend sock and it's as dry as you can expect to be.

However, the venting is the Achilles heel of these shoes. They are NOT for all weather situations and you WILL get wet feet due to puddles and standing water in parking lots and such.  If they only made this shoe with Gore-Tex XCR liners (or at least on the vent to prevent water intrusion) I'd lose my mind!

She had explained how the shoe needed some break-in, which I didn't believe because most of my other soft leather shoes felt broken into at purchase. reviewText: Not a watch nut but own about 6 and was looking for something new to add to the rotation.  This watch was a great value and fit my needs well.  Its easy to read, face is a little larger without being a Silver Dollar on your wrist.  Victorinox makes some great watches and this one is nicer than my Tag.  The red contrasting hands look outstanding.

These are going fast - 3 left when I ordered, now down to 1 - another listing on Amazon has 5 but for a bit more money.  It's a discontinued watch that's been blown out lately.

This particular movement, as some others have noted, is an ETA 251.262 - becoming rarer to find lately as Swatch now owns it and apparently non-Swatch companies (they own quite a few major brands) no longer have access to it.  It has been used by many makers including TAG and Breitling and in several VSA models that will be very hard to find now.  I have a TAG with it that has been very reliable for several years.

The main great thing about this movement is the BIG minutes counter rather than a subdial.  There are few automatic watches that feature this and a few quartz watches based on the Soprod movement that was in TAG's Calibre S and now the VSA Chrono 1/100.  The downside to those movements is that the entire face of the watch is used for the chronograph so that real time and measured time are not simultaneously visible.

This is a great deal on a really nice looking, well built watch and a bargain at this price.  Good luck to the last lucky buyer!

As also noted, read the manual to learn how to zero the hands - there's a handy PDF version on-line too.

I am a watch aficionado with far more watches than I really need.  But this is one of my favorites.  Here are some likes:

1.  It has an ETA 251.262 movement.  This movement displays chronograph minutes with a full-diameter sweeping hand, like its red sweep second hand - but silver colored.  This makes makes reading minutes of the chronograph 1,000% easier than typical tiny sub-dial watches.

2.  It's titanium which reduces weight and makes the large size reasonably comfortable to wear.

3.  I like the clean design.  Many chronographs are encumbered with a lot of fine markings which obscure readability.

I have only one complaint:
The hands and numerals are reflective steel.  At some angles this is great.  But at other angles they are too dark against the background of the black dial.  I prefer matte finish white painted hands and numerals.

I selected this watch for my 30 year company service award 12 months ago.  After reading reviews and researching this model, am very glad I selected it. I get lots of compliments on the style and look.

I looked at other, similar watchs, but this watch just blew me away!  I "almost" bought an Air Boss, but this watch has SO much more to offer. I love that it has the Air Boss - style of full size second and minute hand chrono. But it ALSO has a standard second hand, which the AB does not. So, if you are trying to synch your time with a computer down to the second, how would you do that with an AB with no second hand? Also, the watch is drop-dead gorgeous.  I really like the counntdown bezel, which is often what I use to time the grill, etc, but this is so elegant, without the big "handles" or protrusions of other Swiss Army models. The hour up-or-down is a great feature, too, and not every model has that. In short this model has it ALL.

I can't ever recall being so happy with a purchase. Amazon makes it so easy, too.

reviewText: The presence of so many positive reviews is a testament to the quality of this watch.  For a sporty quartz chrono, it nears perfection for its price range.  Every detail is immaculately crafted, from the alternating brushed/polished steel on the bezel and bracelet, to the domed crystal and intricate detail on the face.  I hacked the second hand to official time 96 hours ago, and have been comparing the time. In four days, I am yet to see it lose or gain even a single second.  I have no doubt that it will after a while, but I can always see at least some inaccuracy after four days on most watches. Not this one.  That's one reason why so many people love the ETA 251.262 movement.  The red highlights in the hands and logo are a tasteful addition to the look of the Alpnach, and the second hour hand coupled with the rotating bezel for marking elapsed time is actually a useful feature.  This is a watch lover's watch, and I believe it stacks up in form, fit, and function to quartz watches in any price range.  I sometimes wonder at the MSRP of other Victorinox watches, but I can see why this one has a suggested retail well over $800.00. At the time of this review, I paid 360.00 for mine,and at that price the value is unbelievable.  Even if it was over $500.00, it would still be well worth it.  You can't go wrong with this watch, so long as you buy it from a reputable seller who can exchange it in the unlikely event of malfunction.  This watch will not disappoint!

Beautiful new timepiece

summary: Beautiful new timepiece Love the ETA 251

I needed a comfortable, light weight travel shoe for an upcoming trip in general but more specifically for canyoneering in the Dominican Republic.  Something that would give me good traction, especially when wet, for the rappels and be comfortable in and out of the waterfalls.  I have wide feet and a high instep so when I see that shoes are true to size based on customer reviews, I always contemplate going a half size up to get a little extra room in the toe box.  I'm normally an 8.5W so I ordered both the 8.5M and 9M, planning to keep the one that was more comfortable and return one all along.  However, both were too long.  Do NOT order up a half size like some of the reviews say and do NOT be nervous about selecting this shoe if your feet are on the wider side.  Consider ordering a half size down if you are worried about your normal size fitting.  This shoe offers quite a bit of adjustment for fit in the laces as well as the heel strap so I probably could have gotten away with the 8.5M but I just didn't think it was worth turning a once-in-a-lifetime day trip into a miserable experience because my shoes didn't fit properly, risking blisters and pain.  A VERY slight inconvenience but I like the shoes too much to shop around for another brand/model.  I've already placed another order for the 8M and will return the original two larger sizes once I confirm the smallest pair fits but I assume they will be perfect.  I will update my review on how they worked out for my particular activity after the trip!  UPDATE: The 8M fits PERFECTLY and I LOVE them!
