reviewText:
The PUMA Men's Tazon Cross-Training Shoe is a very good product aimed at people who are both regular runners as well as workout enthusiasts. The shoes are well fitting and also look quite good. It provides good arch support and is definitely comfortable enough to wear for long workouts at the gym or for running a few miles.

The shoes however are not quite as comfortable to wear all day and is best used when limited to periods of activity that require good athletic shoes. These shoes are somewhat wide, however that does not take away from having a comfortable experience engaging in strenuous activity in them.

For USD 65/-, this shoe sits on a medium price range. As a daily user of this product however, I believe that there might be better shoes on the market within the same price range that can also be used in a larger variety of situations. Apart from its price and comfort pertaining to long term use, these shoes are definitely a good choice for any casual athlete or avid runner.

Enjoy!
summary: The PUMA Men's Tazon Cross-Training Shoe is a very good product aimed at people who are both regular runners ...

Sharp looking, Hard Working, Soft Fitting.
All around Badass kicking pair of sneakers.
FITTING: I gave a local Puma store a chance with these, but they didn't carry the Tazon 3. Anyway, I got the chance to try a similar model and confirm that I needed a number 10 size, instead of the usual #9.5; Plus, at about $50, Amazon gave me a better deal.
STYLE: These kicks got a nice styling, cool but subdued at the same time, very classic look no matter if you're using jeans or shorts.
PERFORMANCE: They provide good support to the whole foot, stability to the ankle, flexibility, grip... How do I know all that? Well, I've been putting mine to intensive use on the street, walking, running, driving, playing a lot of street basketball with them (tough I know I shouldn't). Never had an issue with them.
COMFORT & BREATHING: They are very comfortable even after many hours of use. Something very important as I live in a tropical country, is the capacity of the shoe to breath. These sneakers are not leather, but synthetic, but they breath very well, keeping my feet from overheating. Those many perforations, and the interior construction of the upper allow for the air to circulate when needed.
My recommendations with this and any other sneakers: Always use socks, sometimes use talc powder, and google "ankle lock sneakers".
RELIABILITY: In five hard months these Puma's only issue was to lose the upper layer of the sockliners, which I reattached with some thin double tape after the last wash. Other than that, they are as good as new inside, outside and downside, which is outstanding, when you consider the amount of punish that I had dealed to this loyal pair of sidekicks.
Do I recommend them? Well, I'll get another pair of breds when (and if) I finish these, and soon will consider to buy a pair in another color combo. So, yes, I do recommend them, because they are well beyond their price range. (And yes, a pair of proper basketball shoes in its way, thanks)

I didn't purchase these shoes for running so much as for a starter weightlifting shoe that would offer stability overall. I needed something that was wider closer to the front of my foot than the back, but also not cost me several hundred dollars to get started.

Now that I've used them for over a month, they continue to maintain their seams well, and provide the comfort that's needed when weightlifting. With them being a bit narrow, id likely need to wear them continually to break them in, but all in all these were exactly what I needed to get started.

reviewText: Comfortable and fits great

Been buying the same line of shoes for quite a while now. Im a creature of habit. They always fit pretty much the same, though its luck of the draw on how long they actually last. Some have held up considerably well for the environments in which I wear them. Others have deteriorated quicker. I think I have had around 4 pairs of these now. Different colors but mostly black/silver. I hate going shopping for shoes, and I know these always fit. Hence, why I am a return customer.

At first, the fit of these shoes were kind of small on my feet. I'm tall and have large-ish feet, and I"ve worn PUMAs before, so I kind of expected this. After a while, it does get easier to use. I'm a frequent runner so I tend to wear out my running shoes, but these are still lasting me from when I bought them. I also like that I feel well supported on these shoes. I've had running shoes where I barely feel there's any cushion, but these feel comfortable (after the first couple weeks).

I do recommend these shoes, or anything PUMA, I guess ultimately, make sure the size is perfect for your feet! Maybe go up half a size or so.
summary: Smallish fit at first, but great shoe otherwise!

reviewText: Love them and their comfortable

These shoes are very comfortable and seem (so far) to be well-constructed. They are listed as cross-training shoes, but the insoles actually have "running' printed on them. They are definitely not as well suited for running (which is fine for my purposes, as I have other shoes for running) due to limited breathability, but they are great for walking, light sports/exercise, and for general casual wear.

I have narrow feet, and the width is great for me. If you have wider feet, you will probably consider these shoes to be tight and restricting. Overall, the size seems to run a tiny bit small. I normally wear a 12.5 or 13, depending on the shoe. These in a 13 really feel more like a slightly small 12.5, so you might want to try a half-size up from your usual size.

Also, I have high arches, so the arch support could be a little better. I can't hold that against these Pumas, as I have yet to find a pair of shoes (athletic, casual, dress, or otherwise) that has enough arch support for me. All-in-all, these have better arch support than most.

Overall, these feel great and look great. I've only had them for about a week, so we'll see how they are after the break-in period. I'm optimistic.
summary: Great casual/light exercise shoes. Good for narrow feet. Nice styling.

CONS-

 Arch support  similar to all Puma shoes I have owned, the arch support isn't spectacular. I have fairly flat feet so it doesnt bother me much but people with high arches might have issues.

reviewText: In the last 10 years or so I've had the best luck fitting into Puma's, partially because I always have the problem of one foot just doesn't fit right.  In this case left foot didn't fit right, it was just slightly rubbing against my little toe, but I've always had somewhat wide feet.  Right foot was perfect.  I ended up going with Tazon 5 Mesh Training Shoe.

The only thing that really bothered me was that the Crimson Red on the sides look a little pinkish in the sunlight. But it's not that big of a deal.

The shoes are very nice. It looks like its well built, and when I put them on, they were pretty light too.

It came a little small, just as I wanted. I wear a 12.5 Wide shoe. I use two different kinds of shoes, a flat, heavy one for lifting weights, and a light, flexible one for running. However, I needed something that was the best of both worlds due to my gym class switching between lifting and running constantly within class.

The shoe itself is very light. I had no trouble running in them. The bottom is nice and flat, but the design allows it to easily flex in case I switch from a resistance exercise to a cardiovascular exercise. I also choose a shoe size that was a bit smaller than normal so that it'd be a tight squeeze (which it was). This makes it so that I don't lose balance as easily when I run, and so that my feet stay in one place when I lift.

Cross training is right. It's a nice shoe. I just wish they came in 12.5 sizes so that it'd be a perfect fit.
summary: Somewhat small, but I factored that into my choice

Back story:

I'm middle aged, so I'm probably not the target audience for these shoes BUT I broke my foot a couple months ago and had to wear a "boot" until it was mended.

I'm not great with doctor's instructions and after about a month, my foot still wasn't feeling right, but I wasn't going to wear that darned boot any more.

I purchased these cross trainers intending to use them at the gym for additional support as I worked back into a workout routine.

Funny thing...these shoes are so supportive and well padded that they feel better than the boot did AND I don't limp when I'm wearing them.

I'm told it will likely take my foot another six months or so to get fully back to where it was and I intend to wear these sneakers as much as I can to help me do the job.

Review:

These PUMA's are good looking, but most importantly, they are practical, and effective.

Cross trainers should be useful for a variety of athletic requirements - particularly the gym.

These shoes are very supportive laterally as well as from the sole. There is good cushioning.

The shoes run a bit on the small size, so you may want to order up a half or whole size from your street shoes.

The quality seems to be quite good.

I highly recommend these shoes.

reviewText:
Pros:
Comfortable, breathable, very good stabilization in the heel, low-to-moderate rise in the heel.

Cons:
Not much arch support, sole is a bit stiff for running.

This is a nice, comfortable cross-trainer.  It's a bit large, and if this is common across sizes (I typically wear a 9), I would suggest looking at something a 1/2 size smaller than what you typically wear.  Or just load up on socks.  The complaints about arch support and the stiff sole are minor gripes.  The shoe felt a lot worse when I first put them on, but they are breaking in nicely after about a week of occasional use.

All told, these shoes will be my regular gym workout shoes and occasional/travel running shoes.  The arch support and sole are not really designed for serious running, but they will suffice for the occasional 5-10k while I'm away from home and don't want to carry too many sets of shoes.
summary: Fit is a bit large, but otherwise a decent cross-trainer

Per the recommendation of other reviewers, I purchased size 11 when I usually take 10.5. This was nearly not enough of an increase, you may want to get 2 half sizes bigger. They fit like a snug glove for me though, with no hot-spots. I think they will feel even better as they break in.

I will admit that my foot is slightly wider than a true D width, but not so wide as to justify a EE.  However, most shoes (especially athletic shoes) have enough flexibility to allow for my extra width without any discomfort.  Not so with these.

My advice is to understand that Pumas run small (and narrow).  If you can make these adjustments and find a well-fitting shoe, these appear to be an attractive purchase.

reviewText: I wanted to like this so did my husband.  He wears a size 10 shoe, has for years.  I ordered a 10 and it was about 2 sizes too small.

I wear them with a trouser sock usually with pants but have worn them barefoot with just a sprinkle of powder (Zeabsorb) on the weekends paired with shorts  Very comfortable and they still smell new inside.  I'm LOVING THAT, and may speak to the antimicrobial properties in the footbed.

I hope to find a lace-up style like this but with no pattern, like plain black or something so it can go with more outfits.

I did change the laces to regular, black round laces though.  I did not like the 'boat shoe' laces it came with.  They look good also with round, black dress laces.

I was absolutely hesitant about this purchase because it was recommended by the infamous "friend of a friend", and as I selected above, they definitely fit a bit smaller than other shoes of the same size, but Sanuks are excellent. I've bought several other products from the company since this order. The padding in the sole cushions every step and it feels like you're almost floating; the tribal pattern doesn't hurt the overall quality one bit. For the cost, for any cost.. definite purchase if you're interested.
I love these.  With or without the leather laces they fit and feel great.  The black print on the shoe is subtle and looks awesome.
I have taken the laces out and they still feel a little close but if there like my last pair they will soon stretch.

These shoes are amazing. Below is a detailed review:
Look/Style:  They look fantastic!  They go with just about anything.  I wear them with jeans, board shorts, khaki shorts, swimming trunks, anything.  They have a very classic look and I get a lot of compliments about how they look.  They some with an extra set of laces so you don't have to keep the leather laces on them, but you can also go without laces because the tongue is connected to the shoe with a bit of elastic.
Comfort:  This is where these shoes really stand out.  They have all the comfort of a Croc-like sandal without any of the downsides.  My feet get nasty sweaty in Crocs, but with these I am always comfortable.  The upper part of the shoe really help wick away moisture and keep your feet pretty dry.  They also breathe really well.  They are light, but protect your foot quite well.  There are no weird rubbing spots and I wore them out of the bag without any blisters or sore spots at all.  The innersole is a rubber material and quite comfortable.  Also they have an anti-bacterial treatment that really helps to keep your feet from smelling bad.  I wear them with and without socks.  They are comfortable either way.
Durability:  I will post again after a few months, but so far, so good.  These things are holding up to the worst Africa has to throw at them.  There are no cracks or tears and the seams are all holding up very well.  I didn't expect them to last, but they are performing well beyond my expectations.  They dry out quickly after getting wet and are great pool shoes as well as leisure shoes.
I cannot recommend these shoes enough.  They are awesome and I will be buying a pair every time they go on sale.  These are truly worth the money.  Best Shoes Ever!

I like Sanuk as the cloth is loose and so it is kind to my Bunyon.  I also like there casual funky look. One improvement I would like to see is that they last longer.  Still I have tried many shoes and all hurt my bunyon except Sanuk.

These shoes came exactly as advertied, Fits true to size and are as comfortable as shoes can get. The stlying is rad, and always gets compliments. Definitely will be wearning these all summer and for the rest of the year!
Love sanuk.  Their "sandals" outlast and of the competitors. Nice sockless alternative to shoes.  Casual enough yet formal enough to wear any day.  VERY COMFORTABLE
Perfect shoe for everyday use and are really comfy to wear. Look really good and fit perfectly. I would recomend this product to anyone who likes this kind of shoe

The normal retail price is usually about twice as much as what I paid on Amazon.

I normally wear size 7 Sanuks since I know they stretch, but these are lace ups so I went with the 8. If you intend to wear them without laces though, go with a size that's slightly snug. Again, unlike regular insulated and reinforced shoes, these are thin layered, so they stretch.

I now own several pairs of Sanuk loafers in a variety of colors and styles.  All fit and look great.  The laced loafers are my latest purchase and several coworkers have asked where they can get a pair.

They actually send this with tennis shoe laces and the leather ones as options. I wear Sanuks a lot so this is my first pair with laces. Also, the laces could come in handy if you need to strangle someone who doesn't like Sanuks. One pair to keep them on your feet and the other laces for death. On the other hand the New Balance straps are more comfortable - the Moving Comfort velcro occasionally touches my skin.

I do light 3-4 mile runs and am close to a D cup. This bra works great for my needs. Washes well on cold/delicate, air dry.

Have since lost almost a cup size since purchasing this bra and it has become my new favorite. Adjusted my star rating from a 4 to a 5 and ordering more. Still nice and snug. I do wear a cotton yoga bra underneath to help absorb sweat, but this bra would be fine bounce-wise all on it's own.

The downside is that it gives you squashed uniboob, but I totally don't care. It keeps the girls in place and out of the way so I can move on with my life. If I want to "lift and separate" for my husband's benefit, I just wear something else. :-)

As for comfort, it is a little binding. The fabric doesn't have much stretch, but that's what makes it so effective at eliminating bounce. While I'm grateful to take it off at the end of a long day, I'm comfortable enough while it's on to keep it on for up to 12 hours sometimes.

Side note: The straps adjust in the front and are removable, so this also works as a nursing bra. I actually bought my first one for that reason, but I loved it so much that 6 years later I'm still wearing these almost exclusively. The straps are also almost infinitely adjustable, which is great for us petite women who have trouble finding bras with short enough straps (especially sports bras, which tend to be adjustable only on the back half).

Overall, this is a GREAT choice for women looking for a zero-bounce bra, especially if you area also nursing. I expect to be wearing this bra for the rest of my active life.

reviewText:
In summary, I'm impressed as I didn't expect much - new balance bras tend to leave me disappointed and there are few options in the sportswear world for larger-chested women.

This bra is undoubtedly comfortable as far as a bra is concerned, sports bra or regular. The band doesn't cut off air supply but still supplies moderate support - usually sports bras act more like corsets but there's none of that feeling here. There's minimal stretch to the material, but with a back closure it allows better control without contortionist moves to get it on. It is a thicker material so it will show lines through thin material workout shirts.

Like I said there is still bounce with this bra, but only 30% or so which is better than your run of the mill sports bra without the constriction. Honestly, I have just as much bounce in my $60 panache sports bra, but that bra has the extra support and better shaping of underwire. For this bra, moderate activity is perfect; if you double up its good to go for a run.

I am a DDD cup size but the D sizing held me in sufficiently without spillage or squishing. This is definitely a decent bra, not perfect, but good quality for the price and good for at least a backup.

I purchased two of these from a local shop (to get the right fit). These are my favorite bras right now. I wear them all day, while exercising (gym/cardio/plyometrics), walking, and hiking.

As an active nursing mom, I need support and easy front access. I thought a zipper-front sports bra would work but it's a hassle to get back on when I am on-the-go. This bra has hooks to attach the band in the back, like most bras, but it also has straps that are adjustable from the front, and can also be opened from the front. This is how I nurse while hiking/walking.

Folks who say the bra is not supportive enough may be either in the wrong size, or adjusted improperly. You will want the band to be quite tight, for starters. The front straps attach in such a way that you may stop where the velcro stops, but you can make it as tight as you need to. I definitely need to make the straps tighter for higher impact activities and my cardio workouts, this is where all the motion comes from. I am wearing a 34DD and find that I am getting adequate support for what I do.

My ONLY recommendation is to buy a band size down, and a cup size up. This will ensure that the band is tight enough to support you, and that there is room for the bra to stretch out over time as they normally will do. (Going big on the band size is not wise because you will start out using the smallest hooks, and then as the bra stretches there is no way to continue getting support.)

reviewText: This bra fit me well and gave good support while jogging. By comparison, the Champion bra (same size) was painfully tight across the chest and was returned, and the Glamorise Adjustable Bounce bra was comfortable but not as supportive while jogging.

Also, the 40 has 4 back hooks, while the 38 only had 3 (which I preferred).  Both do provide great support when jogging, spinning or doing interval training on the elliptical.

i recently had breast augmentation surgery and bought these bras when looking for something more affordable than Under Armour's 32D zipper front bras (which are perfect, but a little pricey at $50 a pop).

I recently ended up being professionally fitted and found that I am really a 32DD. These bras do run a bit small and I kind of feel like they are cutting off much needed circulation to my healing breasts (this may be my mistake for not being fitted before buying) BUT! they def do the job as promised--no movement what so ever when working out. The straps are adjustable with velcro, but don't budge. I wish they made these with more adjustable straps, they don't give the opportunity to adjust very much.  Three options for hook closure at the back, very sturdy.

My suggestion is to get fitted before buying (for free at Victoria's Secret) or if you know you are between sizes buying one cup bigger.

First of all, if you prefer pockets this purse is great.  The small zipper pocket on the right will fit any non-tablet phone securely.  The larger diagonal pocket on the front is shallow and has two pen slots  There's a velcro pocket right behind those.  There's one more smaller zipper pocket on the back of the purse that fits a standard square wallet, or for me my coin purse.  The biggest zipper pocket and the main part of the purse is huge.  I keep my wallet, GPS, a small notebook, a ziplock bag with my lotion and hand sanitzer, and various other lady things in there and still have room to spare.  Theres another zipper pocket inside here as well.

The inside is lined in the same light green on the front.  It's made of a more durable polyester that so far after about six months is showing zero signs of wear and tear.  The strap can easily adjust and STAY adjusted to be either an underarm purse or in my case I use it more like a messenger bag.  It's generally flatter than most purses I've had so it works very well as a messenger and hugs your side nice without bouncing around.

My only issue with it is that it's just a bit big for me.  I tend to collect papers and reciepts in my purse, so the bigger they are the more crap I collect, but that's a super personal preference (I'm not really the trendy type).  Otherwise it's really an average size purse at about 14" long.

(In order to leave a review I had to select a 'how does this tie fit' option, which I did only so I could write a review).

I'm not sure what all the 5-star rave reviews are about. While the tie design as pictured warrants a 5-star rating, in both my husband's and my opinion the tie itself is only a 3 or a 4 star, at the most.

The picture in the ad appears to be HD (high definition), because if you look in the picture below of the actual tie - the tie print does not look dimensional.  Whereas the tie in the ad has hazy-blurred highlights that make it look so good - the actual tie does not have that effect.  The white/lighter highlights on the tie are flat, which really detracts from the appearance - compared to the image in the ad. (Please compare the image I posted to the advertisement image, and you will see what I mean.)

That said, in my opinion this is only a 'nice tie,' nothing to rave about.  Appearance is good, quality of material and workmanship is just OK (nothing to brag about).  This is an OK value for the $18.95 sale price I paid.  Although my husband likes the tie for the music themed design, both he and I are disappointed that the tie does not look as good 'in person' as it does in the online image that prompted the purchase.

Again, the image of the tie in the advertisement has been touched-up; it looks air-brushed or HD.  The blues and highlighted areas are brighter and more prominent in the ad than the tie actually is. This is why I only gave the tie a 3 star rating. If it had looked as good as it does t in the ad, I would have given it 5-stars.
summary: OK TIE AT AN OK PRICE, BUT NOT AS EYE-POPPING AS IT IS IN THE AD

reviewText:
I have been wearing Brooks motion control shoes for almost a decade now.  I needed a pair that would not be so obviously out of place in the office, and these are the first in black I'd ever found.  Having always gotten Women's shoes from Brooks, I actually called my local store (Who did not currently have this in stock, but would gladly order it for me!) and asked about the size differences from Men's to Women's.  I wear 10 in Brooks Women's and a 9 in Brooks Men's.

So long as you do your homework and pay attention, these shoes truly are everything they are supposed to be.  My body never feels so good in any other shoe.  Bear in mind, if you do not need the motion control, you might want to look at another shoe, because these are pretty strong for us pronators. ;)

Brooks Addiction 11
 shoes are the most comfortable!
Not just for running! They are my every day shoe!
Wish they came in other solid colors.

A few years ago, I had a proper shoe fit from a running shop that suggested Brooks shoes for my wide, flat feet. I liked them so much that I bought two pair in a row. This time, I decided to try out the Addiction 11s. They fit a bit wider than the same size in the Brooks GTS model; enough that there is noticeable lateral sliding while running, which is pretty annoying. The Addiction 11 shoes are also a lot heavier. While they have a ton of extra sole in the arch of the foot, they actually don't seem to support my feet any better than the GTS model. The extra sole makes them look like orthopedic shoes that your grandma would wear. The black model (which I purchased) is so ugly that my wife shuns me anytime that I wear them.
Quite simply, saved my feet! The least expensive and best answer to my problem. Would recommend without any hesitation. Great.

I have low arches and have found that Books shoes, combined with a medium grade arch support, allow me to be on my feet all day without pain.  The Addiction series (I've worn the 9, 10 and now the 11) shoes are the only ones I've found that do the job my feet require.  They're a bit expensive, but also nice looking and long lasting, equally meaning attributes to most purchasers.

My husband has flat feet and I bought these for him for his morning runs. He was shocked at how much of a difference the extra arch support provides for comfort as compared to his old pair of Nike Air Max. Great shoes.

I have run in Addictions for more than 10 years. For stability, cushioning and motion control this shoes is outstanding (I have serious pronation on my left foot which used to destroy other shoes, but after 500+ miles on a pair of Addictions there is never any visible inner wear on the left shoe whatsoever). You may find one shoe more highly rated for cushioning, another shoe better for motion control, yet another which is lighter, still another which has more cushioning, but for solid ratings across the board in ALL the aspects combined (as well as reasonable pricing) I wouldn't want to trade my Addictions.
summary: My Go-To Training Shoe for More Than A Decade

I got my first HOBO bag as a gift almost 10 years ago, and I've been a fan every since. The only purses I buy are HOBO, because they last, they're comfortable and they rarely go out of style. That initial purse I received, I still get compliments on it.

Oddly enough, I didn't own a single black pursue until this one. I couldn't be happier. You may hesitate on the price initially, but I shop around for a good deal. The one piece you need to remember is you're not buying a purse that's only going to last a few months, these will last you a decade plus if you take care of it. And by take care of it, I mean normal use, wipe it down on occasion, but live your life :)

A few things, the size in the picture of the lady holding it, is pretty accurate. It  is wide, however this is not an oversized bag. It is slim lined so it fits perfectly under you arm, but had enough size that you could probably hold a 6 pack of water bottles. The small straps may seem like they'd be uncomfortable, however unless you're going to be packing 20 lbs in that purse, it's quite comfortable. The two pockets on the outside of the purse are glorious. I use the small one for my keys, the big one for my phone, it's perfect. But, if you're in a "questionable" area, the handy pockets on in the inside (which every HOBO has) fit an iPhone, and another for my keys just perfectly. It's a very clean, understated and classy purse without being overbearing. The leather is extremely soft, and the vintage looks gives it a slightly broken in look. Which, I have to give HOBO a hi-5, I own 3 vintage leather bags and they get more compliments than any of the other bags I own.

All in all, this bag will be a staple for you.

**Oh one small thing, and I think this goes for any leather bag with sealed seams on a stiff handle. If you are a heavy user of a single purse without switching out regularly (which I am, a very seasonal user), you will notice wear on the handles and some slightly cracking in the seam sealer. I've really only noticed this in the lighter colored bags like red, grey and pink. I haven't experienced this with the darker colors like black and dark brown.  Again this is ONLY with the stiff handles, I don't believe this bag will have that problem.

reviewText: This HOBO Tote Handbag is beautiful!  Love the color.  I purchased this handbag for a silent auction item at my golf outing fund-raiser, "Beat Breast Cancer", August 23rd.  I like handbags with many "pockets" and this one definitely meets that criteria. Regarding my silent auction, I always purchase items I would like to own  myself and I'm sure the women attending the outing will be thrilled.  This handbag is a "thumbs up."

I purchased this bag for it's many functional features.  The leather is soft and supple. Outside pockets for cell phone and keys makes organizing easy and my ipad fits as well.  Bottom is wide and due to the design, bag opens up wide and you can easily see everything inside.

The color is fantastic and after 2 weeks and an airplane ride, holding up well.  I really like the little feet on the bottom and the side pockets are perfect for storing my cell phone and keys.  The only suprise for me (I don't know why I was surpsed since the picture is pretty clear!) is the width of the straps.  They are pretty thin but seem to be robust and holding up fine.  I love the HOBO brand and this bag is perfect for me.
This bag is everything I hoped it would be  very roomy, comfortable to carry, soft and supple. Love it!
The leather if so very beautiful to look at and to feel.  I would recommend this bag and this leather to my friends.:)

My bag was just delivered and I am about to have a thrill seizure!! This has got to be the PERFECT bag! It is for me anyway!
Perfect size, not too big or to small, lots of usable room with 5 inside pockets for organization. Then an outside pocket deep enough for a wallet if you choose. We all know how convenient an outside pocket is, yet so many bags lack one! Then the extra special delight of the little smart phone pocket on the back. This feature is not listed in the ad, and had I not read someone's review would not have known about it. Had to really enlarge the photos to find it even then. You really have to search the photos but once you know its there you can see it right at the top center of the back. Beware, the new Patti is different and doesn't have it as well as several other features I love.
I love the way the straps are attached without clunky cheap looking metal rings. Which the newer has (ugh). I also love thin straps, wider straps again look cheap to me. And the length is perfect! It can be carried easily by hand or over the shoulder. This is fantastic as with some bags they have handles and a shoulder strap, and you have to decide which, OR deal with all that tangly strap mess everyday!
The leather has to be felt to believed! Scrumptious is the only word for it! I got the Keely wallet in Harvest for C'mas and loved it so much went searching for a matching bag! The match is perfect of course.
There are the usual little HOBO touches. The pretty contrasting linings that make finding your contents easier, and enjoyable. There are the HOBO imprinted zipper pulls, and a sweet little HOBO hangtag that removes to be used as a key fob.
This design has metal feet, another worthwhile feature missing from the new Patti. I really appreciate this feature to keep the bottom of your bag clean.
The bag is just structured enough that it stands upright. This is so important to me that i have actually opened the seams in linings and added lightweight cardboard to bags to get this feature. I hate bags to flop over, when you remove the paper, loosing all the design style that attracted you in the first place.
To me this is THE perfect bag, so much so that I am going to purchase it in another color before this style disappears from the marketplace.

This bag is very light to carry and makes it easy to access anything I may need.  There are plenty of pockets for all my stuff.  I love the cell phone pocket.  The color is great & the leather feels & smells fabulous!  I LOVE HOBO BAGS!!!!
Absolutely love Hobo brand. Such soft leather. Feels great and wears well. The imperfections created in the leather from regular use just add to the beatiful character.

Purse is attractive enough . My problem is that it just does not feel like a $250.00 purse. It is a bit flimsy - does not stand up but collapses a bit. I like the size. This purse feels like it should  have been in the $100 to $125 dollar range based on the look and how it feels. I adore the Hobo brand. Have had several clutches which still look great after several years. Hobo is a quality brand.
summary: Does not feel like a Hobo

reviewText: I'm not a purse fan by any stretch. But I do need one. I carry this every day. It's great for work, and also great for shopping. Now that CA charges 10 cents a bag, and all those bags are wasteful anyway, it's nice to be able to toss a small purchase in my purse. Very high quality. I love Hobo bags.

I'm usually a size 9, and I couldn't even get this size 9 boot on my foot.  This seemed like more of a manufacturing error than running small. I was also disappointed with the general quality of the boot, the leather was fine but the sole was so thin. Bummer.

This is the most comfortable boot I've purchased in the last 10 years.
Great product. Don't quit making them..That's why I ordered another pair.

These boots are very nice. They do run a bit small so go a half size up. Also they are somewhat narrow. Good for me, but not so good for someone with a wide foot. The heel height is great and very comfortable to wear. They look great with both jean or a dress.

First off, these shoes definitely run small. I sized up from my usual 8.5 to a 9, and I thought for certain I'd mistakenly ordered the 8.5 when I tried it on. It fit, but it was still tighter than I expected. Until I break these in a bit more/ stretch them out, I'd be hard pressed to wear semi-thick socks at all. It also seems to run slightly narrow, so I'd go for the wide if you have even the slightest hint of a wide foot.

On the plus side, Bass nearly always does a great job with actually padding their shoes, which is great for my high arches. It's one of the main reasons I keep coming back. And the quality of construction is really evident. I think it's just going to take a bit of breaking in before these go from reasonably comfortable to definitely comfortable.

The sizing is the only reason for 4 instead of 5 stars.  They're really beautiful and well made, and very comfortable.  But, as another reviewer wrote, they run small, and I needed the next size up.  Other than that, they're a 5-star pair of boots.

Addendum: BEWARE. I'd gotten the smaller size from Planet Shoes. I'd checked their return policy, and they said "free returns." Well, there IS a return fee... $6.95, which they skate by with, by calling it a "handling fee" or some such.  So they don't charge for the shipping, but 7 bucks is NOT free. AND you have to drop it off at UPS.  No home pickup.  Total lie and rip-off.

Comfortable, cute, a little different with the laces instead of zippers. I found it better to leave that top lace a little loose for more comfort when walking. Nice caramel color. Looks great with dress pants as well as jeans.  Nice leather. Looks like suede in the picture, but it's not which is good for me. Now I won't worry about wearing them when it's wet or in light  snow.  It's not easy buying shoes online, but these are a hit.

Bass does typically run a bit narrow.  I ordered up a 1/2 size, because I knew I'd want to wear real socks with the boots when the weather turns cold.  I can still wear them with thinner nylons.

The only disappointment:  they are made in China.  Bass used to be made here.  Sigh.

Really like the style of this shoe.  Bought it in two colors.  Very comfortable once you get the correct size.  My foot size is a 6, but I always wear a 6.5 to compensate for the painful bunion on my left foot.  This shoe however, runs very small.  I ended up exchanging them for a size 7.  Now they fit perfect and are extremely comfortable and very stylish.
All I can say is AWESOME!  I ordered these shoes for my wedding in November.  They are perfect, arrived quickly.
Really comfortable.  Leather is gorgeous.  Very soft and supple.  Super cute!  Thinking of getting them in tan as well.  Definitely recommend.

I ordered my usual size, 11W. The first time I tried them on, they felt a too snug. Their definition of "wide" isn't very comfortable. I loosened the laces and adjusted the width that way and that improved the fit. I am planning on re-lacing the shoes with some longer string so I can widen them a bit more.

I also have a high instep, so the shoes felt a bit cramped, especially across the base of my toes and over the top of my foot. Loosening the laces helped with this. I also removed the insole and replaced it with a much thinner one and that definitely increased the depth of the shoe and the comfort level. (This is not really a criticism as I expected this. I usually have to remove the insoles of most shoes I buy and replace them with a thinner one.)

After the minor "adjustments" I made, I am very happy with how the boot fits. It looks amazing with a skirt or skinny jeans.

Bottom line: If you have wide feet or a high instep, you may have to make some adjustments in order to get this shoe to fit.
summary: Runs a bit narrow, but great overal

Shouldn't they be 100% waterproof, especially out of the box??  Undecided about returning these, since they are better than the alternative.  Would give them 5 stars if it weren't for damp feet!

Update: Feeling disappointed, I finally returned the shoes to Merrell in April because they weren't waterproof. My feet stayed dry, and so much lighter than with other waterproof trail shoes which can be so clunky. Past experience tells me Gore-Tex doesn't last forever so I hope Merrell keeps making these forever!
A nice comfortable walking shoe

I have to say I was skeptical that these shoes would be comfortable running on the trail - there's not much to them.  And, I doubted they'd really be waterproof.  But, they were super comfortable to run in and they shed water really well when they were new.  I could walk right through shallow water and my feet stayed dry.  LOVE.

They lose a point because they weren't especially durable.  I run in them about twice a week on forest floor terrain, but I expected them to last more than a few months.  But, after only a few months they were worn through and no longer waterproof and no longer very good as shoes (falling to pieces, literally).

It's not worth a point, but I will also note that I hate this color with a pink hot passion - the shoes are ugly.  And, the women's gore-tex ascends only came in this one horrid color (which they dare call "black").  I wore these shoes way longer than I should have because I was hoping to hold out until the new colors came out.  But, I couldn't wait that long.  The shoes were shredded.  So, now I have a second pair of these ugly shoes in the same nauseating color.

But, that's probably a testament to how much I love wearing them.  I just hate that I have to spend so much time staring at my feet in them - if I don't, I tend to fall over vines and roots.

No arch-support, so NOT worth the price..
so we take off the 3rd star, leaving 2.

Update- 3months later Review:
~These shoes took about 2 weeks of short time uses, periodically, just to loosen up enough to be comfortable to wear.. but quite honestly, I wouldn't have made the effort to break them in if it weren't for wanting to get the most out of my purchase..
So after about a month of owning these shoes, I was finally able to wear these shoes out of the house without fear of needing to remove them due to their plastic material..
Here's what happened after my first full day of wearing these "Cinderella slippers" .. I was complimented on them a few times, they have an attraction that gives a very pretty image..
After walking for about 3 hours I felt my feet sweat .. which is not normal, seeing as I work in an A/C office and do not have this issue with my heels.... I found myself having to wipe down the inside of these shoes every couple of hours, just to wear them for the rest of my shift.. but other than that, completely comfortable and cute.

These shoes did lose their shape after I wore them to work for 3 days, and I no longer wear them to work for that reason, they have been downgraded to house shoes, which I only wear short periods of time due to their strange sweat causing lining.. I do not wear these to go out.. I will say they have lasted this long due to not being worn regularly and they may not be around next month because the temperatures will not permit it. Happy shopping, everyone!

reviewText: You guys. These boots. Are my new life. The picture can't do them justice. Just incredible to behold. The spikes on the heel make them unbelievably edgy. I'm a normal Women's 12 so I sized up like everyone suggested and I am so glad I did; I have much more room in the toe box with the 13 so I'm betting that will give me longer wear-time. Also, I'm 6'1" and 260 lbs, so I was worried the boot would be too narrow in the calf. I was wrong. After lacing them up and buckling them to the right fit, the top of the shaft fits beautifully around even the biggest part of my calf, which is 17.5" . Don't worry about loosening the laces as much as you need. There's no running out of lace...it's EXTRA long. TRUST ME. Also, the buckles have plenty of holes to be adjusted, and there is extra room on the end of the flaps if you needed to poke an extra hole...or three. The quality of the boot is pleasantly shocking. Excellent quality. Nice leather, not thin. Good, solid zipper. The steel heel is completely strong and I feel very secure walking in them - no wobbliness. Very heavy (but probably just because I bought a size 13 as opposed to an 8, obviously...) I have never purchased anything like this in my life. I'm not exactly the girl who perused Hot Topic growing up, but these are just a little something I got for myself and MAN am I impressed. I laced them up and stood in front of the mirror and it LITERALLY took my breath away. I cannot WAIT to surprise the boyfriend with these tonight!!!!

reviewText: I bought one of these as a replacement wallet to the one I had since it was falling apart. It's a good size and has a good ratio of pickets to overall size. It is advertised as an rfid blocking wallet which it does not do. I have an Nfc 2fa authentication key that sits in my wallet and is easily read. Aside from that I have an rfid master access card which gets read no problem by any readers I try. 2 stars for being a good wallet. 3 stars off for the false advertising/non function.

Good, sturdy leather. Plenty of card storage options, although not as slim as I hoped, it being advertised as "slimfold." I moved up from a bifold, but moving all cards to this wallet makes for uncomfortable for back pocket storage, whereas I had no issue before. Takes a while before it breaks in and lays flat.

If you are like me then you have the perfect wallet in your pocket right now, only its nearly worn out.  Every time I see a wallet display I look at all the choices and there is nothing that is like the one I have.  My current wallet is a Columbia that is at least 10 years old.  This Columbia model is as close to it as I could find.  Now let me tell you what I do not like about this wallet.  First off there is a decorative Columbia patch on the outside that will catch on your pocket and will be the first part to wear off.  Second the wallet is NOT all leather.  Only the cover is leather, the inside is man made materials and feels cheap.  The design of the pockets looks good to me but the reality of this design is that your cards on either side are going to rub against each other resulting in an uneven thickness and unnecessary wear on your cards and the wallet.  Not sure how synthetic materials hold over the life of the wallet. I think I could have overlooked these  issues but for the fact that the card pockets vary in depth.  Cards in the pockets need be evenly showing to pull out easily.  The center an top pockets on the left are too deep so the cards get lost.  Bottom cards stick out too much.  This one is going back, I will have to stick with tried and true and continue to search for my perfect wallet.

The claims of RFID blocking wallets are ridiculous these days, as you just don't need one, but everyone insists on marketing theirs RFID blocking.  To test these claims I use my ADT security door badge that uses RFID in various points inside the wallet to see if the wallet is capable of preventing it from being read, and they all fail.  I can still use my badge to get to work, so it is not blocking a significant amount of RFID.  Since this advertises RFID blocking, but is not successful at it, I deduct a star.

The wallet is a nice leather without any strong smells.  I like the insert as it is not removable (not going to fall out), and the drivers license is easy to remove so if you get carded and they make you remove it you don't have to fight with your wallet for 30 seconds.  There are room for 11 cards, but if all are used the wallet might get thicker than you car for.  I prefer bifolds because they don't bend up the bills so much, and this one is nice and slender and easy to slip into a pocket.

The color is nice and hasn't bled yet, and the stitching has held up well.  I would give it 5 stars if it weren't for the misleading claims about RFID blocking, which I don't even think they need to add.  Most modern cards don't even have RFID chips, they use the physical contact chips, so the feature of RFID blocking is 100% useless (even if it worked).
summary: Not RFID blocking, but nice bifold

The wallet also has a slot in the back for cash that is too shallow if you have more than a few bills. It was hard to get cash in and out without everything wanting to bunch up or come with it. Overall I won't be using the wallet as it is uncomfortable to have in my back pocket when sitting at a desk a lot. I am going to stick with my Big Skinny Men's Slimline Leather Bi-Fold Slim Wallet because it is so much more functional and easy to carry around.

reviewText:
The fact that it has some sort of blocking technology would make you think that you would feel a little stiffness or that the material would be more solid than ordinary leather (or semi-leather) wallets. Considering how one way of blocking RFID intrusion is to wrap your credit cards in aluminum foil, I was expecting something detectable. That isn't true: it feels just as you would expect an ordinary wallet to feel.

The material is 25% leather and 75% other materials. It is non-shiny black and has an applied leathery-look texture that is fairly realistic. If I were to nitpick a bit, I would have preferred that it had a little bit of a gloss. I find it too flat looking. My husband, on the other hand, says he prefers it this way because it doesn't look brand new. Go figure. "Brand new" is a positive for me.

It is nicely finished and carefully stitched. The card capacity is ample and the wallet design is efficient. Even though it is slightly thicker than my husband's old wallet, it still slips in and out of his back jeans pocket more or less easily. (I put that qualifier in because he tends to fill it up with receipts and, when it gets full it's harder to shut and pocket. When it's only cards and ID's it's no problem).

One always hates the moment one has to switch wallets since the old model has been a companion of long standing and getting used to another model is always annoying. Men, in particular, have a harder time with shoes and wallets than women do but, I have to say, I've heard few complaints with this switch than with others.
summary: Comfortable design and good build and finish.

reviewText: My husband has been using this wallet for a couple of weeks now. He went from a traditional, slightly larger one to this nice, slim one. It holds all of his cards easily. It doesn't have any room or space for photos, but realistically, my husband commented that he likes the slimmer style better. Plus, he doesn't usually peruse through his photos anyway. The RFID feature is a nice touch. We were on vacation this past week and my husband kept his hotel card key in one of the outer pockets. The key was one that you just have to hold up to the lock, you don't have to insert it, so he liked being able to do that without removing the card from the wallet. The wallet looks nice and is constructed well.

Perfect for gift giving. This nice soft leather bi-fold wallet from Columbia has tons of storage for credit cards and a nice plaid interior for cash. Hidden behind the liner is the RFID blocking device. It is almost imperceptible and adds no weight to the wallet. This wallet comes in a nice gift tin perfect for gift giving. I surprised my husband with his for Father's Day! He immediately removed all his stuff from his tri-fold wallet and everything fit in the bi-fold very handily. Note: Columbia states: Cards that are surrounded by the inner fabric liner only when wallet is closed. (Protection)
My husband did not place any cards in the outside pockets. He stated he probably would not have regardless.
He is very pleased with this wallet and I recommend.

This is a very well-designed and well-made bifold wallet, with plentiful slots for credit cards and such.  There's one cash compartment, otherwise it's all card slots.  The inside flap has an id window on one side, and 3 card slots on the other, and a pocket under as well.  There are another 6 card slots on the outside flaps, with pockets under each.  So more than enough for all those cards one has to carry these days, I think.

I found the leather soft and pliable, the whole thing comfortable to tuck into a pocket.  The stitching appears to be good, similar to wallets I've been able to use for years without trouble.

One note however: if you're paying extra for RFID blocking, do make sure you need it.  Most of the new credit cards with the chips (EMV cards) don't use NFC/RFID, that's why they have to be inserted to be read.  Look at your card and/or ask your credit card provider.  (I have no way to test the RFID blocking, so have no comments on its efficacy.)

The Columbia Slimfold Wallet has some attractive features.  There are six slots for cards and small photos in addition to a plastic-covered sleeve in the center that can hold a driver's license as well as another form of ID. This good-looking wallet has room than most.  However, the RFID blocking is not a strong selling point for the average user. I am particularly concerned that the wallet is made of only 25% leather, and the exact composition of the remaining materials is not specified. Wallets must stand up to a great deal of wear and will deteriorate quickly if they are not sturdily constructed.  Only time will tell if this one holds up under daily use.

Second, the RFID blocking feature is essentially useless, because none of my credit cards use RFID, and we do not carry any debit cards (some still use RFID, but I believe those are going away).  Furthermore, credit cards are moving away from RFID.  Third, the center portion, which includes a clear plastic window on each side, is not removable.  So, when the plastic window deteriorates, cracks, or breaks, this wallet is not repairable.

On the plus side, this wallet holds a minimum of 8 credit and identification cards, with many more possible because each of the side pockets will hold more than one credit card.  There is also a pocket behind one of the side panels for holding credit/identification cards that will hold more cards.  Also, this black wallet is attractive.

From my perspective, the pluses do not outweigh the minuses.  I like the way the wallet looks.  I like that it holds a lot of cards.  I do not like that there is traditional place to hold pictures, and the RFID feature is useless for me.  If this wallet was in a store on a shelf, I would pass it by in favor of another design.  Even so, if a user does not carry pictures, and still uses cards with RFID, this wallet might be a good choice for that person.

Enjoy!

reviewText:
I like the slim profile of this wallet, and the flexibility it has to conform to the male body part it usually is carried next to. Not an unimportant thing, for if a wallet doesn't sit right in the back pocket, it can be quite uncomfortable and in extreme cases can cause back pain.

With 9 card slots and one with a clear window for a driver's license, This wallet was made for men who carry a lot of cards.

A layer of RFID blocking material is added to the wallet, ostensibly to prevent credits cards from being read at a distance and hacked. The validity of RFID blocking items is an issue of great differences of opinion. I suppose it doesn't hurt, but I don't know if it is really necessary. I have no idea what impact adding RFID blocking has on the price of this wallet, but at under $25, it's a decent enough price.

The leather on this wallet is muted and really nice looking.  This is a pretty standard style wallet.  It is narrow, but wide enough for dollar bills.  There is a pretty usual flap in the middle for picture identifications that are easier to get out of the wallet.

The case makes a nice looking gift package.

Now about the RFID.  I spent a few minutes on google and checked a couple of wallets to discover this:
This wallet says it has RFID protection. I am not sure that RFID protection is even necessary. Most credit cards don't transmit information. The only credit cards that have RFID technology are cards that can be held up without being swiped or without being absorbed by the little square end. (I despise those for being so slow!) The little metallic square is not RFID either. That is why it has to hold the card for so long.

The other thing, other than someone standing on a corner and waiting for you to walk by, is that most people who are going to steal your information are just going to do son online! I was once called and asked if I were in London. Uhm, no. And flipping A if someone was using my credit card in London, it better be me. Ironically the card was used on a Black Friday when I had done all of my shopping in ONE day in a few hours. And it was cancelled that day so every single purchase was declined. Thank goodness for Amazon that honored every single sale and sale price and let me repurchase everything on Monday when I found out what had happened.

Anyway? RFID cards? None of mine are. None of my husband's are. None of my mom's are. (I looked. She still doesn't know why I went through her purse.) Look. It is really easy to look. See if any of your credit cards have the little oval with the waves that are like wifi signals. If they don't, you don't need RFID protection. And you would know because you would have had to sign up for it.

Received this wallet today. Looks good with plenty of slots for credit cards or your library card. Whatever you need. I don't know or understand what they did to make it 'RFID blocking', but I can only assume that it will work. It came in a very nice metal blue case with Columbia printed in white. Once you remove the wallet, you can use the case in whatever way you like or give to your kids as a treasure box. But the box does make it more special for gift giving.

This is a nice looking wallet that doesn't obviously look like an RFID wallet.

I don't know what it means that it's "25% leather"; I think the leather is quite thin and bonded to other materials. Also, many of the interior pieces (not immediately visible) are fabric, not leather. Overall, it feels a bit plastic-y, but that's true for a lot of leathers that have been heavily treated.

I had thought the interior extra flap might be removable for those who preferred to carry fewer cards and have less bulk, but it's stitched in. So this is really for someone who carries a lot of cards... and then, subsequently, protects them.

The RFID layer is sandwiched between the outer layer of leather and the outside side of the large bill pocket.

I like the outer quick-access pocket; that's a nice touch.

The wallet comes in a tin box with a clear plastic lid; it turns out that there's a tin lid for the box on the bottom. Somehow, the box is an extra perk that I appreciate. Ah, you can't see the box. It's bright blue, with the Columbia logo.

Overall, this is a good wallet for the price.
summary: Nice RFID wallet; slightly plastic-y feel

I generally review entertainment products on Amazon but when Amazon offered this product in exchange for an objective review as part of its Vine Reviewer program (where they send the products to selected reviewers), I requested one since I do use a wallet and do carry credit cards.

My go to wallet is a Buxton which holds 8 credit cards and has a clear window for your drivers license. It comes with a removable insert to add extra cards. I always remove the insert. I want to keep wallet as thin as possible so that it doesnt stretch my rear pants pocket or tear it.

This wallet is not thin it was slots for six credit cards and a double-sided leather insert with two plastic windows  for your license or photo id cards. The issue for me is that the center insert is NOT removable.

The outside of this black leather wallet nice, except that it has a raised piece of leather on the front with the Columbia brand name.  There is a white tag inside that says it is Made in China (the package says handcrafted construction) but I could not find anywhere the info on what type of leather it is. The word leather is nowhere on the package.

It does say that it has a RFID Shield to protect credit card data from being stolen. But, I want to remind folks that nearly EVERY credit card comes with automatic fraud protection (free) so that if you should have charges which are not yours over $50, the credit card company cannot hold you responsible. And, remember that in most restaurants you actually give your card to a wait staff person who goes away with it and brings it back.
Also, in summary, I would not purchase this just because of the shield. And if you need a THIN wallet, Id look at models with removable center card insert.  You can see both the center insert as well as the outside logo in the photos here on Amazon.
But, its not a cheap looking item.

Also, for what its worth it come packed in metal tin that weighs in at 4 oz (and youll probably not need); the wallet (empty) weighs just 2 ounces.

I hope you found this review both informative and helpful.

Steve Ramm

This belt solves what I don't like about regular belts: bulgy buckles and hard leather that dig into your sides when you move. It looks far more classy than other elastic belts with its nice metallic connector, is comfortable to wear and easy to use. It's not quite as easy to thread/unthread through belt loops as a stiff leather belt, but I'd rather take a couple extra seconds to thread the belt and be comfortable all day.

The "buckle" is easy to use. A person does still need enough two-handed coordination to pull the "buckle" together against the strength of the elastic, but the two halves just grab each other like a hook and fall into place so it doesn't require much fine motor coordination. Opening definitely requires less finger strength than would be needed for a snap-fit buckle or side-release buckle that require squeezing to release. I don't think it would be easy to close for individuals who need one-handed operation (unless it's worn for fashion rather than function of keeping your pants up!), though.

(My irritating experience on the top - detailed pros/cons on the bottom)

I was extremely excited to receive my two tanks in the mail today. They were stacked so cutely in the box, and wrapped with purple tissue paper. It felt more like boutique shopping than just plain old Amazon. Imagine my dismay when, as I put the first one on, anywhere the fabric stretched or folded along the bias, those places turned light grey - almost like the elastic was worn out, old, or damaged. This is a skintight workout tank - it bunches and stretches as you work it over your head - that is inevitable. I took the tank top to the sink hoping that the marks were dry skin, or lotion from earlier in the day, or dust on the tank from storage - I tried rinsing some of it out with water - no luck. Grabbed the Woolite and worked a bit in an out - no luck. I'm not exactly a vain gal, but I have too much pride to wear a top that looks like I'm busting out of it so bad that I tore the elastic.

So I grabbed the papers in the box and called Bare Necessities. The SECOND I said I had ordered from Amazon, the representative said she could not help me and hung up on me without even waiting for a reply. Very rude, even if she couldn't do anything for me. Imagine my disgust when I check the return policy for damaged items from Bare Necessities (says they will pay for return shipping and replacement item shipping) and find a button that leads me to contact the seller, but doesn't actually put me in touch with them, and furthermore, gives me a label where I am expected to pay insured, tracked, return shipping... No bueno.

I'm hoping that Amazon customer service can straighten this out.

On the plus side : It is super comfortable when on. I know from my sink-washes that the fabric dries out really fast. The straps are nice and wide, and padded. The colors in the stripes are more in the vibe of the early 90's - lots of little neon squares, instead of the flowing color change the picture looks like. The band on the built in bra is nice and sturdy, and has very, very little stretch. (I'm usually comfy in a Freya 30FF or G - I am using a 2 inch extender to go from can't-breathe to comfy on it right now.) Most of the underwire is really wide and well cushioned. The fabric in the armpits came up high enough that nothing is going to be working its way out, but it doesn't bind up into the crease of my arm either. Happily, it doesn't roll up at the bottom, but it does creep up easily. I have a hard time imagining a woman on whom this tank would "drape" like the description suggests - it fits more like spanx. But, the stripes are very slenderizing, and give an hourglass effect.

On the minus side: The underwire at the very end of the pits has the potential to get poky. If I keep this tank, I'll probably stitch a bit of felt or moleskine over them so I don't wind up with a sore spot a few months down the road and 20 miles up the trail. THE BAND HAS NO STRETCH WHATSOEVER. I agree with an earlier reviewer, in that it is shorter than I would like by a couple of inches, and because of that, when it creeps up, it makes me look stubby.

Also good to know - while the inner band SAYS the exact bra size, my 30G has a hangtag on it that says "D-H Cup Size." I don't know about anyone else, but I don't consider D-H to be interchangeable sizes. In my opinion, it is certainly sized more to the H than the D, and with the cups being structured, it's quite roomy and breezy in there. Additionally, unless I am engaging in perfect, shoulders-back posture, the one-size-fits-most cup gapes forward at the fabric above the gore because of the stiff structure. Fortunately, all that airspace doesn't seem to collapse the cups, so I actually look a little more well endowed than I deserve credit for. (Hot dates from the gym, anyone?!?!) I haven't decided if it feels like cheating, or if I should just shove my keys and phone in there like I usually do and be happy about it.
summary: Very mixed feelings... Quirky fit, Hang tag states "D-H Cup Size," no stretch in band, problems with fabric on first try-on

This is a nice looking watch. I love automatic watches, and I already have a different Stuhrling Original automatic watch in a different style. When I received this watch I realized that it had a functionality problem. It seemed to be losing time. I decided to test it against my other watch. I put both watches on, wound the crown a few times, and then wore them both for 2 hours. After 2 hours I removed them and just let them sit on the table to see how long they would run. The new watch had stopped within 2 hours. The older watch kept going for 11 hours! This might not sound like a big deal, but I had noticed the watch losing time even before I tested it. I decided to return and replace the watch and see if another one would do this as well. Same test performed on the replacement watch, and it ran for 5 hours. I decided that was acceptable, but then when taking the watch off one of the leather loops that holds the band in place broke. So frustrating because I do like the look of this watch. I am going to try a third time. Hopefully this one will work out better.

Two more notes on the looks:
  The actual color is slightly closer to yellow gold than it is depicted in this image on amazon. (Still looks nice though) Go to Stuhrling website for a more accurate depiction.
  The 4 in roman numerals is shown as IIII on the watch face. Not as IV like it should be. Not that noticeable really, but still an issue.

All in all a nice looking watch for a decent price, but has quite a few faults as well.

reviewText:
I NEVER have anything to wear!! Well, at least in my head, not in my closet. With 35 different colors, this maxi dress is great on those such occasions, or when I'm out and about or just at the beach. My daughter and I wear sundresses over our swimsuits, so this is perfect.

I'm about 5'2 and the dress length stops at the top of my foot. It's 92% (itchy and heavy) Polyester and 8% Spandex. The plunging bust is fitted, but you can easily wear a camisole or halter top under it. This dress is sleeveless, but covers the shoulders well. The fit is similar to a dress slip. I personally love it. For a "tighter" fit, order a size or 2 smaller. Remember, this is loose fitting, so if you take it down 2 sizes, I think it'll be more of a true fit than anything. The company does offer free returns/exchanges on most colors and sizes, so you'll be able to find the right fit.

I recently wore this with flip flops (a South Texas must have), but it can be paired with wedges or stilettos. The beauty of this dress is that you can go casual or fancy with accessories. With the low price, I'll definitely be ordering other styles in the future.

This dress is very comfortable. It looks just like the picture on Amazon. I bought the pink and black chevron dress in a large. I am 5'5, 160 pounds, and I usually wear a large. I would say this dress fits a little big. I think I could have worn a medium, but it would have been more form-fitting. I prefer the looser fit. There is some room in the stomach area, plus it's stretchy, so I could see this being worn as a maternity dress. I like that it covers my stomach chub, lol. The bust area hangs a bit loose on me. I wear a smaller C cup, for reference. I will probably have to pin the bottom of the bust so I don't flash everyone, lol. The fabric is light, breathable, and on the thin side, but isn't see-through. I could easily wear this dress all day long. The fabric is stretchy to where movement isn't restricted too much. The dress doesn't hang down quite as much as I would prefer. It's a few inches above the ground. Girls taller than me might want to keep that in mind, because it might hang too high on them.

The dress is made in China, FYI. The fabric is 92% polyester and 8% spandex. Polyester supposedly never fades, so that's a plus. The only fitted part on me is right under the bust where there is an elastic waistband. The colors are really nice and look just like the picture. I'm not sure how long this dress will last. I noticed some of the stitching at the bottom already coming loose. For that, I will knock it down a star. The chevron pattern doesn't match up on the side, so that's a little weird, too. But I really do like the dress for casual wear. It is extremely comfortable and easy to move around in. I am happy overall, I just hope it lasts. reviewText:
This is a beautiful coat.  The dark wool/cashmere is very soft to the touch.  It is a longer coat that goes down to around your mid-thigh.

The material is nice and warm for those brisk autumn and winter days.  It has buttons to close and/or a zipper.  Lining consists of high quality fabric as you might expect for a coat of this price.

This is now my favorite coat to wear around town.  Highly recommended!

Classic coat with a simple cut. Immediately my favorite feature was that this does not feel like a typical wool blend coat. The cashmere makes it feel much softer than a wool blend. The pockets are ample and each side pocket has two entrances. The inside bib, although not removable, has a very sturdy zipper and will not let the wind creep in. It's perfect for a dressy or a casual night. Sleeve length was right on. THere's plenty of room for a suit coat or a sweatshirt or hoodie underneath without looking too baggy. The neck, when zipped up fully, is just the right amount of snug to keep out the chill without feeling too constricted. I'm super-happy with this coat.

As a tall guy (6'5", 220lbs athletic) it's always hard to tell how these things will fit. Most are way to short in the waist and the arms.
This is just a tiny bit tight in the shoulders and back, but it's only noticeable when I'm driving. Which is a bummer since this is a "car coat" so you'd assume that's where it would provide some play, but it's really not bad.

Aside from that it looks amazing. It's a nice fit, not too slim, not too baggy.
It's warm, I wouldn't wear it in really cold weather but unlike my last car coat I can wear it in cool weather without sweating to death.
It zips up pretty high on the neck and the collar snaps closed around the neck as well to cover up pretty thoroughly.
I really like bibbed coats for reasons like this.

So gripes.
Well if you want to use the pockets you'll need a seam ripper or a tailor to prep the coat because both of the side pockets are sewn shut for some reason. You'll also need the seam ripper to remove the "Fabrique made in Italy" tag that is sewn to the sleeve. But you'll only need scissors to remove the plastic tag on the collar that reads "Fabric from China".
It was that last tag that threw me a bit. Yes some of the fabric is from China, some of it is from Italy.
The coat is only 10% Cashmere as well. But that's not a big deal because it's mostly wool, which keeps it warm, and the cashmere blend makes it soft. Still, advertised as a cashmere coat when it's mostly might throw some people off.

Overall, this might be my favorite coat ever.
I'm serious.
I just feel great in it and I've already gotten several comments.
I wish it had more play in the shoulders so I could be more comfortable while driving but that's not enough to make me want to stop wearing it.
summary: Great looking coat. Soft, warm seems to be decent quality.

reviewText:

This is a beautiful coat.  The fabric is just gorgeous.  I was really impressed by the quality of the wool and a little curious as most wool is itchy to me even if the quality is good.  This wool coat has 70% wool, 10% recycled cashmere, and 20% nylon. That is probably what smooths the coat out and makes it feel so soft and pleasant.

The lines are really pleasant on this coat.  This looks especially nice on a tall lanky young man.  Ours is 6'4" now but still weighs about 150.  I usually select small items for him but he likes to have more room in coats and tends to wear layers.  This coat has an especially nice look on such a tall boy, I mean young man.

reviewText:
My boots were delivered yesterday, and I love them! They are true to the picture, and the cognac colour is as shown. I'm 5'1" and the boots come just under my knee. The zipper on the back seems to work smoothly and the buckles are well attached. The quality of the material seems good right off the bat - but I don't plan to wear these once it starts to snow heavily, since they likely wouldn't stand up well to salt. The widest part of my calf is about 13", and there's room for me to tuck in pants/jeans and knee high socks. With the lovely Canadian weather, I tend to wear out a pair of riding boots every year - so for the price, these are absolutely perfect.

A few things to keep in mind about these boots:
- The sole does scuff fairly easily. I tend to hit my other foot a lot when walking, so the sole does mark up the foot of the boot. It was fairly easy to clean this off with a cloth.
- The zipper doesn't go all the way down to the bottom of the heel, so sliding your foot in will require a bit of a tug. I don't see this as a problem, since it will keep the heel from deteriorating quickly. I've had other boots where the zipper went down all the way to the bottom, and they only lasted about a month before the zipper started to split.
- Despite other reviews saying these ran small, I went out on a limb and ordered my usual size which is a 7 (I'd say I'm on the smaller side of a 7, and can sometimes wear a 6.5). If I'm wearing thin socks my foot slides around a bit. With thick socks, they'll be perfectly. The back of the boot doesn't rub against my heel, so it's fairly safe to say that I will be avoiding any dreaded blisters.

As a guy who normally wears 32 waist normally, and 33 in my favorite Levis I read the reviews and went up a few sizes to a 34. I could barely get these suckers buttoned and when I did these was absolutely no room to even tuck in a shirt. If I put my hands in the pockets I could see the bones in my fingers clearly through the fabric. After this strange experience I put on my other pair of 34 dickies khakis and for me they were too big, even a little baggy. So the size is definitely an issue. About an hour of casual city walking the button broke which was almost a relief because then the tightness was not as extreme. The other issue is the fabric is not very flexible so if are climbing stairs or bending over to pick something up prepare to do some awkward positions in these pants.

On a positive note, the fabric does seem quite durable and they look as advertised, and the low cost didn't set me back too much so I am not too upset. I do not plan on returning these as I think they will fit better as I lose more weight and break them in (and fix the button), but again, the size is definitely an issue and is probably 4 sizes too small.

reviewText:
I've ordered 4 pairs of these now in different colors. Was thrilled to find pants in 30 width by 31 length. I am 5' 7" at 145 lbs, athletic but not a overly muscular. These are EXACTLY the fit I was expecting. Definitely "slim", but not "skinny" -- they hug your hips/thighs without completely restricting movement -- and the length is perfectly in between pants I have at 30 and 32 lengths. If you take "leg day" seriously, you should look elsewhere. I read some other reviews that complained about the quality, i.e., torn stitching, but these look really great to me so far without having worn them a bunch of times.

One thing that is definitely worth noting: the pockets--both front and back--are surprisingly deep. At first I thought this was great, but then I walked 4 miles in them. I kept a large phone (Galaxy Note 3) in my left back pocket, and my wallet in the other. Both actually started hurting my butt in a way I was not expecting, due to how far down the objects sit on my rear. I kept having to pull the objects back up out of the pocket a bit to get them to rest properly on my body. Of course they would inevitably fall all the way back in, but it was temporary relief. For me this is definitely worth detracting a star. I like these pants so much, I might even take it upon myself to sew the pockets to a shorter depth. This fixed, I feel these pants will become some of my go-to pants.
