These pants were returned.  Too tiny; and obviously made in the orient for men born there. I had a terrible time getting them off, never mind getting them over my heel.  And I'm a little guy of 5'4 and weigh 105. Historically oriental males are small in stature with thin bone structure.

I'll start by saying that I'm a dancer and a cyclist (5'8", 159 lbs, mesomorph downstairs, ectomorph upstairs) and I have some seriously muscular hindquarters, so I ordered these pants largely *because* of all the reviews that mentioned that these pants are cut loose in the caboose.  That was, for me, a strong selling point.

Turns out they're actually a little looser in the caboose even than I need -- but the fit through the calves and thighs (again, pretty muscular, here) is perfect.  Clean and straight without looking indecently tight.  This can be a real challenge when shopping for nicer trousers for legs like mine.

Based on the recommendations of a previous reviewer, I also ordered a size larger than I would normally wear (a 34x31 when I'd normally choose a 32x31).  I think I probably could have stuck with the 32 -- there's a lot of room at the waist.  Nothing a belt can't handle until I get these tailored, but something to keep in mind when you order.

Length is about perfect for me (to offer an idea: a standard 30 inseam is always short for me; a 32 is sometimes just a hair too long).

The waist is, indeed, quite a bit higher than it looks in the pictures here.  While high-waisted trousers aren't my very favorite, I'm all right with these.  The waist on mine sits just below my navel, so it's not high enough to be obnoxious.  Paired with a sharp vest , the higher waist makes for a smooth, classic silhouette, which is nice when you want to look sharp.

If you're looking for grey trousers, by the way, it turns out that "Army Grey" has a lot of brown in it -- it looks very brown, indeed, when paired with a black jacket, for example.  I actually like the color (in fact, I just ordered a second pair), but that's also something to keep in mind.

Pros:
+Nice fabric
+Solid construction
+Great price on Army Grey
+Fit that works for guys with muscular thighs and butts

Cons:
-Highish waist may not appeal to some wearers
-"Army Grey" isn't really grey

Overall: recommend for guys who don't skip "leg day."

Very nice set of keys! I really like the set as a whole but it does have its problems:

Pros:
Nice box -- Mine came with the box in pristine condition. The inside padding was very warped but it's nothing big as the keys weren't damaged.
Great size -- The keys are about 3" long and each are very nice to hold, fit great on a key chain (like for your car keys), and even on the provided necklaces.
Nice keys -- All 12 zodiac keys are present, along with 5 silver keys, 2 FT logos, 3 other golden keys (which I will talk about later), the Dragon Chain Cannon Key, Grey's pendant, the clock hand, and a bunch of jewelry-accessories.

CONS:
Paint apps -- Most paint apps are spot on, but a lot of them have runover or are completely absent, in the case of Gemini and Scorpio. Nothing that can't be fixed with some of your own paint but I would rather prefer them be painted.
Unidentified keys -- There are 3 keys which I have no idea what they are and haven't been able to find what they are. Two have the Libra and Pisces symbols on them and look completely different than the actual counterparts. (Maybe they change shape when Lucy acquires them), and the third key looks like a slightly larger variant of Aries with a hollow portion in the handle. This isn't Capricorn, so I wonder what exactly it is. I would have rather the money for these keys go to paint apps or at least come with a list of all of the keys provided.
Key ring -- Mine came with only 10 rings for the keys. Luckily, I found and ordered an identical key ring (link at the bottom if you wish to look) to add to my ring set. There should be at least 12, if not enough for all of the keys.
Mini chain links -- My set came with a bag full of chain links that were very hard to put on the keys without a set of pliers due to their sheer size. I liked that they were included, but they were a bit troublesome.

reviewText:
WARNING:

This item is a bootleg (unofficially licensed product).  The company that owns the licensed of Fairy Tail and those for making merchandise did not make these. There are only 8 officially licensed keys made by a company called GE ( Great Eastern ).

Please do not buy these, it only encourages them to make more crappy unofficial items that rip people off.

I was so excited to see them come in the mail! It took about 10 days to deliver, and I was expecting a couple of months .
It's a great product, but there are a few mistakes. The painting on the keys were quite off(Virgo, Aquarius. & Cancer), & nearly all of the colors were incorrect. Even a couple of the keys weren't even painted over. (Scorpio & Gemini) There's also two keys that don't look at all familiar.

I like having Gray's necklace, & two different colors of the Fairy Tail guild symbol to wear as a charm. Other than the mistakes that have been pointed out, it's great & I'm most definitely going to use it for my Halloween costume as Lucy ! :)

The product came in a week early. The outside packaging was good and it came from China. The keys themselves are really good quality and out of all the key collections on Amazon this one  has a bit more then the other ones. The only concern I had was that the box it came in was bent and one of the sides was torn, the box itself also felt a bit oily. However the keys are really good and they are about the size of my finger. Really great purchase and quality for a decent price.
I absolutely love these keys. I'm adding each key to the chain each time Lucy gets a new key. It's so exciting.

I really, really like these keys! My mother got me this for Christmas, and although I don't wear the actual keys often, I will if I get the chance.
They are about 3.5 inches in length, shiny, and look pretty much exactly like the keys from the anime. Well, minus the two arc-related ones (the dragon one from edolas and the infinity clock one aren't celestial keys and neither is the little cross one)
But it's nice they were included, anyway.

The keys are made of real metal, and are not fragile. I am going to warn cosplayers, they are quite heavy, so you may want to avoid wearing them all at once.
The key ring confused me at first, but if you have a clamp then you can actually put all of the keys onto the key ring, or if you want, even as a pendant for a necklace.
It includes all 12 zodiac keys, and then a couple I can't quite identify, as I haven't exactly finished the series yet.

The box is kinda nice... I'm not going to go into detail on it....

There are two necklaces; the blue pendant and the red pendant. They are metal, shiny, and well-detailed in terms of shape, also notably larger than the necklace that you'll find by itself on here.
I recommend not using the wire for a chain, though. Find a different one (which, if you're like me and fancy wearing necklaces, shouldn't be hard).

I wear this red necklace in the shower, and to bed, and it's still just as it was when I got it a month ago. I wear it every day and every day I meet new fairy tail fans.

If you like - no, if you LOVE fairy tail, get this, not just for all the keys, but for the necklace, too.
You won't be disappointed!

UPDATE: THIS SET DOES NOT COME WITH SCORPIO KEY. There is no Scorpio Key.

Overall a very good set of keys spanning all the way into the Grand Magic Games arc and beyond. The set not only includes the Celestial Spirit keys, but also several other keys from Fairy Tail, such as the key to the Dragon Chain Cannon from the Edolas Arc. My biggest gripe with the set is that several of the keys I can't recognize from the show (they could very well be manga exclusive, I'm honestly not sure) but they leave the Zodiac Keys incomplete, leaving out Capricorn's Key. It's not like he hadn't been introduced when the set was made, seeing as Libra's and Pisces' keys are present, and they appeared quite a bit later than Capricorn, plus he's one of Lucy's premier spirits. It's not enough to ruin it for me, it's just something that kinda bugs me. I'd highly recommend this to any Fairy Tail fan who won't be overly bothered by Capricorn's absence.
summary: Very nice overall, but where is Capricorn.

reviewText:
I so love this dress!  Since I'm the first reviewer on it I'll try to be as thorough as possible.

First: I'm 5'4", 160 lbs, 38C, pant size around a 12-13, and I usually buy an XL top because I like it a little on the roomy side.  I bought this dress in XL (coral - luscious!).  I might have gotten away with a L but I didn't want to take the chance.  Well, it fit me perfectly, was not tight or constraining anywhere; and in my opinion the XL will fit a larger-bosomed gal easily, probably a XXL I'm thinking.  I took it to 93-100 degree Phoenix and it was soooo comfortable to wear; it was like wearing a cloud - the dress wafted around me, didn't cling anywhere, lots of air circulation in that heat.  It quickly became my go-to dress.

The length hit me a little below my knees.  The tube top was ample enough that I was able to snug it up under my boobs to enhance the empire styling which is really flattering.  I chose to wear the tie but certainly didn't have to as the top would have easily stayed up by itself. I loved how it just floated around me whether I was standing or walking, and I think because of this not too many extra little wobbly-bits showed.

BTW, I washed it before I wore it, cold water; it didn't bleed or become misshapen.  I line-dried it, and it help up wonderfully.  Nothing frayed, nothing warped or wrinkled, no weird things happened, just a lovely dress that stayed lovely.  It packed well and wasn't wrinkly when I hung it up. The material was soft, dreamy, and sensuous.

The quality of workmanship was fine; I didn't see any loose threads anywhere, all hems were hemmed, everything hung straight, the tie was aligned in the center.

I can't think of anything else to add right now. If I do, I'll add it.  I wouldn't hesitate to buy this.  It's comfortable, light, and cool.
Forgot to say -- it's not see-through.
UPDATE 6/8/15: I just bought this dress in the lovely green color. I'll update again soon on the first washing and how it fares. I truly don't expect anything different than what I've experienced with my dreamy coral dress. A quick try-on says it fits the same, that is, just like the coral one. And I didn't see any loose threads, hems were all intact, fabric was cut correctly and therefore displays nicely. The only hiccup is that the green color my browser showed me is a soft mint green (oh so yummy), and the actual color leans towards a soft grassy green (but it's a green without a yellow base or tone to it. The green has more of a blue base undertone.  Does that make sense?)  I was a little disappointed at first because of this; however, it's such a comfy dress I decided to love it.  I'll update if anything strange happens after washing it.
UPDATE 7/12/15: After 1st washing on the green dress, the top line of the tube-top stitching unravelled which made the tag want to flip over and outside the dress. I used my tie straps and that helped keep the tag hidden. A pleasant update note: If the dress gets wrinkled while folded up in your closet, all the wrinkles will completely disappear after only 5-10 minutes of wearing.  No ironing required (yay!)

reviewText: My daughter likes it and says it's comfortable enough. She wore this the whole day at disneyland and were fine.

First - let me say - I like this shoe.  Purchased it over a year ago at a local shoe store. I LOOOOVE Mary Janes.  For work - I love flat Mary Janes or kitten heeled Mary Janes.  For play - platformed, high-heeled Mary Janes. I love them.  Some may consider them basic - but for me - I feel like - 'if it ain't broke - don't fix it.'

The only reason I'm giving this show a low rating is because while I love the way it looks on my fat, short, stubby foot.  And it's super comfortable - the first pair I purchased locally - did NOT stain my toes with black dye. I actually loved this shoe so much that when I needed a replacement comfort Mary Jane - and no one sold it locally - I decided to do the "Monk" thing (fans of Tony Shaloub's Monk will get the reference) and order multiple pairs.  The first time I strapped on the first pair - all was fine - until I took my shoe off that first night.  My toes (both the top edge of actual toe of skin and nails) were HORRIBLY stained.  I used nail polish remover, bleach, lemon juice, pumice stones.  And even 2 weeks later - I can still see a faint black stain from the dye.

I even tried a SECOND pair - and wore tights instead of stockings - not only wore the tights ruined and stained by dye - but toes were once again stained horribly.

These shoes are cute - and comfortable. But honestly - I've worked with all sorts of clothing dyes and even wood dyes - have NEVER had this much trouble removing dye.  Not sure if this is why the only place these shoes can only be found is on Amazon or what - but what I will - say is this - when you purchase - WRAP your toes in fabric bandaids until all the excess dye has been absorbed.  Once it's been absorbed - you will be good to go - and you will love these shoes!
summary: First - let me say - I like this shoe

reviewText: So I bought these right as they came out because I love my Oakley Mars and have been having to get third party replacement nose pads and new non Oakley replacement lenses seeing as how they are 18 years old now. So imagine my excitement when I see Madmen an obvious homage to the classic Mars style. Well sadly to say the Madman was a monumental let down, after years of dependable durability form my Mars the Madman with its structural compromises only lasted a month, I had been loving how comfortable they were to wear and one day I take them out of my cargo pants leg pocket and both ear stocks had broken off at the hing. Needless to say I was not only heartbroken at the sort life of my Mars replacements but appalled at how the newest installment of what I thought of as the legendary X-Metal line up had fallen flat on its face. After decades of considering Oakley the pinnacle of industrial grade sports wear I was forced to reappraise my opinion of what I thought was hands down the best and only company to turn to for my sunglasses needs. The costumer service was fine, I sent in the broken pair and they sent me a new in box replacement. But honestly I haven't even opened them, I thought about selling them but I had no desire to burn someone else like I got burned, who knows maybe it was a fluke, maybe I got the one bad apple, but the tiny point where the hing meets the ear stock that snapped on both sides seems to me like a glaring design flaw in what is supposed to be a rough and tumble sportsman's sunglasses. This having been my 5th pair of Oakleys I for one hope this is not the beginning of a trend.
summary: Big let down for a long time Mars fan.

As one reviewer noted, these scarves are thin, but to criticize them for that is unfair. These scarves are meant to be very lightweight...just enough volume when slightly bunched to take the chill off a bare neck in spring and fall while adding a touch of color and style. I purchased two shades. The mocha brown is true in colors to the screen shot and rates five stars. The steel gray, while still attractive, is not as vibrant and variegated; the majority of the scarf is actually black with touches of several shades of gray here and there.

One important note: Should you purchase one of these scarves, do NOT try to pull off the adhesive tag, for you will damage the scarf. Instead, wet the tag from the back side of the scarf with a bit of adhesive remover or lighter fluid and rub it slightly with your finger. The tag will fall right off and you can wipe off the cleaner with plain water to remove any smell or residue. This process left no water spot or residue on either of my scarves.

reviewText: I was looking for a very thin scarf to camouflage  a surgery wound and these are perfect.  If you are looking for a warm scarf, this isn't it. I ordered 6 of these (Steel Gray, Coral, Sunset Red, Caribbean Green, Pink and Fuschia Pink) and they are all as pictured.  I had a hard time deciding between the Orange, Sunset and Coral, and I have to say that the Sunset and Coral are similar; as one might expect, one has more red, one more coral, but similar.  I plan on going back for the purple and maybe one more.  I also took other reviewers advice and dabbed a wet rag on the scarf side behind the tag, and it peeled right off.  I'm not sure why that sticker is necessary, but as a suggestion, the manufacturer should look for a different sort of tag. For the price, these can't be beat.

reviewText: This scarf was beautiful- loved the colors and light weight of the scarf.

I liked the scarf itself very much. I don't like scarves that have so much volume that they get in the way when say dining out. I loved the colors in my blue one. However there was a big tag stuck haphazardly on one end of the scarf that I felt made it unwearable. I sew and understand how to handle fabric. I tried putting the scarf in the freezer like one would try to remove chewing gum. That didn't help. Then I tried using the steam from my steam generator iron without making contact with the fabric in an attempt to get it to release. That didn't work either. So I returned the scarf as defective.

Now I am on here reading the reviews of other people and see only a few comments about this tag issue. One person used an adhesive remover but I know that some dyes are very unstable. That was confirmed by another reviewer who said hers water spotted in the rain. And yet another said they used water to remove their tag. It would be nice if the seller would address this issue with instructions on how to remove it. The fabric is too fragile to pull it off. Mine was not placed in such a way that it could be "hidden in the folds" either.

This is the first item that I have returned as defective. Customer Service suggested reordering but I haven't decided yet if I will do that or not. The over all rating on this item seems to be very good so perhaps I just got a bad one. The seller has no way of knowing because of the way they are rolled, twisted and packaged up.

I opened one up to see the scarf (and also to remove the original plastic; since it's a gift I don't like to leave something in its original packaging like that, and honestly thought there would be tags somewhere else on the inside)...but I literally ruined the packaging. reviewText:
First thing is first, the ring itself deserves the 5/5 with no questions asked. With that being said, I will provide details on both pros and cons of the ring and the packaging.

First I'd like to get the cons out of the way. There are only a few, but for someone who wants an absolutely perfect flawless item, this may be important.
The biggest con would be the packaging. As displayed in the uploaded picture, the ring came inside of a small brown box with an emblem on top. The box itself looks good, but the emblem on top was worn down like someone took sandpaper to it. For me, this isn't a huge deal, because I bought the ring for myself. If this is meant for a gift though, it looks less appealing. My second issue is debatable as to whether it's even worthy of being a con. The ring is ridiculously light. It makes sense since it's a strip of wood and the metal is lightweight, but I like a little heft to my ring that this ring didn't have. That's more of a personal problem though, so I did not count that towards the rating.

Now for the good part!
First, I'd like to state that the ring itself is very comfortable, and very slick on the inside.
Second, the wood looks fantastic. The gloss over it is just enough to give it a little magnification to make it pop out more as well.
Third, I have yet to scratch it, and I was really rough onn it already, so I feel like the material will last a good while.

In conclusion, I find the ring very stylish, elegant, and sophisticated. I woud recommend this ring to anyone who is looking for a metal and wood ring.

reviewText:
I needed a travel bag for short weekend trips. I ordered this Weekender Bag by Haular bag because it seemed like the right size and had a great look to it.
When this travel bag arrived two days later, thanks to amazon prime, I was a little taken aback by the size of the box. It was shipped shipped in a huge thin box so as to ensure the bag was not folded and retained its shape during shipping. It was also wrapped in plastic so it was really well protected.

First thing I noticed about this bag is how sturdy it was. This is definitely very sturdily made and is of good quality. The canvas material is made to last. The leather accents are just great and add to the overall look and appeal of this bag.
The zippers are also strong and work just fine. The bag comes with an optional Shoulder strap as well.
The bottom of the bag is studded (has 5 metal studs) which is good so you can put the bag down anywhere without ruining the bottom.

The bag is well made, durable, and looks very stylish. The stitching all looks well done as well. Overall I am happy with it.

I rely on amazon for reviews of nearly everything before I buy. One of the reasons I shop so much on Amazon is the amount of healthy customer feedback about the products there. I like to give back to the community by reviewing items myself. My reviews are always honest and accurate to my experience. Some items are offered to me for a discount. My opinion and review is never persuaded by this fact. I do not only review items that are sent to me at a discount either, the majority of my reviews are on items that I paid full price for. here are two main problems: the weight and the lining:
(a) Weight. This is a heavy bag, even when it's completely empty. I weighed it at ~3.25 pounds! That's a lot of extra weight to carry around. It may not seem like a big deal, but when I'm running through an airport trying to make a flight, I can feel every ounce on my shoulder. And despite the substantial weight, the canvas isn't crisp enough that the bag can stand up on its own when empty---this makes it difficult to load and unload.

(b) The lining is not secured to the walls or bottom of the bag. You can see in the photo below that the entire interior can be pulled out from the mouth of the bag. I don't know if this is an intentional design feature or not (i.e. like maybe it's helpful for shaking out the dirt and lint?) But the downside is that all that loose fabric just flops around, and can bunch up and twist around small items, making it difficult to find what you need quickly. Also, the lining is a very dark brown, which makes it even harder to find things. I wish they'd made the interior all grey at least, like the rest of the bag---it would be easier to find things fast.

On the bright side, there are nice touches everywhere: a wide mouthed zip closure, stud feet, attached keychain, and two "shoe pockets" The more organization, the better in my opinion, and this bag is a solid performer. I wish it was lighter weight, and that the lining was taut, and stitched into place--but it's still a handsome weekend carryall

With that in mind, this item was sent to me for a discount in exchange for a review. I have thoroughly tested it and my reviews are always 100% honest and are not affected by the discount given. reviewText:
I was specifically looking for a weekender bag, as opposed to an overnight bag, and this one fits the bill.  It's spacious and the unisex style is very appealing.  But while it's very attractive, there are several noteworthy drawbacks that stop it from being a five star item, and I want to be very fair about representing them.  I hate it when I buy something that has all rave reviews, only to discover that there were obvious issues that I wish someone had mentioned.

There are two main problems: the weight and the lining:
(a) Weight.  This is a heavy bag, even when it's completely empty.  I weighed it at ~3.25 pounds!  That's a lot of extra weight to carry around.  It may not seem like a big deal, but when I'm running through an airport trying to make a flight, I can feel every ounce on my shoulder.  And despite the substantial weight, the canvas isn't crisp enough that the bag can stand up on its own when empty---this makes it difficult to load and unload.

(b) The lining is not secured to the walls or bottom of the bag.  You can see in the photo below that the entire interior can be pulled out from the mouth of the bag.  I don't know if this is an intentional design feature or not (i.e. like maybe it's helpful for shaking out the dirt and lint?)  But the downside is that all that loose fabric just flops around, and can bunch up and twist around small items, making it difficult to find what you need quickly.  Also, the lining is a very dark brown, which makes it even harder to find things. I wish they'd made the interior all grey at least, like the rest of the bag---it would be easier to find things fast.

On the bright side, there are nice touches everywhere:  a wide mouthed zip closure, stud feet, attached keychain, and two "shoe pockets"  The more organization, the better in my opinion, and this bag is a solid performer.  I wish it was lighter weight,  and that the lining was taut, and stitched into place--but it's still a handsome weekend carryall, which is why I'm giving it four stars.

This is definitely a 5 star bag.  It's gorgeous to look at, and thoughtfully designed for the user--- it's an excellent piece of luggage, and it looks more expensive than it really is.  For years, I'd been using a crappy weekender tote that came free with my Victoria's Secret purchase as a carry-on bag. It was just one big empty cavern inside; there was no thoughtful organization or any feature that would make the bag more useful---I can't believe I suffered so long!  I stumbled across a lucky promotional opportunity, where I was given a sample for the purposes of a candid, independent review, and I jumped on it!  Goodbye forever, stupid Victoria's Secret bag.

What I appreciate most about this bag is that it has the luxurious look and feel of leather, while being entirely animal-friendly.  I never want animals to be hurt, but I also can't exactly weave my own bags out of hemp, right?  So it's really nice to find a vegan-appropriate option that is still stylish and impressively posh!  When you look at this bag, there are no tell-tale giveaway signs that the bag is not leather.  The texture and sheen are exactly on point. The hardware is reliable and sturdy, as you would expect on a leather bag---but a major benefit of this one is that it's much more lightweight.  I used to use a big heavy duty leather satchel years ago, but even when it was completely empty it was a drag to carry around due to the ridiculous weight.  Forget about loading it with books, shoes, clothes, and electronics.  You'd need to be a weight-lifter to carry that thing around.  But by comparison, this bag is reasonably lightweight, but it still has some structure, so it doesn't crumple into a flat soggy mess when it's empty.
And it's really the perfect size to use as a carry-on bag

The interior is just as nice---it's a cheerful fabric, and there are numerous pockets and divided areas that make it user-friendly, so I don't spend hours digging around inside.  There's definitely enough room in there to pack enough for a long weekend getaway.  Bottom line: this is a good looking carry-on and I have no trouble recommending it.

Silly me, I ordered the shorter one (18 inch) which is a wee bit shorter than I would like, but that's my own fault. I like the feel of this chain being 4mm thick, it is thicker than the average chain in my collection. I like the black and the way it catches in the light, but I can already see where the black will rub off if it spends much time against other chains, so I would recommend wearing the chain on its own and not hanging pendants from it to keep that from happening (so minus one star for that). The clasp seems pretty durable, so that is nice. And the way the chain is roped prevents it from getting all knotted up the way more delicate chains do, so that is cool. All in all I just wish I had bought the longer one. I might still do that and give this one to my kid with her scrawny neck. I received a discount on this item in exchange for an honest review, but might buy another (longer) one at regular price too. It's a cool chain. It does not come in a fancy package though, if you're looking to give it as a gift, but it does come with a nifty little black drawstring pouch, so there's that.

Love this wallet.  Slim and looks great.

I have been using the wallet for less than a month on a daily basis.  The wallet is already losing its shape.  It looks much older than it is and I'm not rough on wallets.  I work in an office and treat the wallet properly (I don't toss it around, place things on top of it, etc.) thus the wallet is not subjected to harsh conditions.  It has a very nice soft leather but there are problems.

When placing a driver's license, 4 credit cards and 6 bills (US), it ends up being as thick as a regular wallet.  I don't know what the "slim" description means in this case.  I don't like thick, bulky wallets that's why I purchased this wallet, because it was "slim" according to the description.

Removing credit cards from the leather slots can be difficult.  It's good they don't fall out but it should not require lots of effort to remove the cards.  There should be a balance between security and ease of use.  The slots need to be a very small fraction larger to allow easier access.

The tab (EZ Access pull handle) used to pull out the credit cards under the main area is not working properly on my wallet.  I've used such a system before and it has worked well on other wallets, not this one.  When cards are inserted and lowered, the tab protrudes more than what is shown on the picture.  It looks tacky.  Other people who have seen the tab also have made comments how it looks "weird".  The tab looks too long.  When using the tab, the cards don't come out to a good comfortable level for removal.  Believe, as my wife noted, the tab was not properly set in the pocket when it was manufactured.

At this price point, I would have expected a bit more quality.  Although I like the feel of the leather, the actual use is not acceptable thus getting a different wallet from another manufacturer.  If this wallet was much older, I would have given it a higher rating but with such a short time of use, the best this wallet deserves is 2 stars - that's primarily because of the good leather feel.

reviewText:
I was looking for a minimal wallet and took a bit of a chance on this since obviously you can't handle it or judge the exact size with just the listing.
Pro:  The size is perfect.  Your cards "face" each other so you won't have them dropping out of the slots like a toploaded wallet.  The currency slot is cool because it has a little cover that makes it disappear-- I don't use paper money much but to have a few bills there for emergencies is nice but you don't have the cash in the way every day.  There is a separate "exposed" slot for coupons or whatever.
Con: The leather seems very high grade but it's very smooth, almost slippery, especially when the wallet was brand new.  This can be nice in that it comes in and out of the pocket easily but it's easy to drop it too.  The material inside the wallet is slippery too-- again a plus to get cards in and out but they do shift a little.
Overall, good quality at this price point.
Ordered this for my son's Birthday in July, he loves Red . It came  very nicely pack looks very expensive.

When my previous card wallet went walkabout, I started searching for a replacement, but had a few things on my list it needed to have. First, it needed to be slim. I had gotten used to my previous wallet being in the front pocket, so wanted something similar.

Next was quality leather - not the weird waxy or cardboardy type leather you get on cheaper wallets. Ideally it would have an ID window, space for a few notes (though I don't usually carry cash) and finally, RFID protection. It wasn't a biggie, just a nice to have.

In the Ikepod I nearly found all of the above - its a fairly slim wallet, very carryable, with space for flat notes and little hidden extras like a SIM card slot and coin pouch. The security of the RFID protection was a definite bonus.

So I returned it.

Why? Well, two things bothered me about it - the leather, though it seems quality and is very supple, is a little thin for my taste. It does seem robust for a few years, but the thinness of the leather didn't quite float my boat. And second, the color. I'm a fan of the tobacco type of color - it just gives leather that classic look. This color wasn't quite what I was looking for. It's not red but also not quite brown.

Color is a very subjective thing - and for a wallet with so many features I want, color may not be a big deal. But there's a few things in life you use, like a wallet, a pillow, etc that you'll need to use everyday, and if it's not 100% to your liking, then for me the search continues. 99% of people who buy this wallet will probably like it, so it would be unfair of me to mark it down harshly just because the color is a bit off. So therefore, if you like the choices this wallet comes in, I'd definitely recommend it.
Love, love, love! I bought this for my boyfriend after I had returned two other wallets. This is perfect. Such high quality, perfect size. Boyfriend loves it too :)

I searched for a long time for a replacement for a Coach vertical bifold slim wallet. There are only two choices; Bellroy and Ikepod. That is,unless you want to spend a small fortune on a wallet. I would give it another 1/2 star actually, 4 1/2. I would knock down a tiny bit because the leather, albeit very nice quality, is a bit thin. Not too thin such that is feels cheap, but the leather could be slightly more substantial. This is a little nit picky, but relevant if one is looking for Coach quality leather.

I bought a second one as either a spare or to give as a gift.

reviewText: This wallet is amazing!!!  I was in need of a new wallet, and looking to find a quality wallet that would be around for years, and I believe I found it. You can tell just from the packaging that you're getting quality, I mean they didn't skimp on anything.  I like that it has a liner inside, and is made with quality leather, it fits all of my things perfectly and actually does a good job at still looking good. I was given this product at a discounted price for my unbiased review. I love this wallet!!!

This may bey a bit lengthy so I'll start by saying I LOVE this wallet. That way if you need to move on and were looking for a simple one liner reviews, there it is.

Now, for those who want to know more let me start by covering a few areas that made me a satisfied customer.

1. Packaging. The wallet showed up in a very nice fit-to-size box. Complete with styrofoam cut to size to make it snug. It also was placed in a very nice suede pouch. Overall it just felt like I was opening something of quality versus a cheap product. The seller obviously spent some time thinking about packaging and the look and feel of it.

2. Leather Quality: Well it's obviously real letter. The look and feel are thinner but good quality. I don't think I'd go for a thick side of beef style wallet anyway so this being thin and soft leather works great for me. It's not so thin that it feels fragile but soft to the touch. Very good stiching and it doesn't seem like it a bunch of pieces sewn together. Rather, it appears to be just two large pieces of leather and the trim added.

3. Comfort:  I've been carrying this for just over a week now and I love it! I don't carry a ton of stuff cause I think guys that walk around with a brick on their butts look pretty dumb. This wallet is the perfect size for what I typically carry. I keep 3-4 credit cards, ID in the ID holder, minimal cash, and I always have 8-10 of my business cards in there for the just in case moments when I need one. All in all it doesn't feel bulky at all. Huge plus for me on this!

4. Price: Can't go wrong on price! I searched a lot and found a few other that look the same but nearly 3 times the price. Belroy looked similar but at $89.95 versus $38.95 it's an easy decision for me!

Hope this helps. I haven't figured out how to get free stuff for my reviews yet so I write about what I buy.

The picture makes this "Coat" seem better than it is. The back is not much longer than the front, the dovetail effect doesn't happen when the net difference in length is maybe 2 inches. The picture makes it look much more dramatic than it is. It's basically the same length all the way around. The material is a thin, stretch polyester rather than a wool, so this is not a coat, it's a long blazer, and totally unsuitable for anything but a temperate day. It has *zero* pockets. Come on!! We have so few pockets (or totally useless ones in our pants) that outerwear should have at least an inner pocket. This has nothing. It's window dressing and it's not all that impressive at that. I will alter it and shorten the front to get the promised shape, add a pocket and, since I had to order xxl to get one that will fit my bust and shoulders upon other reviews, take in the waist and arms to give it a better shape. Not everyone is willing or able to do this to clothing to make it work, and it's irritating to me that I have to do it. I'd return it immediately if I weren't able to fix it. There's no tag except a size and paper branding tag on the inside with minor care instructions, so if you're allergic to certain synthetics, you're gonna want to avoid this one. The lining is so thin, the seams are clearly visible and create ugly lines. If I'd spent a lot on this, I'd be angry. Avoid. On the plus side, shipping was very fast, but it's sad that that's the only positive I'm coming away with.

I usually wear a large, but based on the reviews, the size chart, and my prior experiences with "Asian sizes," I ordered an XX-Large. It was unflatteringly too big.

My actual sizes are distributed around the size chart between Large and XX-Large. My waist is bigger than the XX-Large, my bust is X-Large, and my shoulders are Large.

Other reviewers who typically wear a Large like myself have mentioned ordering two sizes up. But I found two sizes up was significantly too much, and now I'm not sure whether to size down one size or two...

One of the issues with "Asian sizing" aside from when the sellers don't make an attempt to convert appropriately for selling to American customers on Amazon is the inconsistency. One customer's XX-Large can arrive significantly bigger than another's. And sometimes the seller will respond to the reviews by improving the size chart or converting the sizes, but won't indicate in the description that they did so and on what date.

I'm not sure what the culprit wss here: that 1 size up is more appropriate than 2, that the sizing is inconsistent, or that the seller has adjusted the sizing. But even the waist was too big. My guess is that the sizes are very inconsistent.

Overall the quality of the item was okay in terms of fabric and stitching and cut. It's not a warm coat, it's light and more fashion than function, but it wasn't crappy thin costume fabric, either. I liked it in person,  although of course it's not as nice as the sample in the photos.

However, another inconsistency in the item appears to be that, although you can see closures on the model and mine arrived with both buttons and hooks on it, there were no button holes or loops in which to employ them. This is in my opinion a pretty big issue, although I have coats I never button, the cut and drape of this one is not friendly to that look.

I'm a huge fan of layering with the simple white onesie; in the winter, my daughter will wear one maybe 5-6 days a week.  Unfortunately, with the onset of potty training, our daycare teachers have forbidden onesies and are even threatening to cut off the snaps if we continue to send her to school in them.  Thus, my dilemma: find a soft, very-close-fitting, plain white t-shirt that can slip over a very large head (I like to joke that my daughter has the proportions of a lollipop).

I looked at a ton of t-shirts before ordering this one from Lovetti.  It's a great shirt, but ultimately not what I'm looking for.

Ignore the reviewers that say this runs small; it does not (see attached photo comparing 2T against a Carter's 18m onesie).  The fabric is lightweight, smooth (almost silky), and very stretchy (the fabric composition 7% elastane, folks!) -- all of these are attributes you'd want for a layering t-shirt.  If you still can't imagine the fabric, think of it as the t-shirt cousin of your favorite leggings.  The seams, including the collar, are finished nicely.

Unfortunately, the collar is what caused me to return this shirt instead of sizing down.  Because it's finished, the collar doesn't stretch as beautifully as the rest of the fabric and my daughter's head is really quite large for her age.  Also, I'm somewhat disappointed at how confusing the sizing for this shirt is: "1" is "1T" (in other words, 12-18m), and "5" is the next size after "4T".  Basically, this shirt comes in a HUGE size range that should last you from diapers to puberty.
summary: True to size and great for layering.  Sizing is confusing.

reviewText:
I'm kind of picky about sunglasses.  I have paid hundreds of dollars for glasses I ended up hating and also paid $2.50 for the best pair of glasses I've ever had.  I've had the best luck with nice (but not high end) glasses from Costco.

The optics on these glasses are great.  They are actually polarized, which isn't always the case with glasses advertised as polarized.  The lenses are large and provide good coverage.  The lenses are plastic and are nice and clear.  I don't notice any image distortion at all when I look through these lenses.

The fit and feel is also really good.  They are nice and light on my face and they don't pinch anywhere, which are my 2 biggest complaints with most sunglasses.  The nose piece is adjustable by bending the metal, which is an okay way of customizing the size.

The great thing about this pair of glasses is the titanium frames.  They feel like nothing on your face.  They are almost ridiculously light weight.  But, being lightweight doesn't make them feel like they are falling off or anything.  The frames make these glasses just spectacular.  I know Maui Jim makes some glasses like this that are CRAZY expensive.  I've never tried the Maui Jim ones, but these glasses are just great.

All in all, I'm glad I bought these glasses.  These are probably going to be new go to glasses for everyday wear.

I received a small discount on these glasses for my honest review.  But, for under $20, I will probably happily buy more of these to try different lenses and frame colors.
summary: Just awesome. You will not be disappointed in these glasses.

reviewText:
I am 5'5" and 115 lbs. I typically wear a XS in most American retailer sizing; I ordered the small of the blue dress and it fit well. The color is beautiful. The arms are loose, as shown in the picture. I'm a 34A bra size, and the chest was a bit tight. It does have quite a bit of stretch, but the material is also pretty thick, so it flattens me out just a little if I'm not wearing at least a soft cup bra. Even so, it still looks professional, and with the right heels and bold accessories it looks amazing for work or semi-casual evenings. I think the length was a great balance to the conservative neckline and sleeves, but if your workplace is very conservative, the dress might be too short; it fell below my fingertips with my arms at my sides, but did come above the knee. The photo makes the dress look like an A-line, but it didn't flare out nearly as much as it looks like in the picture, at least for me. I don't have much in the way of hips, so the pockets did bulge a little if I'm being super picky. Regardless, I'd rather have the pockets than not, and overall, I will get a ton of wear out of this dress.

Pros:
- Love the bold, vibrant color
- Material feels very substantial and seams are well sewn
- Line of the dress is flattering
- Pockets!
- Sleeves are comfortable
- Length is appropriate for most modern work environments and social gatherings

Cons:
- Chest is a bit tight, and I'm only a 34A
- Hips/pockets are a bit loose and bulge a little-- prob wouldn't be a problem if you have wider hips than me

I received this product in exchange for an honest and unbiased review.  All opinions expressed are solely my own and have not been influenced in anyway.

I got this for my daughter who is very petite (5' 2") and is normally a size US 2, 3 or 4 (depending on the make).  This is a very form fitting dress, made from a nice stretchy material.

It has a nice rounded neckline that sits comfortably on the shoulders.  Can easily move and stretch in the dress without it binding or bunching.

The sleeves come to just above the elbows and are not too tight and allows for freedom of movement.  The length comes to just above the knees.  For someone taller, I'm sure it would be a bit shorter.  Nice long zipper in the back that was easy to use.

My daughters favorite part is the pockets!  It's hard to find flattering dresses with pockets and this fit the bill in all aspects with the beautiful blue color, the feel of the fabric and the pockets are at hip level on her and are very deep.

Can be used for multiple occasions.  The dress is so comfortable, she can not wait to wear it to work or school.  Would go great with flats or heels.

Well see if it holds it shape and color after a few washes.  If we have issues, I'll be sure to update this review.

All in all, a beautiful and well made dress.

They do not do exchanges but will allow me to return the shirt. If the shirt was worn it has to be washed before returning it... no problem for I could not get the shirt on anyway so tags etc were all in place. If you pass 30 days, there is a restocking fee of 20% which I was unaware of.
When I questioned the vendor why I have a Large and ordered the same size it did not fit. The vendor stated that Under Armour has different sizing charts for different shirts.  That just did not make sense. How are you to buy a product with "floating" sizes.
So, I went online to Nordstrum to find the same exact heat guard compression tee. There was a size chart that could be pulled up to check size before ordering.... only 1 chart for Under Armour. I did all the measurements correctly to find that I was to order a Large.
I know the shirt fits tight but since I already HAD a large that fits, and the chart from Under Armor at Nordstrum confirmed that I had ordered the correct shirt size, the statement that there are different size charts for different Under Armour shirts " just doesn't fit!".
I personally will visit a store and actually try it on to avoid the hassle and disappointment of waiting for a product that does not fit, seemingly was ordered correctly, and then had to be mailed back.

reviewText:
The best looking chronograph watch in the Alpnach series of Victorinox Swiss Army watches, now discontinued.

https://www.swissarmy.com/us/product/Timepieces/Discontinued/Professional/Alpnach-Chronograph/241196

Both the 1/10 second (upper right) and the hour (upper left) dials sport red hands, evoking a classic aircraft instrument panel.  I bought mine on Woot.com almost a year ago for $300, and it has kept time perfectly.  It has full length chronograph minute and second hands, as well as a 1/10 second dial, thus providing excellent stopwatch functionality.  The only minus is that the shiny center section of the band is prone to scratching.

In hindsight, at that price, I should have bought two: one for myself, and one to give to my son as a family heirloom.

I'm not a watch expert.  But I have loved watches since I was a child.  I always wanted a good watch but felt that it was a waste of money when a cheaper watch would do.  This year my wife asked me what I wanted for Christmas.  The only thing that came to mind is a watch.  I like the idea of a Swiss Army watch.  Of course I have a Swiss Army knife to go along with it.

I struggled with keeping the watch.  It has too many dials and hands. And being cheap, I thought it was expensive.  At first I thought it was a fake because it is not in Victorinox's catalog.  But I found it in the discontinued section.  It was released in 2011 and I guess discontinued this year.  So, it is an authentic Victorinox watch.  It seems to be highly regarded by others.  It is my understanding that the watch mechanism itself is still used in later models.

There was one inconsistency.  The description of the watch on the Victorinox site is that it has a see through back case.  This one does not.  However, the Alpnach model comes in the Swiss Quartz version and a mechanical version. Though I did not see it stated, it seems that the mechanical version is the one with see through back case.  It would be interesting if someone could verify that bit of information.

As to the hands.  It has a lot more going on than is really necessarily needed to tell time.  But I figured out how to deal with it all.  Smartphones really make a watch like this obsolete.  However, wearing a chronograph watch is a good tradition for manly dress.  It looks good and it has all the functionality that a person could want.  And sometimes, you don't have your smartphone with you.

I have never had a Swiss watch before. It looks good in both casual and dressy situations.  It seems to keep good time.  It feels substantial as you would think a Swiss watch should.  The claim, and I guess it is true, is that the seller was an authorized Victorinox dealer which means that it has the three year Victorinox warranty.  I'm glad that I bought it. And it is a bargain, especially when you see what others are selling it for.

I got this Omega because the blue dial really appealed to me.  The dial has a "micro-starburst" pattern that reflects light in a "spoke" pattern around the dial.  The hands and applied markers are silver, and this watch is extremely readable in low light conditions.  Luminous paint highlights the markers and the dials, and it works--although it's not as bright as some "sports watches."  I have other Omega automatics of the same 2500C caliber, and this is the most accurate one of the lot.  It keeps time well within the Swiss COSC specs, not gaining or losing more than 1 - 2 seconds per day; in fact, it will give many quartz watches a run for their money!  The case is actually 39.2mm in diameter.  It doesn't feel too heavy or too light.  Shirtsleeves slide right over it, instead of hanging up as they might on a bigger watch.  The sapphire cystal is extremely resistant to scratches, and will shrug off knocks that would leave other crystals badly scratched.  The caseback is also sapphire, and you can view the inner workings of the watch.  The Omega movement is a beautiful one, and is rhodium plated to increase life and resist corrosion.  The crown is of the screw-down variety, which means that you have to unscrew it a bit before it pops out to allow winding or setting.  A screw-down crown also helps to ensure water resistance, and this watch is rated to 150 meters underwater.  I would not go swimming with it, however, as there are "dive watches" made for that purpose--and my personal rule is not to swim with any watch not rated for at least 200 meters.  You can wind this watch to get it started, or to make up for periods when you are not wearing it.  It has a power reserve of around 42 hours.  This is the perfect watch to wear with a pair of blue jeans or with a suit.  Like all Omega coaxial movement watches, it has a three-year warranty--IF you buy it from an Omega authorized dealer.  This model is being replaced by the newer 8500 caliber Aqua Terra series with the teck dials; however, many people prefer this style over the newer one.  Both the older and newer models feature coaxial movements, which means reduced friction and greater accuracy over the long run.  This is my favorite watch for everyday wear, as it is good looking, accurate and just feels good on your wrist.  There is never a battery to replace, and you can probably go 6 - 8 years before having it serviced.  If an authorized Omega service center does the service, you get two years of warranty following that service!  This watch is an extremely good value, and you should pick one up before they are all gone!  I plan on keeping mine forever!
summary: Best Omega Watch for Everyday Wear

I bought this particular model for my daughter, who borrowed my full size mens Ironman once and fell in love with it. This one is a little more compact, a plus for either gender I think. It also has a slightly less fashionable band than the regular Ironman Womans model, making it cheaper. (There are so many models bearing the "Ironman" moniker  that "regular" is probably meaningless. Wish I could be more helpful, but it would seem that overwhelming us with choices is part of Timex's marketing strategy.) Since she's in the habit of loosing watches I didn't want to pay more than I had to, and this model gave us the functionality we both love at a reduced price.

I'm a long time runner and probably a little more obsessed than some with timing my runs. I like the latest Ironman functionality better than previous watches (various Casios including G-shock, Timex Expedition, Older Ironmans). I particularly like the button layout (start/lap button easy to hit, stop and indiglo buttons hard to hit accidentally, accidental resets virtually impossible) and I've gotten so used to using my 50-lap chrono to track my split times that I hate being without it. This ones says 100-lap in the description, but my daughters says "10-lap" on the watch itself (look closely at the picture and you can see this). I tested and it actually remembers 30 laps (go figure). The big difference, however, as that while I can record multiple workouts on mine, with the date of each, hers only remembers the last workout, and once you reset the chrono your data is gone forever. Personally I would hate that. This watch also lacks the Dual interval timer that I use for reminding me when to "eat" (gels) on long runs, and has only one alarm. Mine has three.

The Klamath model is a big disappointment for me. It has a different foot bed and I found it very uncomfortable. I had to give mine away and get something else. Don't buy these before you try on a pair to see if they work for you. I am an avid hiker and walker, have a high instep and arch, and this boot actually bruised my right foot. Buyer beware. I still love my other Keens.

The leather on these unique hikers has a rough-hewn and tumbled look, rather charming really, like they were cobbled together from a pair of well-oiled baseball mitts. The sole is like the work of some mad scientist--with a shank plate interlocking the outsole, and a rubberized cork section plainly visible on the heel. With the well-known Keen wrap-around toe protector and webbing strap to snug up the heel, you have a distinctive looking pair of boots with lots of built-in character.
The really good part is that they are genuinely comfortable right out of the box. The wide sole makes for an unusually stable, secure, and anchored stance. They feel so good you don't want to take them off at the end of the day. Downsides? They run a half-size small, so you may need to size up for a good fit. Also, the tongue is made of a thick material that requires careful centering to keep it from clumping. Other than that, these are a wonderful example of bootmaking ingenuity. Good going, Keen!

This bracelet makes my wife's Momentum yellow diver look much better than the black Velcro strap that came with it.  The bracelet is solid, brushed stainless steel and is very well make.  Even the end links are solid.  The fit against the watch case is so precise that it makes it look like the end links are part of the case.  It gives her diver a whole new, and much classier, look.  She can wear it to the office now instead of just with her jeans.  I've paid less for quality men's bracelets, but where else would I find a 14mm stainless steel bracelet that would fit her Momentum diver so perfectly?  No where, that's where.  So in the end, I'd say it is worth the price.

She has really small wrists, so I sized the bracelet for her with an $8 bracelet sizing tool I had already purchased from Amazon a while back.  On the inside of the bracelet, there are arrows that show you the direction the pins should be driven out and and put back in.  The clasp also has four micro adjustment holes for a more perfect fit. It was just as easy to re-size as any other bracelet I've done in the past, which is to say, it was pretty simple.  :)

That being said, my watch is a St Moritz and not a Momentum but when I would search for St Moritz watch bands I would get Momentum results and it looks as though the companies are one and the same so I gave it a try. The band is beautiful and has a heavy weight to it that gives it the look and feel of quality. The supplier quickly acknowledged my request for return, and refunded my purchace. I hope it works for you.

Kate Spade heels are my favourite high heeled shoes brand, especially with their made in Italy lines of leather-soled high heels. I own three pairs of their Dani Dress Pumps, which in my opinion are daintier versions of the Karolina pumps:

1) Toes: the Dani's are true almond toed, while Karolina are slightly more round toned;
2) Heels: the Dani's have more slender and narrower heels, while Karolina's have sturdier and slightly larger heel caps.
3) Platform: Dani's do not have any platforms. Karolina has a low platform, making them definitely much easier to walk in, and they felt sturdier too.

Still, I prefer the looks of Dani; but if I knew I'd been standing prolonged period of time, I will put on Karolina.

Well, let me tell you that not only should be wary to buy these gloves because of the poor fit but also because the seller is deceitful.

I purchased a size 9 and it didn't fit and then returned them to the seller and purchased a size 10, but the seller shipped both back to me because they said I returned the gloves in 'worn condition' which I did not as I returned them in the same condition as received (I know you're saying to yourself no seller would be that deceitful, but Fratelli Orsini is).

After hearing my experience Amazon felt compelled to give me $100 credit to my account and my Credit Card Company (Chase) also did the same so I walked away with two pairs of beautifully made gloves which I cannot give away because they don't fit a mans hand...So again I repeat "Buyer Beware."

/Mike

PS after speaking at length with Amazon Customer Service I was informed in order to combat deceitful merchants like Fratelli your best defense if to file an A-Z claim within 90 days and ensure when you return the product to them you do so with a tracking number so you can prove you in fact returned them to the seller as you say you did. My mistake was not filing this and going straight to my credit card to issue a Chargeback. I was told if I filed the A-Z claim that I "100% would have won" and should do that going forward.

reviewText:
I purchased this ring as my "vacation ring" because it's similar to my real engagement ring.  A couple things:

(1)CZ stones are heavier than diamonds (or so I'm told) so the same carat weight of a CZ will appear smaller than a diamond of the same carat weight.  My real engagement ring has a 2.1 carat solitaire, which is visually similar to this 3 carat CZ, so do not expect a stone that is the size of a 3 carat diamond.

(2)The stone on this ring isn't set perfectly centered, but you can only tell if you look closely.

(3) The stone also isn't set tightly, so I can actualy move it around in the setting, but unless the prongs break, I don't think it will fall out.  This might be unique to the one sent to me, but overall the quality isn't fantastic.

All in all, it looks great if you don't look too close, and it'll do the trick for being my "vacation ring," but it's definitely no substitute for the real thing!
summary: Not bad for what it is

I can only compare this jacket with the Zuni Jacket (not the current model, but the one from 2 years ago) from Ground Sportswear and the more traditional Adidas unlined Wind `ClimaProof'.  I use the jacket mainly for running as I have been exclusive to the ASICS Kayano shoes for distance training the past 7 years.  All 3 are far superior to less expensive `wind breakers' that I have had in the past.

I am overall happy with the jacket and prefer the feel of this softshell to the nylon types like my Adidas.  It does better than the Ground or Adidas with the rain.  It has breathable vents on the back and on the underside of the sleeves.  While this helps in warmer weather, I train a lot in windy conditions and though the jacket says `wind proof', the noticeable vents certainly don't help keeping wind out, but the 80% of the jackets that doesn't have the vents does a great job keeping out the wind.
The zipper really stands out compared to the Ground when fully zipped.  The Ground is more of a hiking/rock climbing jacket and therefore the collar zips to high and not the snug you would want.  The ASICS is better designed for running.

Positives:  Overall this is the best running jacket I have ever owned.  It is relatively light, and great for running in weather about down to 40 degrees.  It does OK in the wind and pretty good in the rain (but don't expect GoreTex performance).  It fits snugly and does not go much below the waist so you can wear it during your hard tempo and interval runs as well as your long easy runs.  If you want this jacket for running in weather 40-65 degrees F then you will be happy.

Negatives:  When I run in weather under 40, I really have to layer up.  This creates a problem for me since I wear a 46 suit jacket.  It gets tight though it claims to be XL.  While some reviews say it is nice enough to wear around the town, I don't totally agree (for me).  Unless my clothes are really tight fitting, it feels uncomfortable.  It does not seem to keep you very warm either when you are not exercising in chilly weather.  In contrast, the Ground Jacket looks better (for wearing around town), does a better job with wind, gives you more room to move around, and seems a little warmer when you are not exercising.

A big fan of Asics shoes but not all of their clothing.  This jacket was made of a strange material and not like other Thermpolis clothing items I had purchased in the past.  The fit was ok - Under Armour makes better clothing in this category.

Okay, this is going to be a comprehensive underwear review.  Not something that I have done before, but I'm hoping it will be helpful to someone.  My goal is to provide my personal opinion about fit, comfort and performance.  This is a review about men's underwear though, including thongs, so I am going to try to keep the discussions clinical but informative.  If you believe you may be offended by this topic, please, do not read any further.  Thank you.

Every male is going to be built differently, so let me explain my situation and why it became so important for me to find "the right underwear."  I have a 37.5" hip measurement and a 38.25" waist (at the belly button) measurement.  All the underwear I have tried is size "large."  I originally tried to wear boxers and boxer briefs, but they became unacceptable in a professional setting.  I switched to briefs, but then found them to be too restricting.  I needed to find underwear that gave me support throughout the day, but also were roomy enough to accommodate my volume.  I honestly believe that male underwear should have a variety of sizes just like women's bras have.  Unfortunately, no man would ever admit that he wears a 38AA underwear, so I guess that isn't going to happen anytime soon. Ha!

The seven pairs I will be reviewing are:
Hanes Classics Men's 3-Pack Full Rise Brief
Hanes Fashion Mid-Length Briefs 5-Pack
Hanes Men's Seamless Pouch Brief (Discontinued?)
Gregg Homme Men's Black Push Up Padded Thong Size Large
Calvin Klein Men's Body Hip Brief, Black, Large
Calvin Klein Men's Body Thong, Black, Large
Papi Men's 3-Pack Cotton Thong In White, White, Large

Hanes Classics Men's 3-Pack Full Rise Brief

These are an economical purchase.  They are what I consider to be the average cotton brief.  The pack came in cool shades, none were white.  The waistband and other materials were pretty comfortable.  The crotch on this underwear is designed for a Ken doll though.  My body would not fit comfortably in these.  The restriction caused an asymmetric arrangement which, during certain movements, would be uncomfortable.  The lack of sufficient cup design caused the gussets to remain elevated off of the body, which in turn causes occasional rubbing and irritation to the upper thigh.  Overall, these are "default underwear."  2 STARS

Hanes Fashion Mid-Length Briefs 5-Pack

These are also an economical purchase.  They were better than the previous default underwear in that the materials were even softer, and the waistband was low enough to allow for no underwear to be seen while wearing certain jeans.  Unfortunately, this underwear suffers the same drawbacks that the Hanes Classics Men's 3-Pack Full Rise Brief did; there is just no considerations taken for large male anatomy.  The gussets again, would not lie against the leg, causing occasional irritation, and the material was so restrictive that it caused asymmetric arrangements that were occasionally uncomfortable.  Overall, these are "better, but not great." 3 STARS

Hanes Men's Seamless Pouch Brief (Discontinued?)

So, I found these pairs on Hanes' website some time ago.  They were so comfortable, that I own over half a dozen of these.  They are spandex-like material, and the crotch is cupped to provide a pouch to give support and symmetry.  All the material is very soft and comfortable all over.  Unfortunately, it is not without drawbacks.  Besides being rare to find and possibly discontinued all together, this underwear has an obscenely high waistband.  It easily goes over my belly button and is labeled with a gigantic "Hanes" logo right in the front.  Now, I do not have washboard abdominals, so on top of everything, my bellow, however minor, causes the material to roll down.  This causes a very mild discomfort, especially while wearing pants that are tight in the waste.  By prefolding the underwear down, I can make a satisfactory adjustment.  Overall, this underwear has been my "long-standing favorite."  4 STARS

Gregg Homme Men's Black Push Up Padded Thong Size Large

Okay, first I will say that this is the first thong I have ever worn, so let me give you a man's opinion on just that first.  On occasion, I have had briefs bunch up and it would require me to make a wardrobe adjustment.  Typically this would be important while wearing professional or evening dress attire, and would involve positioning myself near a wall and doing a slight shift dance so it doesn't look like I'm "just picking."  Now, when I first wore the thong that is the same feeling I had.  I felt compelled to shift and adjust in an attempt to fix my garments.  After some hours of wearing it though, it began to feel more natural.  While walking, the thong feels just fine.  If anything, it feels most uncomfortable while sitting.  If I do an extreme slouch, it feels fine, and if I sit up all prim and proper, it feels fine.  Slouching, just a little though, makes the material tighten down on my coccyx, which causing unfamiliar discomfort.  Being forced to sit up more straight was not something I expected from a thong design.  Now, the rest of the underwear, on the hips and waist, is quite comfortable.  The material is rather thin, but nothing roles down.  Everything stays where it should.  Finally, the crotch design: this underwear has a padded cup, which I was expecting to be something ridiculous, but in actuality, it is quite sensible.  It reminds me of the form material in a bra.  Not so much padded to give you the illusion of extra size, but more preformed for shape.  It feels akin to wearing a costume, like a codpiece.  My body is comfortably symmetric within the cup.  My only complaint is that the cup is not large enough to retain my volume and keep the gussets on the skin.  Again, I have that occasional irritation when the thigh meets the gusset.  If the cup was larger, it would be perfect.  For a man of a different shape, this underwear may be perfect.  Overall, I would say these are "new and interesting, but could use improvement."  4 STARS

Papi Men's 3-Pack Cotton Thong In White, White, Large

Alright, here I have the Papi set.  These win out over the Gregg Homme in multiple ways.  1.) They come in a three-pack for about the same price.  2.) They are significantly more comfortable!  3.)  The pouch is much larger.  The gussets lay flat and do not shift.  Everything is held in place quite nicely.  I love them!  There is one bad thing though.  They are ugly!  Definitely look like a jock strap or a weird pair of whitey-tighties.  So comfortable though!  I never once thought about them, from the moment I put them on and went about my day.  They were perfect.  They will make great everyday wear.  Overall, I would say these are "everyday underwear." 4 STARS

Calvin Klein Men's Body Thong, Black, Large

These are almost as comfortable as the Papi brand.  They definitely look better than those jock straps.  Unfortunately the Calvin Klein are sold in singles.  They have all the same benefits that Papi have in fit and comfort, but I can feel the back a bit more.  It isn't bad.  Just kind of there, you know?  Overall, I would say these are "the evening wear underwear." 4 STARS

Calvin Klein Men's Body Hip Brief, Black, Large

Well, this Calvin Klein was not what I expected.  It is a cotton brief with a very well defined and comfortable pouch.  The waistband is great; in fact, all over, the underwear is comfortable.  The problem is the backside is too voluminous.  I don't have a backside like a linebacker, but my bum isn't flat as a board either.  The underwear is formed to fit a much rounder bottom, and so it is exceptionally saggy.  They are definitely not for dress pants.  I'm wearing them with kakis, and they seem to be okay.  These pants are not the tightest I have.  Definitely wouldn't want to wear them with tight pants unless you want a bunchy diaper effect.  These would probably be very comfortable with jeans while doing manual labor.  In fact, I have to say that comfort is the number one plus with this pair.  Unfortunately, they are not cheap, being sold only in singles.  Overall, I'm pretty disappointed in them.  If they were half the price or if you have a lot of booty, these underwear will be a good buy.  They have quality, just not shaped properly for me.  Overall, I would say these are "overly expensive work underwear." 3 STARS

So, there we have it!  I was really hoping the CK Hip Briefs would have replaced my "long-standing favorite" but I'm surprised to see that award going to the Papi 3-Pack.  They are definitely the most economical/comfortable combo.  They do lack quite a bit of style, so I wouldn't wear them for an evening out.  The CK thong has the most style, sacrificing a little comfort and a lot of coin.  The Gregg Homme was definitely the most gimmicky.  Having never worn a thong before, it does not give a good first impression.  It isn't nearly as comfortable as the others.  It wasn't so bad that I would throw them out outright, but I won't be buying another pair.  The Calvin Klein Hip Briefs were the most disappointing.  They feel great and fit well in the front, but the back is just horrible.  I won't be buying any more anytime soon.  Maybe after rounding out the posterior with some squats.  The three Hanes underwear pairs are definitely out.  The seamless pouch is hard to find and the waistband is way too high.  The other two are just not comfortable unless you're a Ken doll.  The Papi are definitely going to be the next ones on my wishlist.  I'm pretty satisfied with them, and I could see them being my everyday underwear.

I hope this review was helpful to someone.  Every man is going to be different, so I wanted to give enough detail to help you decide.  None of these pairs were of "bad quality," they just have their little pros and cons.  If you have any questions, I would be happy to respond.

I bought this bag in Black from another vendor and i love it!  Its big and deep on the inside.. I carry a makeup case (that weighs a ton), a wallet thats always packed with change, a paperback book, a small umbrella and a few other things and theres plenty of more room b/c the bag is deep.  Not to mention its not heavy for packing all that stuff.. Its actually much lighter than any other bag I've owned.

Leather is soft and supple...Flat handle straps are adjustable and much more comfortable than rounded straps. it also has a cross body strap. Inside pocket is pretty deep and there are 2 outer zip pockets that can each fit a smart phone.  Also on the interior are some credit card slots (which are bit too big for cards so they might fall to bottom of ur bag) and 2 pen holders (i wouldnt put a pen in my bag out of fear of it leaking)

The only reason i gave this bag 4 stars is b/c the interior color and pattern is awful...very tropical; it reminds me of the colors of a parrot. But all their bags have this I think.

I've been using this bag for almost a  year now, and it's the best, most practical bag I've used. I'm a teacher, and this bag can fit the assortment of things I need : 11 inch laptop in a neoprene case, drink bottle, pencil case, notebook, a light sweater, the standard wallet/phone/keys.  The two outside pockets are terrific; I like that on one side, it's a smaller pocket where I can put my car keys. This provides easy access as I'm not fishing around a deep pocket (esp important for me as I'm often walking to carparks at night after tutoring). However I think it would have been better if, instead of all the credit card slots which I've never used, the bag had another pocket in the main compartment - it has one zip pocket which fits a large wallet nicely, but another one, even just a slip pocket on the other side (not in the middle to split the main space) would have been ideal.

The leather : I was disappointed at first and found it quite stiff with a strong, unpleasant smell, however it's softened beautifully and the smell has gone. So if you buy and aren't that impressed with the leather at first, it will improve and become a lovely supple bag.

The only problem I've encountered with this bag are the shoulder straps. There are 4 large buckles on the short straps - I've found the buckles tend to catch and pull on certain clothing like loosely knitted sweaters, and even a textured woven coat (I was shocked when I saw the condition of my coat and took a while to figure out what had caused all these pulled threads on the right upper back and sleeve), so unfortunately I just have to avoid certain clothing with this bag.

reviewText: I have had my Parma for over a couple of years now.  Take it with me to court everyday.  Holds my Mac, my accessories, and my case files. It gets saggy with use and it is so floppy that it will not stand up when placed on the floor.  As far as durability is has not been great. First the rivet that held the strap on failed. Then the clips that finish the inside edges fell off.  Then a hole developed in a corner. After that the leather cover that keeps the inside of the latch from scratching you fell off.  Next the inside zipper failed then the outside zipper failed and finally the side of the bag split when it was lifted without the flap latched. I travel for a living and I am now on the last trip that I will take with this bag. If you like Italian leather and don't plan to use it hard then it is a nice bag. If you are a heavy user you are likely to be disappointed. Oh the strap was so bad that I had to find some stiff leather to augment it; the strap is terrible.

reviewText:

I got the bag at Xmas,and have been using it ever since.  The quality is great, thick leather that is taking on a color of itsown.  The stitching excellent, and the zippers are top of the line.  I added the thick luggage strap, since I travel a lot.  The bag is roomy, I fit my laptop, and paperwork in one pocket.  All my assorted chargers, cables, & hotspot in another.  A few books, and extras in the third.  The outside zip pocket fits my iPad, headphones, & receipts.  One thing to know, none of the pockets are padded, so I suggest a padded case for a laptop.

  The Parma bag is expensive, but well worth it.  I expect this bag to last me the rest of my career.

I aleady had these earrings with earwires instead of the posts that these have. The earrings are rather heavy. The wires pulled down too much on my earlobes resulting in discomfort and worse. But I love the earring design, with these blossoms sparkling with the Svaroski crystals, enough that I was really thrilled to see these with posts; they remind a bit of another era - kind of like Billie Holiday with her iconic gardenia, except that these floral accents grace your ear instead of hair. Sure enough, the posts help stabilize the earrings when wearing them, and help reduce the pull down on my earlobes (which I find in general is a benefit of wearing posts for heavy earrings rather than wires.) So the earrings wear beautifully and look great for both dressy and casual wear. They are stunning accent pieces when worn with a simple, minimal style outfit - I recently wore them with a black top with flattering neckline/cut, jeans and heels and got a ton of compliments from both genders and many ages (the tweens even came over and said they loved my earrings!). Wore the same outfit but with dressy pants fro a more formal event, and it was all good. And also with dresses.

I find that the crystals really do stand out more than it shows in the photos: not a bad thing, but one to be clear about... there is definitely some subtle but clear "bling"; with these but do note that it is only the edging to the blossoms, and the centers. the earring itself is a solid unit and does have some motion where it attaches to the post: I rather wish that the two blossoms were separate pieces so there was a bit more movement, but that is a very minor point and mostly a personal thing.

I highly recommend these earrings. And highly recommend buying them here - from Azaara who is the L.A.-based jeweler produing them (and in several other metal colors....). I bought my first pair from online retailer Peruvian Connection. Had I known, I would way rather patronize the actual jewelry manufacturer as they can better address any direct service concerns you may have.
