reviewText:
Pros:
1) Price on Amazon for this is right on the money ($89) for this swimsuit (I've searched!).
2) It is a very flattering style, the ruching around the bust & waistline do act as a nice camoflauge and give a svelte shaping to the torso.

Cons:
1) Ruching stops at an odd spot, just below the natural waist, but above the 'Mommy pooch line'....which is not so flattering.  Wished it would have continued a bit lower as it would have been more complimentary to more bodyshapes.
2) Sizing is pretty good, but felt just a little big.  I wear about a 12/14 dress, however ordered the 14 suit (as I usually size up in swimwear).  It would have been the right size had I kept the suit, but it didn't particularly feel like a 'perfect fit'.  The straps are a bit loose so the bustline felt low, and not well supported.  I also chalk it up to the fact that since most of my swimwear has some 'control style' features built into the fabric, and this one doesn't, that may contribute to it feeling a big/looser.  It definately does NOT suck you in whatsoever.
3) The WHITE suit is pretty, but very thin!  Beware, you can see the manufacturer tag that is sewn along the inside seam easily right through the fabric.  The ruching in front adds thickness so it's not see through, but the backside, I could see may be a bit questionable when wet since it really is just as single layer.
I do body piercings professionally and I wear this shirt to work every couple of days... usually on the busiest.. and it freaks people out..  my favorite  :))

I'm a huge fan of Danskos. I've worn them across the globe and am always happy. Their canvas line was fantastic, and I've always been sad that they discontinued the line.

I bought these sneakers because I loved my canvas Dansko clogs and I was looking for something that would be similar, but in a slightly different style.

Look:
These shoes are really cute. I love them. They're like a mary jane and a sneaker in one. The color is neutral, so it's incredibly wearable with almost anything, and the insoles have a fun stripe pattern that makes these feel even cuter.

Arch Support:
Danskos generally have a lot of arch support, and these are no exception. The clog styles provide more arch support than the Valerie style, so if you're looking for arch support, you may find more in the clogs.

Fit:
With most Danskos, you generally want them to fit a bit loosely. The clogs work well in that respect, but these...maybe a little less so. I found that my usual loose fit wasn't quite as appropriate here, and I wanted these to fit a bit smaller. However, the toe box made me think that, if I'd gotten my normal size, I would've been uncomfortable. In fact, it was my uncertainty about which size I needed that made me return these shoes and try a completely different shoe.

If you've worn Dansko clogs, you may like these, but don't expect them to fit the way your clogs do.
summary: Super cute, but don't expect them to be the same as your Dansko clogs

For the price, this shoe should be manufactured better. Directly under the ball of the foot on the inside edge, the lining material in both feet is bunched up and forms a small hump under the ball of the foot exactly where one of the spikes is located on the outside of the shoe. These kill my 14 yr old's feet. Feels like a pebble is in her shoe right where her weight is when she steps or pivots. She has worn them for several games and now has a large (quarter size) blister and callus on the ball of both feet where this hump is. Tried to spend an additional $60 for replacement insoles but wanted a rigid bottom layer on the insoles so that the weight would be distributed over this hump. Ordered some on Amazon but they take 3 weeks to get here. In the mean time, she's added the insoles from her last less expensive pair of Nike's to these shoes and has 2 insoles to try and alleviate the pressure from this hump. My husband also tried to sand down the hump on the inside of the shoes but material they're made of wouldn't sand down. Obviously the material is durable but not happy with the quality and that the molded interior is not smooth especially where the most pressure is applied. These are the only shoes my daughter has ever had that she immediately takes off on the field as soon as the game is over because her feet hurt so bad. We usually spend about $80 for a new pair of soccer cleats each season. This is the first time we've splurged for the more expensive pair and we regret it.

First, I love these boots.  I've had them since March of 2014 and have worn them for nearly every adventure.  They are indeed waterproof... I've been in standing water up to the top for more than an hour.  I hunt, hike, fish, etc. in these things and usually wear them all day.  They are truly comfortable.  The problem is the padding at the top is too thick and they don't zip up around my calves like they are supposed to.  It is a problem others mentioned when I originally read reviews online before purchasing them so it wasn't completely unexpected.  The biggest problems I've had with them though, and the real reason for the 2 star rating is that the zippers just suck and they are hard as hell to get on/off.  The zipper broke on my left boot a month into owning them but I didn't care because they are still very warm and very water proof even with this failure.

After having them for nearly 20 months though, I'm looking for another pair from a different brand.  As much as I like these boots, they've taught me a good lesson about how much I don't like lace ups or zippers for calf high waterproof snake boots.  Having a single, tiny little finger loop on the back side of the boot to pull them on with all your might when the padding is WAY too thick is just painful and annoying when your muscles are already sore day 2 of a long trip.

I can't recommend these things even though I love them simply because the main components are junk and if you can't get them on and off then what they are built for doesn't really matter anyway.  I'll keep them around but these are basically going to take the place of my rubber s*** boots that live in the truck.  These won't be anything I'll rely on in the woods anymore.
summary: Not something I'd ever buy again after the last 20 months and definitely not worth the $200 price point.

reviewText: Love this wallet! I have two different styles of MKs python embossed purses that I purchased at Nordstrom and love them.  However, I got this wallet to mix with my new MKs "Selma" purse in the color Luggage.  This wallet is so pretty, well-made, and will be great as a clutch when running around.  Came with MKs tag attached and wrapped in MK tissue.  Also, came a couple of days ahead of original scheduled delivery date.

I have two major concerns about this wallet's quality being compromised over time. The first issue is that the material on the outer part of the wallet is kind of "scaly" in nature (hence, python) and I could see that over time piece by piece of it may begin to wear off especially being dragged in and out of a purse all the time. The second issue is that there are not as many card slots, which may or may not be an issue depending on the person. I just hate doubling up on cards in the card slots, so I've kept some that I don't need in a drawer for the time being. Other than that, the zipper pouch and outer zipper are extremely high quality, and is a generally sturdy wallet. The inside material seems to be firmly placed and looks great. The logo plaque is not easily scratched although I would be slightly careful with it, and is firmly placed on the wallet. I don't imagine there will be any issue with it falling off or getting loose.
summary: Good quality wallet with some caveats to consider

This soft-sided travel tote with luggage handle "pass through" is PERFECT!!!  The width isn't too large, just enough to fit over your suitcase and under the seat on a plane.  It has compartments on the outside and inside.  And it can hold about 40% of a 21" carry-on!!!!  You can fill this with all your light, small, and soft items.....keeping your 21" carry on free for larger items.  The "pass-through" keeps this tote firmly in place over your bag, and allows you to move about using only one hand.  Combine this with spinner luggage and you're all set to move through the airport, bus or train terminal with ease and speed!  It also comes with a shoulder strap, should you choose to use it alone during day trips or excursions.  The neutral black/gray color is nice. reviewText: I was a skeptic, thinking "running shorts" are for athletic people with too much money, but on distance runs (9 miles +), chafing became an issue in my standard running shorts (cheap men's boxers). Just ran 13 miles in these last night, and couldn't have been more comfortable (zero chafing).  The little pocket in the back is perfect for my car key, too.  Really loving these shorts, really recommend them to serious runners (if you're only running a few miles, men's boxers safety-pinned shut are way more cost effective).  I found them cheaper on Amazon than on the icebreaker site, so shopping around is worth it. If your significant other goes to nursing school, you need to be aware of a couple of things.  First, nurses are nothing like the women in most of the movies.  They don't wear low cut dresses with mini skirts and there is NOTHING sexy about the job.  Most of them have long days doing really gross stuff and they don't like the stereo type of the nurse outfit.  My wife doesn't even like to wear that little nurse hat.

This t-shirt is the quick change a real nurse needs.  Out of the uniform and into the comfy clothes.

It fits, it doesn't fall out. Due to my nose shape the back curve a little in the inside of my nose and does not lay flat.

I recently stretched my nose piercing from 18g to 16g and wanted a new hoop to show it off.

It has a slightly rounded edge to the open side and is extremely comfortable to wear. The flat stopper for the inside is a nice contrast to the bone style as it is less of a shock to your nerves when you accidentally bump or grab your nose (which I doltishly still do even though I have had the piercing for several years now,.. so comfort is key) or when you have a cold or allergies and have to use tissue often; this is not a have-to-remove-before-blowing type of product. ;)

Side Note- The open side of the hoop had to be slightly squeezed onto my cartridge to get the hoop to my piercing-hole... I have a smaller nose so if you have thicker nose cartilage, this may be difficult to wear without stretching it a little with pliers before trying to put it on.

This hoop was a little big for my nose but is as described.  It is good to know how big you want before buying - on my small nose, a 5/16" sized hoop is a better fit,... but I cannot fault the seller as he specifically described the hoop as 3/8" which is a little bigger.

Overall I was very happy with the product and was satisfied with it living up to its descriptions.
summary: Compfortable nose hoop - 3/8" is a little big for some, though. :)

I am partial to Victorinox.  This watch has a nice ETA movement.  It looks very handsome and is very easy to read.  The face is textured and provides a lot of detail that makes it look nicer, without distracting from being able to quickly read the time.  It's a little smaller than the current large watched that are in vogue, and I think it will stay in style for many years.  There is a window in the back of the watch for you to see the winding weight and escapement and all the little parts.  It always amuses kids.  The cystal is sapphire, so it should really resist scratching as much as anything but diamond.  The fact that it is a mechanical watch is highlighted by a very nice looking blue second hand that appears to sweep around.  Workmanship is all very good.  A conservative Swiss automatic watch of pretty high quality that is fine as a business watch.  I have a quartz version of this with a steel colored face that is a bit thinner, and is also very nice, if you want the increased accuracy and lower price of quartz.  As with all mechanical watches, you've got to adjust the time weekly.  They are usually fast by about 10 seconds a day, IMO.  Absolute accuracy is not what this is about though.  Another watch you may consider in this class that is a little less pricey is a Tissot PRC-200.

Prior review:

I really like these and am happy with my purchase.

I don't typically wear a heel due to some old injuries that make them painful, but this boot has a sturdy and thicker heel which makes it a bit more stable for my old ankle.  The heel is dressy but not overly high, and I could see them paired with a casual outfit as well.  The "leather" is naturally not real, and thus not soft and supple, but the look passes well enough for a leather looking boot.

The sole has good grip at the ball of the foot, not too sure on the plastic heel cap though- it feels a bit slick, but with the majority of my weight on the ball area, they should be okay.

They are a bit big (I wear a 9.5 to 10 in most all shoes).  I ordered the ten, but a 9.5 might have been a better fit for me.  I'd say they run true to size to a bit large... my other size ten boots don't have nearly as much wiggle room.  I figure with thick winter socks, they'll be about right, and I'd rather have some wiggle room than for them to be too tight against my toes.

I guess I have HUGE calves because my male friends always comment enviously on my calf muscles.  That said, I am a former ballet dancer who kept her great legs even when the rest of me went to pot (haha).  My legs are pretty slim, thought not quite what I'd call skinny-- but my calves are 15.5 inches at the widest part of the muscle.  These boots fit over my freaky calves just fine- and have a plenty of room to spare. With a skinny jean I can still wear a thick knee sock and have about 2 fingers room around the top of the boot.  If you have super skinny legs... they might be too big for you if you want a snug fit around the upper part of the boot.  I have a feeling in the picture they'd been clipped or altered for a snug fit on the model's thin legs.  They are roomy, not form fitting.  ;)

I am happy with them, and think they will wear just fine.  They seem to be decent quality for the price.  Should they fall apart before their time or have any other issues, I'll update.  But for now, new out of the box, they are exactly what I wanted.  =)
summary: Great looking boot for the price!

A size 9 1/2 moves my toes away from that, and is more comfortable, but it is also too big- and my toes don't show up in the "peep" toe at all, and the shoe flops around on me. I think my problem resides in the fact that these are narrow in the toebox, with a strong angle to the point/peep toe, and my toes are not.
I am going to keep the nine and hope that I can stretch the very soft leather to accommodate my toes. (and I have boney feet, so it's not like there's a lot of flesh...)
Super comfy otherwise, though- with really supple leather. Nicely made. Great with retro skirts/dresses/capris. I'm going to wear them around the house with socks on and hope that will stretch the toe out.
****edited to add: They did stretch out, and now they are some of the most comfy shoes I own. I now have two pairs! Gentle Souls- please continue to make lots of colors- even in the kid leather! We need them!

I could hear her exclaim dramatically, "this is the ugliest thing I have ever seen! How will I ever sleep tonight?" She is 27 yrs old.

I like the color and it has a slight sheen to it not unlike shantung suiting material. It is lightweight enough that one could wear it to a summer event and not feel suffocated, but heavy enough to camouflage figure bulges or imperfections. The skirt had room for heavier hips/thighs. So far, I love this boot. I have yet to put it to a multi-day, all-weather test, but I will update my review when I do.  Many have stated that this boot runs small.  I am a solid size 10.  I purchased a 10.5 and at first thought it good.  After wearing them around the house for four hours, I realized that the arch support doesn't hit me in the right place.  I exchanged for a 10.  Perfect.  I'm not saying that the claims of "run small" are false.  Size ten seems to be the breaking point for design dimensions to change for most shoe manufacturers.  I did also replace the insoles with Superfeet (berry) insoles; those are great if you can always feel the stock insoles arch a little too much.  I put them in every lace-up shoe I have, but that's a different review.

I have worn the Sugarpine boot for about 25 hours total.  Dirt, cement sidewalk, grass, rocks.  They are a comfortable boot all around; not something I say much due to less-than-dainty ankles.  My ankles are less sore than with my former beefy hikers.  They are super light weight.  I do not feel the need to "get them off my feet" as soon as I sit down from a walk or hike.  I can still feel the ground under my feet, if that makes sense.

So far, only a few wet conditions, and they are living up to the waterproof claims.  Keep in mind that nothing is going to stay waterproof if you let water in the top.  My feet stayed dry through a few puddles.  Wasn't exactly a downpour, but it's better results of any shoe I have except the wellies, but who can take a hike in those.

I will live in these for a long weekend soon.  Update to follow.

I noticed some people like to complain about the noise the watch makes but literally I hear nothing unless it is right next to my ear. Everything seems to be of the highest quality and so far it works perfectly.

I love peacocks, and they make excellent adornments. The peacock is 4 1/2 cm  (1 1/2") wide and 2 1/2 cm (1") long. The genuine feather hangs another 12 cm (5")  below. The really cool feature on this pendant is the groove that holds the feather in on the back of the pendant, which will allow for easy replacement if the feather gets damaged. There is a dangle on the rear of the peacock that measures 18 mm (2/3"). The chain is rather sturdy and measures about 25" and is without a clasp. The only drawback I have found is that the jump ring attaching the pendant to the chain isn't very sturdy, and the light weight of the peacock means the pendant flips around backward often. The whole necklace is very light weight. I am thinking of reworking the attachment with split rings and some beads to add weight. I would buy this necklace again and definitely love wearing it with peacock feather earrings.

reviewText: This Cole Haan Men's Wool Cashmere Button Front Car Coat with Knit Bib, Black, Medium is a warm, comfortable coat that serves well for the late fall/early winter wear. I usually wear medium, and this coats fits quite well, even when I have a sweater on underneath. The wool and cashmere blend keeps the cold out. The large buttons are easy to put on and off. To stay even warmer, you zip up the leather-trimmed, inner nylon lining, which goes up to your chin. There are an additional 2 snap buttons to keep you snug. There are the usual 2 side pockets, each with 2 snap buttons at the top corner. For a more convenient place for your mobile phone and/or wallet, Cole Haan has thoughtfully put a pocket on the left side, at mid-chest height, closed with a single snap button. You can access this pocket even when buttoned up. All this would be enough, but coming from Cole Haan, this coat is also stylishly designed. Its elegance swill set you apart from the crowds.

I do leatherwork (whiskeymountainleather.com) and was participating at a craft show with a vendor that sold wearable diffusers. This was a new idea to me! I wasn't quite ready to spend $30 on one of hers (which are basically the same as any that's found on Amazon) so I was excited when I saw them here.
I was able to get mine at a discount in exchange for my review (I paid about $13). It was received quickly.

One reason I'm dropping a star is by how difficult it was to get the cage open the first time. Then, once it was open and I'd put in my oil, it was almost impossible to close! After using it a few times, it's loosened up... but right out of packaging, it was a pain in the butt!

I got a good variety of balls to go into the necklace. I use about 6-10 drops of oil (depending on how strong the scent is) and it lasts a few days.

One improvement would be for the hardware to be metal, as it's actually just painted plastic (but the cage itself is metal). Otherwise, nice necklace for $13 and I wouldn't hesitate buying one as a gift at full price!

I wear a lot of other dress shoes, and the Frye James is by far my favorite. I decided to pick up the James Bal Boot as a second pair and I love them right out of the box. I normally wear a 12D, but a 11D fits best . Snug at first, but after they break in, they're perfect and I can walk for miles in them.

Great build standard. High-quality materials throughout. Oxford-style (Bal) lacing gives a classy touch. Extremely comfortable due to smooth leather interior and leather sole. Round toe with just the right amount of elongation for a classic look that will likely never go out-of-style.
Very comfy. Has become one of my favorite pair.
summary: Has become one of my favorite pair.

I haven't worn these a lot to date but they look great and fit well right out of the box.  At first I thought they would be way too small but once I got my foot inside they were surprisingly roomy for my wide forefoot yet not too big for my narrow heel.  I had also just received a pair of J & M 1850 chukkas as a gift and the Frye boots are more comfortable.  It's also nice to get shoes that are the size they say they are.  The D medium is a great fit whereas I have had to start ordering, wide, 2e or even 4e in some boots/shoes.  I don't mind wearing any of those sizes but it would be nice to know what to expect when ordering.  The six lacing loops vs. three on most chukka-type shoes allow you to better adjust the fit to your foot.  Has a look of quality and simple elegance - really nice boot.

reviewText: These are my favorite shoes. I originally wanted them in black thinking the color would go with more but couldn't get my size so went with banana. The banana color is gorgeous - muted but saturated - as pictured, and goes well with virtually every color of clothing I wear! They fit well right out of the box. No breaking in. I've worn them almost every day since purchasing them a month ago and they've remained comfortable since the start. They are a little more narrow than your average medium-width shoe. My feet are medium, just slightly narrow, and I really like how the width of the shoes feels on me. I could see where they might feel a bit tight on a fuller, medium-width foot. As for the length, I wear 8.5 in athletic shoes and the 8.5 in these fit me well, with the right amount of space between shoes and toes. They are very well made and high quality; the nicest sneakers I've owned. I was a little bummed to see the price drop $25 a few days after I bought them but hope others snatch them up at this price and are as pleased as I am!

These shoes are cute and stylish with a Converse feel. The yellow colour is great too - It will go with most other colours and is unique. I found the sizing to be a bit small. I usually wear a 5.5 or 6, but because I read the previous reviews, I ordered a 6, and I am glad I did. I find that the toe area is a bit snug, but they are stretching out as I wear them. They don't have much arch support, though they are a very nice quality leather outside and in the inside bottom of the shoe. I haven't worn them enough to say how comfy they will be for the long haul.
summary: Cute Shoe, Runs a Bit Small

Also authentic Harris Tweed should have an "ORB Trademark" (google it).  Real harris tweed is expensive. This bag is expensive, so you wouldn't think twice about it having a the authentic trademark (sewn inside), but it didn't which made me feel suspicious.  Also it is made in India, which I don't have a problem with, but for the price they are charging it should be made locally (the British Belt Co.) and not offshore.  The reason I say this is because the British Belt does produce items in England. However after doing research it looks like they are trying to save money because they are manufacturing a lot of bags now in China.

All in all my gut feeling telling me it may be real Harris Tweed but if you are paying this type of money you want it certified that it is.  And if it is real then they should want to have the trademark sewn in because they paid good money for the real thing.

One star may be harsh but they need to either put the ORB trademark on or state this does not have it so you can make an informed decision.

reviewText:
When my watch family outgrew the 10-watch box I had been using for a few years, I needed something with more capacity. I liked the look (and price) of this one and ordered it. It holds 10 watches in the top level which has a glass top and simply opens on hinges and a bottom drawer that has compartments for the other 10. The capacity is twice what the old one was but the footprint is actually smaller. This is possible because, as I immediately discovered, the  individual compartments (and provided pillows) are simply smaller. Except for a couple of the most hefty of my watches, the watches fit, width-wise, into the spaces BUT some of the larger ones are too large to comfortably fir into the bottom drawer spaces - the larger ones simply stick up too much and prevent the drawer from closing easily.

So, I have had to arrange them with the heavier watches on the top level - not what I would prefer. However, I DO need the 20 spaces and do not really want to take up more of my dresser-top with a larger box. It's a trade-off. More watches in a smaller footprint box = smaller spaces.  It works for me because I have  many of both narrow and wider depth. If most of your watches are big and hefty, this is probably not the best box for you. If all of your watches are thin, it is perfect. If, like me, you have some of each, it will work for most of them.

The construction is attractive and  there is a small key-lock for the top level (the keys are under a pillow in the bottom drawer.)
All-in-all, I would say that this box is adequate but limited by the smaller size of its compartments. I have had to put my larger watches (which are not all the ones I would really want on top) onto that top compartment to make it work for me.

It contains all 20 watches and bracelets and looks nice on my dresser-top.
summary: Great for slim watches - not as good for bigger/thicker ones.

As a huge fan of the hard-to-find real eyelash, I happily found this met my standards. Now, the materials aren't as super crazy downy soft as brands that go for $50 per sweater, but this fits like it claims it will, is incredibly warm, is lightweight, feels comfy for the price, and it makes me feel good when I look in a mirror. I should probably also mention it doesn't shed (I ordered a blue one from elsewhere, and it shed like blue snow all over my living room!). It's very sturdy, though it looks and feels delicate.

I'm shocked that with shipping this was only $10!  Must say, I took a dare on that one, as cheap priced shirts on Amazon are becoming a suspicious red flag for me, but it so paid off. It's hard to find an eyelash sweater being sold that looks like it's from a trustworthy seller on Amazon, but I'm so glad I gave sweater shopping here another chance, cuz I love my new eyelash. Sadly these things are apparently becoming a dying breed and aren't even offered in the brand I bought just last year.

Washing Tips: Have to pass on this info for others who hate high-maintenance clothes like I do. I was terrified to do more than hand wash my good eyelash sweaters, but they can be machine washed just like it says on the tag with little to no fuzz loss. You can wash it on warm or cold, inside out. Never put an eyelash sweater in the dryer, to get max life. With dryer heat, it'll turn into a hairball on the side you washed outside! After the spin cycle, a quality eyelash sweater will always get rid of a ton of water it normally soaks up like a sponge. Then you just put it on the hanger in an open area and let dry. If it becomes crazy-haired-looking after drying, don't be afraid to take a broad bristled brush to it and gently coax the fur into shape. The material responds well.

reviewText: no additional comments

This is an initial assessment. I haven't properly tested these on the roads just yet. I like the appearance; its attractive. I thought the leather is kinda thin and that takes away from a premium feel. Normally I could tell a Timberland just by appearance and I have to say It doesn't scream Timberland with their typical excellent workmanship. I'm on the fence still as to whether these are genuine. I was hoping the leather portion would be sewn onto the out-sole but I think the sowing work around the shoes is actually faux sowing for aesthetic purposes. As to how strongly these are glued I really can't say but I would hope strong enough to last some years. The bottom of the shoes has a tough grippy rubber glued onto a slightly spongier rubber that has a really nice feel. My big concern here is that these two surfaces will not separate before any considerable life has passed. Overall these are attractive sandals that feels quite comfortable, but I have reservations about how well the leather is fastened onto the base. Oh one other thing I noticed was that the right foot was looser than the left so basically the left foot fits better. I've contemplated returning them for a different color and or size.
summary: Attractive sandals, medium quality?, reservations about the workmanship...

reviewText:
I purchased this watch on another popular site for much cheaper than this Amazon price, many sellers selling it for that price. MSRP is ~$700.

To start off, this is my first designer watch(Michael Kors). My other watches have all been Citizen Eco-Drives, so I will reference those often. I normally would not even consider buying a designer watch, let alone an MK one, but the price point was too good to pass up. I have not owned this watch for more than a few weeks. I wanted to write an objective review as I was in search of one before purchasing but was unable to find any useful information.

This is a real carbon fiber watch for under $200, my inner geek was too excited about this detail that I took the plunge and bought it without seeing it in person first. Other full carbon fiber watches are $1000s+ easily. The case internals are most likely steel, but it is all covered in real carbon fiber. The bracelet is carbon fiber as well, except the clasp is brushed metal. Overall, it is significantly lighter than any steel watch and bracelet, BUT is not lighter than any of my 3 titanium Citizens, although very close.

In pictures the cf may come off as glossy or matte finish, in person it is more on the glossy side. The weave looks great but is subtle from more than a few feet away. It is both classy, and fashionable,  without attracting too much attention. However, I do not believe it is high quality carbon fiber weave, that is just my opinion. I know there are various grades of carbon fiber weave ranging from cheap 3k(3000 fiber) to 6k to very high quality 12k. This is definitely not of the higher grade weave. But it still looks great for what it is and is definitely unique!
As far as durability, it is resin, it will indefinitely scratch easier than a metal. The resin coating on my watch has some very very tiny chips in some areas where the bracelet links rub together from being too close to each other and not having enough clearance.

The face of the watch has four dials. The eastern dial shows the 24hr military time. The remaining dials are for the chronograph only: the southern dial is seconds, the western dial minutes, and the northern dial shows milliseconds(but only moves for the first few minutes the chronograph starts.) The large red second's hand is constantly moving(personal preference), as opposed to other chronographs I have owned where that that is the chronograph's seconds hand. The bezel around the face is a unidirectional bezel, I don't use it for its intended purpose, as it is more of a fidget tool for me, but sometimes is hard to grip without perfectly dry and clean hands. The chronograph is confusing for me to use, and is not like my Citizens'. The top button is a start/stop, and the bottom is a reset ONLY when it is stopped. When resetting, the dials rewind backwards to their original positions, instead of instantly resetting.

With the pattern of the cf weave on the face of the watch as well as the busyness of the dials, it can sometimes take a little longer to read the time. It is still a very functional time piece, but in direct sun with glare, it can take some getting used to as the weave can catch the light. There is lume on the hands and hour marks, but it is not significantly strong, and I honestly have not used it much at night to make an opinion on it.

Comfort: it is a light watch. As mentioned, not as light as my titanium watches, but still very light compared to any other steel watches. It could be just a bit more comfortable. The links are removable and allow the bracelet to be adjusted. However, my Citizen watches have an extra point of adjust-ability in the clasp that allows the watch to be lengthened or shortened from 1-3mm in addition to the usual link removal. This allows my Citizen watches to truly feel just right around my wrist. With this MK watch it feels barely too tight, or just too big.

The watch movement is a quartz movement. Nothing in particular sticks out. I am not yet knowledgeable to know if it is a high quality one or not, but for the price and it being a designer brand, I can assume it is on the lower end.

Overall, it is a beautiful watch. As a designer brand watch, it is not as functional as other watches, but it appears to be much higher quality and attention to detail than the other popular MK watches I have seen, that I would not ever even consider buying. It is not worth its retail MSRP price, but for the price I got it for, I am very happy to add it to my growing collection of watches, and I do wear it in my rotation of daily watches.
summary: Good watch. Great price for a full carbon fiber watch.

reviewText:
Very cute! As you can see in their picture, that I didn't check before ordering, they cover the whole lobe, this is not a problem, just letting people know before they buy, I actually like it as they could be too tiny to be very sparkly.
 I really like them, they have a lot of sparkle in the little blue gems, but not too sparkly to be worn casually. They are a perfect winter earring.
They are simple and pretty.  Well-made and package in a very decent jewelry box.  The blue stones are set properly and evenly.

I normally would have passed on these earrings, but what made me like them was the blue cubic zirconia stones that are a nice contrast to the sterling silver snowflake. They are a nice, pretty shade of blue.  A snowflake itself is too holiday specific for me, I normally don't wear that kind of jewelry.

The earrings come in a nice black box, that the top is lined in a pretty shade of blue.  Makes for a nice presentation, if you plan to give these earrings as a gift.

The earrings themselves are on the petite side, which I like.  I really am not a fan of large earrings.  I think they look good on a certain kind of face, which is NOT mine. It's been years since I have worn post earrings, I prefer lever back.  The earrings are easy to get on, but the back part, the post, boy is it tiny, a challenge if you have long nails!  The earrings come with both the sterling silver posts, but they also come with the clear plastic part too, so you could use either, or both.  Makes them doubly secure on your ears!

The earring does not cover your entire ear lobe, but it is noticeable, but I do wish that the blue cubic zirconia stones had a little more bling to them, so that they would sparkle more.  They are pretty earrings, suitable for an adult or an older child or teenager.

They would be perfect for a holiday gift, or for someone who loves snowflakes.  Me, I prefer the beach!
summary: Pretty Earrings, For Yourself Or For A Gift

I am writing a review for this bag - disclaimer I purchased it new at Target on clearance for $42,  a steal.  But I think it's well worth the price.

First,  I am using this to replace my current business travel rig.  For years I have never had to check luggage,  even on a CRJ 700, because I carried my rolling slim laptop briefcase and I used by awesome Briggs and Riley compact suitbag to pack everything.  In that suitbag I could put in two full suits, two shirts,  3 t shirts, pair of jeans,  swimsuit, and socks and underwear for a week plus ties, toiletries etc.  Strap that to the top of my laptop handle and I was good.  It was flexible so I could stuff it into the tiny overheads even in the CRJ 700 and put my laptop under the seat; no bag checks, no waiting,  even when they tag your bag on the jet bridge and take it, I could skip the line.  I lived by the phrase,  " a fool and his luggage are easily parted..."  and it was awesome.

Then AA,  (American Airlines),  decides to perform their annual incredible shrinking bag trick and now you can have a carry on that measures 22" with handles and wheels - smallest of any airline domestically and let's face it, utterly unworkable if you have anything larger than a 20" carry on  (if you want the 4 wheel rotating setup your wheels are going to add an inch or two to the dimensions.  So on a recent flight back from Dallas,  they stopped my Briggs and Riley bag from boarding the brand new 737-900.  I pointed out to the gate attendant that this made no sense since I had just flown to Dallas on the smallest of airplanes without a problem,  but Gate Nazi says the dimensions are larger than 22 inches, doesn't matter if it can be squeezed in easily,  and that she will charge me $30 to send it home unless I accept her offer to check it complimentary.  Wow.

So now I am forced to buy a new bag to prevent from having to check anything.  Enter the American Tourister 17 inch spinner.  All I can say is that if you pack this little bad boy right,  it will be the answer to your needs.  being so small,  it fits the ridiculous 22" requirement with room to spare.  But it also is deep so you can use compression packing/cubes or a compression shelf to get in everything I named above,  and cinch it down and it works.  I even got a suit in by using a suit cover and carefully folding it and strapping it to the bottom before packing everything else.  Then I left the suit in overnight with everything packed and came back in the morning and unpacked it,  and the suit was good to go.  Now I wheel through the airport with this and my laptop suitcase strapped to it,  and I used the TravelOn bungee: https://www.amazon.com/Travelon-12181-50-Bag-Bungee/dp/B002EQ9O8C to strap them both.

This solution lets met check on everywhere,  and to get on the CRJ 7000 I can actually fit the American Tourister under the seat and stow my laptop bag in the overhead.  Perfect!  Pictures attached of the complete rig -  easy to get through the airport,  very secure,  right through TSA Pre.

The bag does have two small pockets on the exterior,  handy for phones or travel docs,  I am experimenting with a smaller ziploc toiletry bag for the bigger one to pull out for security and as shown in the photo,  I use the small one for phone chargers.  I keep small cable in there with three of the chargers,  and anytime I need to juice my phone,  I just hook it up and throw it in the pocket with the phone chargers - I can still use it with my bluetooth headset.

So in summary - damn near perfect travel rig.
summary: Great bag for business traveler,  with suit, read my review for the tips/tricks - meets all carry on requirements domestically

This wallet is true to its features as advertised. It is simple, gorgeous, roomy, yet not bulky. It fits my cellphone perfectly, closes without hindrance and still maintains a slim look. The purple colour is just as seen in the pictures. It came well-packaged in a pretty gift box and had a lovely mild scent of roses. The Yahoho charm that was included added a nice touch. I am 100% satisfied with it.

This review is for the Yahoho Women's Large Capacity Luxury Wax Genuine Leather Smartphone Wallet Purple.

This Yahoho wallet is made from ultra soft coated leather that feels so luscious and pliable in my hands. I love a good leather wallet, they last a long time, are durable, and classic. I got the fun purple color, and it is a deep eggplant with a hint of red to the purple. Very pretty.

The wallet is large and holds a TON of stuff. It holds my phone in the front or any pocket really, but if I have the case on my phone, it is a touch bulky. The other pockets hold my cash dollars, business cards, notes, receipts, mirror and whatever else I need to tote around.

There is a card slot area, it holds lots of cards, and the cards fit good and are secure in the slots. I can easily take them out and put them back in without frustration. There is a zippered slot for change; I love how the change doesnt have to rattle all around my wallet like in other designs. There are a few extra pockets for checks, or whatever else you want to carry long, its all very organized and thought out.

The front flap is secure and buttons with a lovely gold button with a fun design. Yahoho also includes a golden zipper charm for the zipper loop if you want to decorate your wallet more, its a nice touch. Overall, a good wallet that would be great for all ages! 5/5 stars!

reviewText:
My watch had problems right out of the box. There was a problem with one of the pins, right where the face meets the watch. It fell out twice  in less than 3 hours of my wearing the watch, causing the watch to smash to the floor and various pieces to scatter. The second time it happened right when I was putting something in the garbage and I had to root through garbage to find the pins.  I was so angry about this inconvenience and would have rushed to return it if I could have.  YUCK!  It was not a one time event, but some kind of problem and it took me a while to get to a watchmaker to get the watch professionally repaired.  So please keep in mind that my glowing review of this watch is of my *repaired* watch, not the defective watch I received.

This is a beautiful, eye-catching watch. The gift presentation was absolutely beautiful, and the watch itself is a knockout. It's fairly large for a women's watch, but not so large that I feel uncomfortable in it. It has some weight to it.  In my old watch I always wore it to sleep, but I found myself  wanting a little break from wearing this one at night. It comes with a fancy certificate of authenticity of the diamonds on the face of the watch---I hadn't even realized there were diamonds from the picture but they are obvious on the actual watch. The entire body of the fish is covered with tiny diamonds. I didn't count but maybe around 30 diamonds? The eye of the fish is a synthetic sapphire.

While there are no numbers on the clock face, the glass is somewhat raised from the face, and there is a band inside that "shadow box" area.  On the inside of that band  there are minute marks and every 5 minutes it counts off by 5, 10, 15, etc. Additionally, there are numbers printed on the gold-tone circle around the face, which turns, so if you want to set a low-tech timer, you could move the 30 (say) to be 30 min from where the minute hand is now, and then when the minute hand reaches the 30 on the bold band, your time is up.  Or you could just keep the 30 by where the 6 would be as usual.

At first I had a huge problem getting the dial to pull out to reset the date/time. I tried absolutely everything I could think of and nothing would budge it. I spent maybe 20 min trying to get it out and almost gave up on the watch in frustration. Then I discovered if you turn the dial a little bit, it releases, and then it can easily be pulled out.  I did look at the directions but there's only 1 page of directions and I didn't see anything about  that on them. So save yourself the worry and just turn the dial to unlock it before you pull it out to reset.

I've been wearing this watch for about 7 months straight now, and it still looks beautiful. Some of the gold-toned links are starting to wear off, showing the steel underneath, but fortunately only the ones on the bottom near my wrist, so I'll be able to wear this for a while yet.  I don't think I've ever received a compliment on it, but I do feel good wearing it and I still really like it.
summary: Once I fixed the defect it came with, I loved it

This is a beautiful watch and so far keeps time very well.  The simplicity of this design allows for wear with both casual and dress clothes. The light weight of it makes you forget you have it on. With bling face watches selling for upwards of $75 in some places, this under $30 watch is a great price point for its beauty and function. I like that the watch itself is made with the silver color bearings and crystal accents, which all flash beautiful in the sun. The rhombus cutting surface mirror and pearl ball running in the watch dial make this so unique and attractive. The back of this watch face is beautiful too...shame it can't be seen while wearing. Nice contrast of darker leather band to a rose gold colored watch face. The band is described as being leather and does feel like leather, although I could not find any marking on the band stating such.  Although this is is a big watch face, I think it makes a great fashion statement to use as a woman's watch with both dressy and casual wear. This does not come with a watch case, but arrives simply wrapped in bubble wrap and was packaged for shipment in a bubble envelope, and there was no damage to it even without additional protection. reviewText:
I found these no-show socks while looking for socks to wear with Keds type shoes.  I really hate when my socks show at all, so the fact that these are very low-cut, as well as being very cute with lace tops, really appealed to me.  When they arrived, I was a little worried they wouldn't fit. I should have expected that, as with many Asian-made clothes you see on Amazon, a "regular" fit sock would be too small for my size 10s.  However, they're very stretchy, and the grippy bands inside the sock ensure they don't slip down at all.  I wore them around the house for a while and they stayed put nicely.  The lace is soft and not at all itchy or scratchy.

I'd also like to mention how nicely these were packaged!  Each pair came in its own sealed mylar envelope, with a cardboard form to keep their shape.

Overall, I'd recommend these if you have size 9 feet or smaller, but they'll work for big feet too.  They seem to stay in place better than any no-show sock I've tried.

I have size 10 feet so sometimes it's hard to find socks that fit. When these arrived I was worried, but once I put them on they were perfect. There are grips in all the right places. Will definitely be purchasing in more colors!

These socks come from China so be warned that they do take quite a bit of time arriving. Although they did arrive before the estimated time frame provided, it was still about 2-3 weeks before I received them. Thats really the only negative thing I can say about these cute and comfortable socks. They arrive well packed and in 3 individual plastic baggies containing each pair. I was actually pleasantly surprised as to how cute they were at first appearance.  I wear a size 7 shoe and they fit my feet just fine with still a bit of stretch left in them. The sides and toe of the socks are made of a super soft and stretchy lace material and the bottom of the sock is a stretchy and soft cotton type material. There is also a bit of silicone glued to the inside of the head to try and keep these from slipping down off your feet and into your shoes. When I got these in I immediately ripped one pair out of the package, tried them on, and started walking around in them. I was a bit worried at first that the lace would dig into my feet or have a hard time staying on, but I was quite pleasantly surprised. They don't seem to slip or rub negatively at all for me and are really quite confortable to wear. When I wear them with my Sperrys then they don't show whatsoever; however, when I wear them with my flats they do peek out of the top of the shoe just a little bit. I always wear ballet style socks with my flats anyway so it really doesnt bother me to have them show a little bit, plus they are lace so I think the part that shows is classy and pretty.

reviewText:
I purchased the OneBarCo. tie bar w/ 10 covers + 2 premium covers (White Pearl + Carbon Fiber) on Kickstarter last year and cannot imagine ever going back to the office without it.

As a mid-20s man wearing suits every day, I really wanted to add an extra dimension to my daily get-up as men's business pro dress code is so rigid (how many suits, shirts, and belts/shoes can you realistically own?). I dabbled with tie bars in the past, but all were too bulky/heavy and boring (silver and gold are decent accents, but don't really make an outfit POP). I originally funded OneBarCo. for the sheer number of colors and patterns to choose from and was pleasantly surprised at how light and well-made the tie bar was once it arrived.

On day 1, I clipped it on and spent all morning swapping different covers to figure out which to wear. I had never seen Baby Blue, Rose Gold, or various patterned bars before; so it was really fun to see how each of them complimented my look. It also was as easy as advertised to swap covers - they are magnetic and takes less than 5 seconds to pop one off and another on - and at least 3-4 covers look great with each outfit, effectively quadrupling my wardrobe. I receive compliments from strangers a few times per week, and who can blame them when the bar is so dapper and unique with colors and patterns that nobody else on the market can offer?

The only feedback I had in 2015 was that the tie bar did not always stay completely in place. I emailed OneBarCo. and within a few weeks they made a minor tweak to the back design of the bar and sent me a new one on the house. It may have been a small move, but with all the giant greedy companies out there it really showed me that OneBarCo. is the real deal by listening to me as a daily user and using my feedback to essentially perfect an already incredible product.

OneBarCo. earned my business and trust with this tie bar and I am eager for any future products it creates to add even more dimensions to my professional wardrobe.

This product is the rare result of an instance where creativity meets function. The OneBar has been a staple accessory since I got it because of one word: versatility. While the tie bar keeps ties perfectly in place like it's supposed to, the magnetic/interchangeable options make matching outfits easy, fun and inexpensive! These natural wood covers are the perfect mix of a modern trend infusing timeless elements, but the rest of the line is worth exploring with leather, pearl and stainless steel covers can add a pop of color to any look. I highly recommend this product and am proud to be an owner.

reviewText: So glad this vendor offers these pants in XXL.  I've found several sold by RaanPahMuang that are.  Hopefully more patterned weaves or patchworks will become available as they see that us big boys like these comfy pants too!  Most of the ones you'll find on Amazon are "one size" meaning-if you're above average size then they likely will not fit and be as loose and comfy as some cut/sized for your above average-ness.  If you are on the fence, don't worry - they will wrap on around you and you'll have room for that extra slice of pizza later :-).  I'd guess if you were a waist sized 36-38 these may actually be a little too roomy and you'd be better off with the "one size" sizes but if you are blessed with above average measurements then these will make you happy!  As for length - I'm just over 6' tall (just, as in about a 1/2 inch) and weigh about 270 with a nice round belly and wear these tied at/around my hip bones - if I try tying them higher up they just fall off when I raise my arms...try keeping pants on a mushroom and you'll see what I mean...anyway, they are just about the right length tied off down that low.  If I pulled them up to my waist then they would be better suited for beach pants they would be so short (I wear these everywhere - "People of Wal-Mart" cameras better get locked and loaded).  I love the course woven 100% cotton which aids with a touch of extra friction to help keep them wrapped and tucked after you tie them on.  If I could wish something different or better about them it would be to add another pocket, maybe make them just a bit longer and offer more patterns or fabric options.  (and mine didn't come with the pattern orientation as shown but rather turned 90 degrees - which was still fine for me but some folks may not like it one way vs. the other.)

reviewText:
This ring is extremely unique. It is super sparkly band not just around the top layer but on the sides as well. It shines like crazy. I ordered a size 6 and I feel it runs a tad small. It runs more like a 5.5 or 5.75 on me. I wanted it for my middle finger and it is tough to get over my knuckle so I wear it loosely on my right ring finger.

The rings comes in a black velvet gift box and is just stunning to look at. It is not smooth around the edges. It is slightly ridged and I can feel that on my accompanying fingers. It doesn't hurt but is was little bit annoying at first until I got used to it. Otherwise, this ring is so unique and shines like crazy. It looks so much more expensive than it is and so far, for me, has held up to hand washings and getting wet without discoloring or getting dull. I really like the ring but I am taking one star off for the uneven (by design, not a defect) texture of the ring that sort of rubs against my other fingers and because my ring appears to run slightly smaller than true to size. Still, for the retail price, this ring can't be beat for quality and shine.

I received a discount in the price of this ring in exchange for my honest review. I'm not affiliated with the seller and was not compensated for my review. I suggest sizing up if you're in between sizes. This ring really is a stunner.
summary: Stunning and unique. It looks much more expensive than it is.

reviewText: This is a gorgeous ring! I love the detail in it and the fact that it has zircons not only on the top but on both sides as well.
